title.zh: 卷八十四 列傳第四十四 鄧琬 袁顗 孔覬
title.en: Volume 84 Biographies 44: Deng Wan, Yuan Yi, Kong Ji
title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第四十四 鄧琬 袁顗 孔覬 Volume 84 Biographies 44: Deng Wan, Yuan Yi, Kong Ji

sentences.zh: 鄧琬，字元琬，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, styled Yuanwan, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan, courtesy name Yuanwan, was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖混，曾祖玄，並為晉尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Hun and his great-grandfather Xuan both served as Directors of the Ministry of Personnel in the Jin Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Hun and his great-grandfather Xuan had both been Directors of the Ministry of Personnel under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖潛之，鎮南長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianzhi was Chief Clerk of the Army of the South.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianzhi had served as Chief Clerk to the Army of the South.

sentences.zh: 父胤之，世祖征虜長史，吏部郎，彭城王義康大將軍長史、豫章太守，光祿勳。

translations.literal: His father Yinzhi was Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Emperor Xiaowu, a Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Chief Clerk to the Grand General under Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Governor of Yuzhang, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinzhi had been Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Emperor Xiaowu, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Chief Clerk to the Grand General for Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Governor of Yuzhang, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 琬初為州西曹主簿，南譙王義宣征北行參軍，轉參軍事，又隨府轉車騎參軍，仍轉府主簿，江州治中從事史。

translations.literal: Wan at first was Chief Clerk of the Western Bureau of the province, a Mobile Staff Officer on the Northern Campaign under Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, then transferred to Staff Officer, again followed the headquarters to become Cavalry-and-Chariot Staff Officer, then again became Headquarters Chief Clerk, and Administrator-Assistant for State Affairs of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wan began as Chief Clerk of the provincial Western Bureau, then served as Mobile Staff Officer on the Northern Campaign staff of Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao. He was promoted to staff officer, followed the prince's headquarters as Cavalry-and-Chariot Staff Officer, then became headquarters chief clerk and Administrator-Assistant for State Affairs in Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 世祖起義，版琬為輔國將軍、南海太守，率軍伐蕭簡於廣州，攻圍踰年，乃克。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu raised the banner of revolt, he appointed Wan General Who Assists the State and Governor of Nanhai, leading troops to attack Xiao Jian at Guangzhou; the siege lasted more than a year before it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu rose in arms, he commissioned Wan as General Who Assists the State and Governor of Nanhai and sent him to campaign against Xiao Jian at Guangzhou. The siege lasted more than a year before the city fell.

sentences.zh: 以臧質反，為江州刺史宗愨所執，值赦原。

translations.literal: Because Zang Zhi rebelled, he was seized by Zong Que, Governor of Jiang Province, but was pardoned when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi rebelled, Wan was arrested by Zong Que, Governor of Jiang Province, but was released under a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 琬弟璩，與臧質同逆，質敗從誅；

translations.literal: Wan's younger brother Qu joined Zang Zhi in rebellion; when Zhi was defeated he was executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's younger brother Qu had joined Zang Zhi in the rebellion; when Zhi was defeated, Qu was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 琬弟環亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Wan's younger brother Huan was also executed by implication.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's younger brother Huan was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 琬在遠，又有功，免死遠徙，仍停廣州。

translations.literal: Wan was far away and had merit besides, so he was spared death and exiled to a distant place, remaining at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was serving far away and had rendered meritorious service, so he was spared execution and banished to a distant post, where he remained at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，得還，除給事中，尚書庫部郎，都水使者，丹陽丞，本州大中正。

translations.literal: After a long while he was allowed to return and was appointed Attendant Within the Gates, a Secretary in the Storehouse Section of the Secretariat, Commissioner for Waterways, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Chief Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was permitted to return and was appointed Attendant Within the Gates, Secretary in the Storehouse Section of the Secretariat, Commissioner for Waterways, Assistant Magistrate of Danyang, and Chief Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，車駕幸歷陽，追思在藩之舊，下詔曰：「故光祿勳、前征虜長史鄧胤之體局沈隱，累任著績。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming, when the imperial carriage visited Liyang, recalling old ties from his days in the fief, he issued an edict saying: 'The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and former Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Deng Yinzhi, was of a composed and reserved bearing and distinguished himself in successive offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daming, when the emperor visited Liyang and recalled his old associates from his days as a feudatory prince, he issued an edict: 'The late Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and former Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Deng Yinzhi, was a man of steady, reserved character who distinguished himself in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 朕昔當藩重，首先佐務，心力款盡，弗忘於懷。

translations.literal: When I formerly bore the weight of a fief, he was the first to assist in my affairs, exhausting his heart and strength in loyal service—I have never forgotten this.
translations.idiomatic: When I held my princely fief, he was the first to assist me in my duties, giving his utmost in loyal service, and I have never forgotten it.

sentences.zh: 往歲息璩凶悖，自取誅翦，沿恩及琬，特免釁戮。

translations.literal: In years past Qu's violent rebellion brought execution upon himself; extending grace to Wan, I specially spared him from punitive death.
translations.idiomatic: When Qu committed his violent treason and brought execution upon himself, I extended my grace to Wan and specially spared him from death.

sentences.zh: 今可擢為給事黃門侍郎，以旌胤之宿誠。」

translations.literal: Now he may be promoted to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, in recognition of Yinzhi's long-standing loyalty.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him now be promoted to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, in honor of Yinzhi's lifelong loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 明年，出為晉安王子勛鎮軍長史、尋陽內史，行江州事。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Chief Clerk to the Pacifying Army under Prince Zixun of Jin'an, Interior Minister of Xunyang, and acting administrator of Jiang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent out as Chief Clerk to the Pacifying Army under Prince Zixun of Jin'an, Interior Minister of Xunyang, with acting authority over Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝狂悖無道，以太祖、世祖並第數居三以登極位，子勛次第既同，深構嫌隙，因何邁之謀，乃遣使齎藥賜子勛死。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor was wild and lawless; because both the Founding Emperor and Emperor Xiaowu had been third in order of birth when they ascended the throne, and Zixun's place in the succession was the same, he deeply nursed suspicion, and following He Mai's plot sent an envoy bearing poison to order Zixun's death.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor was violent and lawless. Both the founding emperor and Emperor Xiaowu had been third in birth order when they took the throne, and since Zixun stood in the same position in the succession, the emperor deeply resented him. Following He Mai's counsel, he sent an envoy with poison to command Zixun's death.

sentences.zh: 使至，子勛典籤謝道遇、齋帥潘欣之、侍書褚靈嗣等馳以告琬，泣涕請計。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zixun's Master of Documents Xie Daoyu, Quartermaster Pan Xinzhi, Attendant Scribe Chu Lingsi, and others galloped to tell Wan, weeping and begging for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, Zixun's Master of Documents Xie Daoyu, Quartermaster Pan Xinzhi, Attendant Scribe Chu Lingsi, and others rushed to inform Wan, weeping and pleading for counsel.

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「身南土寒士，蒙先殊恩，以愛子見託，豈得惜門戶百口，其當以死報效。

translations.literal: Wan said: 'I am a humble scholar of the southern lands who received extraordinary favor from the late emperor and was entrusted with his beloved son—how could I spare the hundred mouths of my household? I must repay this with my life.
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, 'I am a humble scholar from the south who received extraordinary favor from the late emperor and was entrusted with his beloved son. How could I spare the lives of my entire household? I must repay this trust with my life.

sentences.zh: 幼主昏暴，社稷危殆，雖曰天子，事猶獨夫。

translations.literal: The young ruler is benighted and cruel; the altars of state are in peril—though he is called Son of Heaven, in truth he is a lone tyrant.
translations.idiomatic: The young ruler is benighted and cruel, and the altars of state are in peril. Though he is called Son of Heaven, he is in truth nothing but a tyrant.

sentences.zh: 今便指率文武，直造京邑，與群公卿士，廢昏立明。」

translations.literal: Now let us lead civil and military officials straight to the capital and, together with the assembled lords and ministers, depose the benighted and establish the enlightened.'
translations.idiomatic: Let us now lead the civil and military officials straight to the capital and, together with the assembled lords and ministers, depose the benighted ruler and install a worthy one.'

sentences.zh: 景和元年十一月十九日，稱子勛教，即日戒嚴。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jinghe, they proclaimed Zixun's command and that same day declared martial law.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jinghe, they issued orders in Zixun's name and declared martial law that same day.

sentences.zh: 子勛戎服出聽事，集僚佐，使潘欣之口宣旨曰：「少主昏狂悖戾，並是諸君所見聞。

translations.literal: Zixun came out to the audience hall in military dress, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi orally proclaim the decree: 'The young ruler's madness and perversity are things you gentlemen have all seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun appeared at the audience hall in military dress, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi proclaim orally: 'The young ruler's madness and perversity are matters you have all witnessed yourselves.

sentences.zh: 顧命重臣，悉皆誅戮。

translations.literal: The great ministers entrusted at the deathbed have all been put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers entrusted at the deathbed have all been slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 驅逼王公，幽辱太后。

translations.literal: Imperial princes have been driven and coerced; the empress dowager has been confined and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes have been driven and abused, and the empress dowager has been confined and humiliated.

sentences.zh: 不逞之徒，共成其釁。

translations.literal: Lawless men have together brought this calamity to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Lawless men have together brought this catastrophe upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 京師諸王，並見囚逼，委厄虎口，思奮莫因。

translations.literal: The princes in the capital have all been imprisoned and coerced, cast into the tiger's maw, longing to strive yet finding no means.
translations.idiomatic: The princes in the capital have all been imprisoned and coerced, trapped in the tiger's jaws, longing to resist but finding no means to do so.

sentences.zh: 身義兼家國，豈可坐視橫流！

translations.literal: My duty embraces both family and state—how can I sit and watch the flood sweep all away!
translations.idiomatic: My duty embraces both family and state—how can I sit idle while disaster sweeps the realm!

sentences.zh: 今便欲舉九江之眾，馳檄近遠，以謀王室。

translations.literal: Now I wish to raise the hosts of Jiujiang, dispatch proclamations near and far, and plot for the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: I now intend to raise the armies of Jiujiang, send proclamations far and wide, and act in defense of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 於諸君何如？」

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think of this?'
translations.idiomatic: What say you, gentlemen?'

sentences.zh: 四座未答，錄事參軍陶亮曰：「少主昏狂，醜毒已積。

translations.literal: Before the assembly could answer, Recording Secretary Staff Officer Tao Liang said: 'The young ruler is benighted and mad; his wickedness and cruelty have long accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Before anyone in the assembly could reply, Recording Secretary Staff Officer Tao Liang said, 'The young ruler is benighted and mad, and his wickedness and cruelty have long been manifest.

sentences.zh: 伊、霍行之於古，殿下當之於今。

translations.literal: Yi Yin and Huo Guang acted thus in antiquity; Your Highness should do so today.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin and Huo Guang did this in antiquity; Your Highness should do the same today.

sentences.zh: 鄙州士子，世習忠節，況屬千載之會，請效死前驅。」

translations.literal: The gentlemen of this humble province have for generations practiced loyalty and integrity; moreover, this is an occasion that comes once in a thousand years—I beg to offer my life as vanguard.'
translations.idiomatic: The gentlemen of this province have for generations practiced loyalty and integrity. Moreover, this is an occasion that comes once in a thousand years—I beg to lead the way and give my life in your service.'

sentences.zh: 眾並奉旨。

translations.literal: The assembly all accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 文武普進位一階。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were all promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials were promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 轉亮為諮議參軍事，領中兵，加寧朔將軍，揔統軍事。

translations.literal: Liang was transferred to Advisory Staff Officer, placed in command of the central guard troops, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North, and put in overall charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was made Advisory Staff Officer in command of the central guard troops, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North, and placed in overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 功曹張沈為諮議參軍，統作舟艦。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhang Shen became Advisory Staff Officer and supervised the construction of warships.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhang Shen was made Advisory Staff Officer and put in charge of building warships.

sentences.zh: 參軍事顧昭之、沈伯玉、荀道林等參管書記。

translations.literal: Staff Officers Gu Zhaozhi, Shen Boyu, Xun Daolin, and others assisted in managing documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officers Gu Zhaozhi, Shen Boyu, Xun Daolin, and others were assigned to manage documents and records.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守沈懷寶、岷山太守薛常寶之郡，始至尋陽，與新蔡太守韋希直並為諮議參軍，領中兵，及彭澤令陳紹宗並為將帥。

translations.literal: Shen Huaibao, Governor of Nanyang, and Xue Changbao, Governor of Minshan, had just reached their commands and had only just arrived at Xunyang; together with Wei Xizhi, Governor of Xincai, they were all made Advisory Staff Officers commanding central guard troops, and together with Chen Shaozong, Magistrate of Pengze, were appointed generals.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaibao, Governor of Nanyang, and Xue Changbao, Governor of Minshan, had only just reached their posts when they arrived at Xunyang. Together with Wei Xizhi, Governor of Xincai, they were made Advisory Staff Officers in command of central guard troops, and Chen Shaozong, Magistrate of Pengze, was also appointed a general.

sentences.zh: 初，廢帝使荊州錄送前軍長史、荊州行事張悅下至盆口，琬稱子勛命，釋其桎梏，迎以所乘之車，以為司馬，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier the Deposed Emperor had ordered Jing Province to escort under guard the former Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army and acting administrator of Jing Province, Zhang Yue, down to Pankou. Wan, invoking Zixun's command, released him from his fetters, received him in the carriage he himself rode, appointed him Marshal, and gave him the additional title General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Deposed Emperor had ordered that Zhang Yue, former Chief Clerk of the Vanguard Army and acting administrator of Jing Province, be escorted under guard from Jing Province down to Pankou. Wan, invoking Zixun's authority, released him from his bonds, received him in his own carriage, appointed him Marshal, and gave him the additional title General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 加琬冠軍將軍，二人共掌內外眾事。

translations.literal: Wan was given the additional title General Who Conquers Champions; the two men together managed all affairs, internal and external.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was given the additional title General Who Conquers Champions, and the two men together directed all civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 遣將軍俞伯奇率五百人出斷大雷，禁絕商旅，及公私使命。

translations.literal: He sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to go out and cut off Dalei, prohibiting merchants and travelers as well as public and private missions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to blockade Dalei, cutting off merchant traffic and all public and private communications.

sentences.zh: 遣使上諸郡民丁，收斂器械。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to the various commanderies to summon militia and collect weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to the commanderies to levy militia and collect arms.

sentences.zh: 十日之內，得甲士五千人，出頓大雷，於兩岸築壘。

translations.literal: Within ten days he obtained five thousand armored soldiers, marched out and encamped at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he mustered five thousand armored troops, marched out to encamp at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 巴東、建平二郡太守孫沖之之郡，始至孤石，琬以沖之為子勛諮議參軍，領中兵，加輔國將軍，與陶亮並統前軍。

translations.literal: Sun Chongzhi, Governor of the two commanderies of Badong and Jianping, had just reached his post and had only arrived at Gushi when Wan made Chongzhi Zixun's Advisory Staff Officer in command of central guard troops, gave him the additional title General Who Assists the State, and together with Tao Liang placed him in command of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chongzhi, Governor of Badong and Jianping, had only just reached his post when he arrived at Gushi. Wan appointed him Zixun's Advisory Staff Officer in command of central guard troops, gave him the additional title General Who Assists the State, and together with Tao Liang placed him in command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 使記室參軍荀道林造檄文，馳告遠近。

translations.literal: He had Recording Secretary Staff Officer Xun Daolin compose a proclamation and dispatch it to inform the near and far.
translations.idiomatic: He had Recording Secretary Staff Officer Xun Daolin draft a proclamation and send it out to rally support far and wide.

sentences.zh: 會太宗定亂，進子勛號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Ming settled the turmoil and advanced Zixun's title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with the privilege of an office equaling the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Emperor Ming had suppressed the disorder and promoted Zixun to General of Chariots and Cavalry with an office equaling the Three Excellencies in privilege.

sentences.zh: 令書至，諸佐吏並喜，造琬曰：「暴亂既除，殿下又開黃閣，實為公私大慶。」

translations.literal: When the imperial order arrived, all the staff officers were delighted and came to Wan saying: 'The violent disorder has been removed, and Your Highness has also been granted the Yellow Gate—this is truly a great rejoicing for public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial order arrived, all the staff officers rejoiced and came to Wan, saying, 'The violent disorder has been put down, and Your Highness has been granted the privilege of the Yellow Gate—this is truly cause for celebration on every account.

sentences.zh: 琬以子勛次第居三，又以尋陽起事，有符世祖，理必萬克。

translations.literal: Wan, considering that Zixun was third in order of birth and that the uprising had begun at Xunyang in conformity with Emperor Xiaowu's precedent, reasoned that victory was certain.
translations.idiomatic: Wan reasoned that since Zixun was third in birth order and the uprising had begun at Xunyang, matching Emperor Xiaowu's own precedent, victory was assured.

sentences.zh: 乃取令書投地曰：「殿下當開端門，黃閣是吾徒事耳！」

translations.literal: He then took the order and threw it to the ground, saying: 'Your Highness should open the Gate of Correct Beginning—the Yellow Gate is a matter for the likes of us!
translations.idiomatic: He then seized the order and flung it to the ground, saying, 'Your Highness should open the Gate of Correct Beginning—the Yellow Gate is a trifle for the likes of us!

sentences.zh: 眾並駭愕。

translations.literal: The assembly was all struck with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly was struck with alarm.

sentences.zh: 琬與陶亮等繕治器甲，徵兵四方。

translations.literal: Wan together with Tao Liang and others repaired weapons and armor and levied troops from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, Tao Liang, and the others set about repairing weapons and armor and levying troops from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史安陸王子綏、荊州刺史臨海王子頊、會稽太守尋陽王子房、雍州刺史袁顗、梁州刺史柳元怙、益州刺史蕭惠開、廣州刺史袁曇遠、徐州刺史薛安都、青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固、湘州行事何慧文、吳郡太守顧琛、吳興太守王曇生、晉陵太守袁標、義興太守劉延熙並同叛逆。

translations.literal: Zixun's younger brother Zishou, Governor of Ying Province; Zixun's younger brother Zixu, Governor of Jing Province; Zixun's younger brother Zifang, Governor of Kuaiji; Yuan Yi, Governor of Yong Province; Liu Yuanku, Governor of Liang Province; Xiao Huaikai, Governor of Yi Province; Yuan Tanyuan, Governor of Guang Province; Xue Andu, Governor of Xu Province; Shen Wenxiu, Governor of Qing Province; Cui Daogu, Governor of Ji Province; He Huiwen, acting administrator of Xiang Province; Gu Chen, Governor of Wu Commandery; Wang Tansheng, Governor of Wuxing; Yuan Biao, Governor of Jinling; and Liu Yanxi, Governor of Yixing—all likewise rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishou of Anlu, Governor of Ying Province; Prince Zixu of Linhai, Governor of Jing Province; Prince Zifang of Xunyang, Governor of Kuaiji; Yuan Yi, Governor of Yong Province; Liu Yuanku, Governor of Liang Province; Xiao Huaikai, Governor of Yi Province; Yuan Tanyuan, Governor of Guang Province; Xue Andu, Governor of Xu Province; Shen Wenxiu, Governor of Qing Province; Cui Daogu, Governor of Ji Province; He Huiwen, acting administrator of Xiang Province; Gu Chen, Governor of Wu Commandery; Wang Tansheng, Governor of Wuxing; Yuan Biao, Governor of Jinling; and Liu Yanxi, Governor of Yixing—all joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 先是，廢帝以邵陵王子元為冠軍將軍、湘州刺史，中兵參軍沈仲玉為道路行事。

translations.literal: Earlier the Deposed Emperor had appointed Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Xiang Province, with Central Guard Staff Officer Shen Zhongyu as acting administrator on the route.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Deposed Emperor had appointed Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling as General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Xiang Province, with Central Guard Staff Officer Shen Zhongyu as acting administrator en route.

sentences.zh: 至鵲頭，聞尋陽兵起，停住，白太宗進止之宜。

translations.literal: When he reached Quetou and heard that troops had risen at Xunyang, he halted and reported to Emperor Ming for instructions on whether to advance or withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Quetou and learned that an army had risen at Xunyang, he halted and reported to Emperor Ming for instructions on whether to advance or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 太宗以子勛起兵，本在幼主，雖疑其不即解甲，不欲先彰同異，敕令進道。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, considering that Zixun's uprising was originally directed against the young ruler, though he suspected that Zixun would not immediately lay down arms, did not wish to reveal division beforehand and ordered him to continue on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming reasoned that Zixun's uprising had originally been directed against the young ruler. Though he suspected that Zixun would not immediately disarm, he did not wish to reveal open division and ordered the prince to continue on his way.

sentences.zh: 信未報，琬聞子元停鵲頭不進，遣數百人劫迎之。

translations.literal: Before a reply arrived, Wan heard that Ziyuan had halted at Quetou and would not advance, and sent several hundred men to seize and bring him in.
translations.idiomatic: Before a reply could arrive, Wan learned that Ziyuan had halted at Quetou and would not advance, and sent several hundred men to seize him and bring him in.

sentences.zh: 乃建牙於桑尾，傳檄京師曰：

translations.literal: He then raised his command banner at Sangwei and circulated a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his command banner at Sangwei and circulated a proclamation to the capital, which read:

sentences.zh: 陽六數艱，雲雷相襲。

translations.literal: The yang sixth line marks repeated hardship; cloud and thunder follow in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The yang of the sixth line marks repeated hardship; cloud and thunder follow in succession.

sentences.zh: 高皇受曆，時乘雲轡，頓於促路。

translations.literal: The High Emperor received the mandate but, riding the chariot of the times, was halted on a narrow road.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor received the mandate but, borne on the chariot of the age, was cut short on the road.

sentences.zh: 文祖定祥，係昭睿化，翦於中年。

translations.literal: The Literary Ancestor fixed auspicious signs and bound himself to enlightened transformation, yet was cut down in midlife.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Ancestor secured the auspicious mandate and bound himself to enlightened rule, yet was cut down in the prime of life.

sentences.zh: 二凶縱禍，三綱理滅，宗王俯首，姑息逆朝，枕戈無聞，偷榮有秩。

translations.literal: Two villains unleashed calamity; the three bonds of order were extinguished. Imperial princes bowed their heads, indulging the rebellious court; none were heard to sleep upon their spears, yet they stole honors and kept their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Two villains unleashed calamity and the three bonds of moral order were destroyed. Imperial princes bowed their heads and indulged the rebellious court; none were heard to sleep upon their spears, yet they stole honors and kept their ranks.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝釋位泣血，糾義入討，投袂戎首，親戮鯨鯢，九服還輝，兩儀更造。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu abdicated his place and wept blood, mustered righteous forces to march in punishment, flung aside his sleeves at the head of the army, and personally slew the great monsters; the nine domains regained their radiance and heaven and earth were remade.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu set aside his throne and wept blood, raised righteous forces to march in punishment, took the field at the head of the army, and personally slew the great monsters. The nine domains regained their radiance and heaven and earth were remade.

sentences.zh: 而穹旻不惠，棄離萬國，皇運重替，嗣王荒淫。

translations.literal: Yet Heaven was unkind, abandoning the myriad states; the imperial fortune turned again, and the successor king was dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven was unkind and abandoned the myriad states. The imperial fortune turned again, and the successor king was dissolute and cruel.

sentences.zh: 孤以不才，任居藩長，大懼宗稷，殲覆待日。

translations.literal: I, lacking talent, hold the position of a feudatory prince and greatly fear that the altars of state await destruction from day to day.
translations.idiomatic: I, lacking talent, hold a feudatory command and greatly fear that the altars of state await destruction with each passing day.

sentences.zh: 故招徒楚郢，飛檄京甸，志遵前典，黜幽陟明，庶七廟復安，海昏有紹。

translations.literal: Therefore I have gathered followers in Chu and Ying, dispatched swift proclamations to the capital district, intending to follow the ancient precedents in deposing the benighted and elevating the enlightened, so that the seven temples may be restored to peace and the line of Haihun may continue.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have gathered followers in Chu and Ying and dispatched swift proclamations to the capital, intending to follow ancient precedent in deposing the benighted and elevating the worthy, so that the seven temples may be restored to peace and the royal line may continue.

sentences.zh: 豈圖宋未悔禍，弑亂奄臻，遂矯害明茂，篡竊天寶，反道效尤，蔑我皇德，干我昭穆，寡我兄弟，恣鴟鴞之心，蹈倫、穎之志，覆移鼎祚，誣罔天人。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that Song had not yet repented of its calamity, that regicide and disorder should suddenly arrive, that they should falsely harm the bright and flourishing, usurp the heavenly treasure, turn against the Way and imitate past crimes, despise our imperial virtue, violate our ancestral temples, diminish our brothers, indulge the heart of the owl, follow the ambitions of Lun and Ying, overturn the sacred vessel, and deceive heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that Song had not yet repented of its calamity, that regicide and disorder should suddenly arrive—that they should falsely harm the bright and flourishing, usurp the heavenly mandate, turn against the Way and imitate past crimes, despise our imperial virtue, violate our ancestral temples, diminish our brothers, indulge the heart of the owl, follow the ambitions of Lun and Ying, overturn the sacred vessel, and deceive heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 藐孤同氣，猶有十三，聖靈何辜，而當乏饗。

translations.literal: They hold in contempt my brethren of one breath—there are still thirteen of us—what crime have the sacred spirits committed that they should lack sacrificial offerings?
translations.idiomatic: They hold in contempt my brethren of one breath—there are still thirteen of us. What crime have the sacred spirits committed that they should lack sacrificial offerings.

sentences.zh: 昔隆周弛御，晉、鄭是依；

translations.literal: In former times, when prosperous Zhou relaxed its grip on rule, it relied upon the states of Jin and Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when prosperous Zhou relaxed its grip on rule, it relied upon the states of Jin and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 盛漢中陵，居、章抗節。

translations.literal: when flourishing Han was mid-collapse, Ju and Zhang upheld their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When flourishing Han was mid-collapse, Ju and Zhang upheld their integrity.

sentences.zh: 支苗輕屬，猶或忘驅，況孤忝惟臣子，情地兼切，號感一隅，心與事痛。

translations.literal: Distant branches and light kin have sometimes forgotten themselves in devotion—how much more so I, who am both subject and prince, with ties of feeling redoubled, crying out in one corner while my heart shares in the pain of events.
translations.idiomatic: Distant branches of the clan have sometimes forgotten themselves in devotion—how much more so I, who am both subject and prince, with ties redoubled by kinship, crying out in one corner while my heart shares in the pain of events.

sentences.zh: 是用飲血衽金，誓復宗祀。

translations.literal: Therefore I have drunk blood and grasped my weapon, swearing to restore the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have drunk blood and grasped my weapon, swearing to restore the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 今遣輔國將軍諮議領中直兵孫沖之、龍驤將軍陳紹宗，率螭虎之士，組甲二萬，沿流電發，逕取白下。

translations.literal: Now I dispatch Advisory Staff Officer and commander of central guard troops Sun Chongzhi, General Who Assists the State, and General of the Flying Dragon Chen Shaozong, leading warriors fierce as dragons and tigers, twenty thousand in linked armor, to advance like lightning along the river and strike directly at Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: I now dispatch Advisory Staff Officer Sun Chongzhi, General Who Assists the State, in command of central guard troops, and General of the Flying Dragon Chen Shaozong, leading warriors fierce as dragons and tigers—twenty thousand men in linked armor—to advance like lightning along the river and strike directly at Baixia.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍領中直兵薛常寶、建威將軍領中直兵沈懷寶，長戟萬刃，羽騎千群，徑出南州，直造朱雀。

translations.literal: General of the Flying Dragon Xue Changbao, commander of central guard troops, and General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaibao, commander of central guard troops, with ten thousand long halberds and a thousand companies of feathered cavalry, will march straight out from the southern capital and advance directly on Zhuque.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Flying Dragon Xue Changbao and General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaibao, both in command of central guard troops, with ten thousand long halberds and a thousand companies of feathered cavalry, will march straight from the southern capital and advance directly on Zhuque Gate.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍諮議領中直兵陶亮、龍驤將軍焦度，揔中黃之旅，梟雄三萬，風掩江介，雲臨石頭。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North, Advisory Staff Officer and commander of central guard troops Tao Liang, and General of the Flying Dragon Jiao Du, commanding the hosts of the central yellow guard, thirty thousand fierce champions, will sweep like wind across the river lands and descend like clouds upon Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North Tao Liang, Advisory Staff Officer in command of central guard troops, and General of the Flying Dragon Jiao Du, commanding thirty thousand fierce champions of the central guard, will sweep like wind across the river lands and descend like clouds upon Stone City.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍張冽，龍驤將軍何休明，提育、獲之徒，勁悍之卒，邪趨金陵，北指閶闔。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Zhang Lie and General of the Flying Dragon He Xiuming, leading warriors like Yu and Huo, with fierce and stalwart troops, will march obliquely toward Jinling and point north toward the Changmen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Zhang Lie and General of the Flying Dragon He Xiuming, leading warriors like Yu and Huo, with fierce and stalwart troops, will march on Jinling and point north toward the Changmen Gate.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍張係伯、龍驤將軍陳慶，勒輕銳五千，強弩一萬，飛鋒班瀆，齊會西明。

translations.literal: General of the Flying Dragon Zhang Xibo and General of the Flying Dragon Chen Qing, leading five thousand light elite troops and ten thousand strong crossbowmen, will fly their blades in array along the Du River and assemble together at Ximing.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of the Flying Dragon Zhang Xibo and Chen Qing, leading five thousand light elite troops and ten thousand strong crossbowmen, will deploy their blades along the Du River and assemble at Ximing Gate.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、尋陽內史鄧琬，撮湘、雍之兵，勇敢四萬，授律緫威，飆集京邑。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Minister of Xunyang Deng Wan, gathering the forces of Xiang and Yong, forty thousand brave men, will apply the military statutes and marshal their might, sweeping like a whirlwind to assemble at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Minister of Xunyang Deng Wan, gathering the armies of Xiang and Yong—forty thousand brave men—will apply the military statutes, marshal their might, and sweep like a whirlwind upon the capital.

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍、領府司馬張悅，蒼兕千艘，水軍五萬，大董群校，絡繹繼道。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the Barbarians and acting headquarters Marshal Zhang Yue, with a thousand green rhinoceros ships and fifty thousand naval troops, will greatly oversee the commanders in continuous succession along the route.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the Barbarians and acting headquarters Marshal Zhang Yue, with a thousand war vessels and fifty thousand naval troops, will oversee the commanders in continuous succession along the route.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、豫章內史劉衍、寧朔將軍、武昌太守劉弼、寧朔將軍、西陽太守謝稚、建威將軍、領中直兵、晉熙太守閻湛之，皆掃境勝兵，薦誠請效。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Minister of Yuzhang Liu Yan, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Wuchang Liu Bi, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiyang Xie Zhi, and General Who Establishes Might, commander of central guard troops and Governor of Jinxi, Yan Wanzhi—all have swept their territories for victorious troops and offered their loyalty, begging to serve.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions Liu Yan, Interior Minister of Yuzhang; General Who Pacifies the North Liu Bi, Governor of Wuchang; General Who Pacifies the North Xie Zhi, Governor of Xiyang; and General Who Establishes Might Yan Wanzhi, commander of central guard troops and Governor of Jinxi—all have swept their territories for victorious troops and offered their loyalty in service.

sentences.zh: 後將軍、郢州刺史安陸王子綏懷恩纏慕，鞠旅先辰。

translations.literal: Rear General and Governor of Ying Province Prince Zishou of Anlu, bound by gratitude and longing, has mustered his troops before the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Prince Zishou of Anlu, Governor of Ying Province, bound by gratitude and longing, has mustered his troops ahead of the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、湘州刺史邵陵王子元席颿陵波，整眾遄至。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Xiang Province Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling, with sails spread riding the waves, has assembled his forces and hastened to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling, Governor of Xiang Province, with sails spread riding the waves, has assembled his forces and hastened to arrive.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、荊州刺史臨海王子頊練甲陝西，獻徒萬數。

translations.literal: Vanguard General and Governor of Jing Province Prince Zixu of Linhai has drilled his armor west of the passes and presents troops in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard General Prince Zixu of Linhai, Governor of Jing Province, has drilled his troops west of the passes and presents an army tens of thousands strong.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍、冠軍長史、長沙內史何惠文，見拔先皇，誠深投袂。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State, Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Champions, and Interior Minister of Changsha He Huiwen, favored by the late emperor, has shown the deepest devotion in flinging aside his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State He Huiwen, Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Champions and Interior Minister of Changsha, favored by the late emperor, has shown the deepest devotion in taking the field.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、雍州刺史袁顗，不謀同契，雷發漢南。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers Champions and Governor of Yong Province Yuan Yi, without prior counsel yet of one accord, has thundered forth from south of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers Champions Yuan Yi, Governor of Yong Province, without prior counsel yet of one accord, has thundered forth from south of the Han.

sentences.zh: 建武將軍、順陽太守劉道憲，懷忠抱慨，不遠三千。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Martial Power and Governor of Shunyang Liu Daoxian, cherishing loyalty and embracing indignation, has come from no less than three thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Martial Power Liu Daoxian, Governor of Shunyang, cherishing loyalty and embracing righteous indignation, has come from three thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 梁、益、青、徐、兗、豫、吳、會，皆密介歸誠，誓為表裏。

translations.literal: Liang, Yi, Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Wu, and Kuaiji—all have secretly pledged their loyalty and sworn to be inner and outer supports.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, Yi, Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Wu, and Kuaiji—all have secretly pledged their loyalty and sworn to stand as inner and outer supports.

sentences.zh: 孤親緫烝徒，十有餘萬，白羽咽川，霜鋒照野，金聲振谷，鳴鼙聒天。

translations.literal: I personally command the massed hosts, more than a hundred thousand strong; white feather arrows choke the rivers, frosted blades illuminate the fields, golden clamor shakes the valleys, and drumming resounds to the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: I personally command a host of more than a hundred thousand; white-feathered arrows choke the rivers, frosted blades illuminate the fields, golden clamor shakes the valleys, and war drums resound to the heavens.

sentences.zh: 凡諸將帥，皆忠無匿情，智無遺計，果幹剛鷙，譎略多奇。

translations.literal: All the generals are loyal without hidden motives, wise without neglected stratagems, resolute and fierce, with cunning plans in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: All our generals are loyal without hidden motives, wise without neglected stratagems, resolute and fierce, with cunning plans in abundance.

sentences.zh: 水陸長驅，數道並進，發舟踰險，背水爭先。

translations.literal: By land and water they will drive forward, advancing on several routes at once, launching boats over perilous waters and contending to be first with the river at their backs.
translations.idiomatic: By land and water they will drive forward on several routes at once, launching boats over perilous waters and contending to be first with the river at their backs.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，孰能斯禦，推此義銳，滄海可垔。

translations.literal: With such a host in battle, who could withstand it? Push this righteous keenness forward, and even the blue sea could be dammed.
translations.idiomatic: With such a host in battle, who could withstand it? Push this righteous fury forward, and even the blue sea could be dammed.

sentences.zh: 諸君或荷寵前朝，感恩舊日；

translations.literal: You gentlemen have either received favor under the former dynasty and are grateful for old kindness;
translations.idiomatic: Some among you received favor under the former dynasty and remain grateful for old kindness;

sentences.zh: 或弈世貞淳，見危授命。

translations.literal: or for generations have practiced pure loyalty and would give your lives when danger appears.
translations.idiomatic: others have for generations practiced pure loyalty and would give your lives when danger appears.

sentences.zh: 而逼迫寇手，效節莫由。

translations.literal: Yet you are coerced by the enemy's hand and have no means to prove your loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are coerced by the enemy's hand and have no means to prove your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今大軍密邇，形援已接，見幾而作，豈俟終日！

translations.literal: Now the great army draws near in secret; visible support is already at hand. To act upon seeing the first sign—why wait until the day's end!
translations.idiomatic: Now the great army draws near, and support is already at hand. To act upon seeing the first sign—why wait until the day's end!

sentences.zh: 便宜轉禍趣福，因變立功。

translations.literal: It is fitting to turn calamity into blessing and, seizing the moment of change, achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Seize this moment to turn calamity into blessing and achieve merit through timely action.

sentences.zh: 夫旦、奭與三監並時，金、霍與上官共主，邪正粈雜，何世無之！

translations.literal: Dan and Shi existed at the same time as the Three Overseers; Jin and Huo shared rule with Shangguan—the crooked and the straight have always been mixed; what age has lacked this!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao lived at the same time as the Three Overseers; Huo Guang and Jin Midi shared rule with Shangguan Jie—the crooked and the straight have always been mixed. What age has lacked this!

sentences.zh: 但績亮則名播，姦騁則道消耳。

translations.literal: Yet when merit shines bright, fame spreads abroad; when wickedness runs rampant, the Way is extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when merit shines bright, fame spreads abroad; when wickedness runs rampant, the Way is extinguished.

sentences.zh: 紀季入齊，陳平歸漢，身尊譽遠，明誓是裒，成範全規，殷監匪遠。

translations.literal: Ji Ji entered Qi, Chen Ping returned to Han—their persons were honored and their fame reached far; their bright oaths were gathered up; their completed models preserve the full measure; the stern lessons of the past are not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Ji entered Qi and Chen Ping returned to Han—their persons were honored and their fame reached far. Their bright oaths endure as models preserving the full measure; the stern lessons of the past are not far off.

sentences.zh: 若玩咎惟休，告舍罔悟，則誅及五族，有殄無遺。

translations.literal: If you treat calamity as rest and, warned repeatedly, still fail to understand, then punishment will reach the five kindreds and none will be left alive.
translations.idiomatic: If you treat calamity as rest and, warned repeatedly, still fail to understand, then punishment will reach the five kindreds and none will be left alive.

sentences.zh: 軍科爵賞，信如皦日，巫山既燎，芝艾共煙，幸遵良塗，無守毀轍。

translations.literal: Military regulations and rewards of rank are trustworthy as the bright sun; once Mount Wu has been burned, wormwood and mugwort share the same smoke; may you fortunately follow the good road and not hold to a course of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Military law and the rewards of rank are as clear as the noonday sun. When Mount Wu is set ablaze, wormwood and mugwort burn together. Follow the right path—do not cling to a road of ruin.

sentences.zh: 檄到宣告，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: When the proclamation arrives, proclaim it so that all may hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: When this proclamation arrives, announce it so that everyone may hear and know.

sentences.zh: 購太宗萬戶侯，布絹二萬匹，金銀五百斤，其餘各有差。

translations.literal: A reward is set for Emperor Ming of a marquisate of ten thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred jin of gold and silver; the rest each receive differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: A bounty is offered for Emperor Ming: the rank of marquis with ten thousand households, twenty thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred jin of gold and silver. All others receive rewards in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣荊州典籤邵宰乘驛還江陵，經過襄陽，袁顗馳書報琬，勸勿解甲，并奉表勸子勛即位。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had sent Shao Zai, the chief clerk of Jing Province, to ride post-horses back to Jiangling; passing through Xiangyang, Yuan Yi sent a letter in haste to report to Wan, urging him not to lay down arms, and also submitted a memorial urging Zixun to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had sent Shao Zai, the chief clerk of Jing Province, to ride post-horses back to Jiangling. Passing through Xiangyang, Yuan Yi sent an urgent message to Deng Wan urging him not to lay down arms, and also submitted a memorial recommending that Liu Zixun ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 郢州承子勛初檄，及聞太宗定大事，即解甲下標。

translations.literal: Ying Province received Zixun's initial proclamation, and upon hearing that Emperor Ming had settled the great affair, immediately laid down arms and lowered its banners.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province had received Liu Zixun's initial proclamation, but upon hearing that Emperor Ming had secured the throne, it immediately laid down arms and lowered its banners.

sentences.zh: 繼聞尋陽不息，而顗又響應，郢府行事錄事參軍荀卞之大懼，慮為琬所咎責，即遣諮議領中兵參軍鄭景玄率軍馳下，并送軍糧。

translations.literal: Subsequently they heard that Xunyang had not ceased, and that Yi had also responded; Xun Bianzhi, the acting recorder and adjutant of the Ying Prefecture office, was greatly afraid, fearing he would be blamed by Wan, and immediately sent Zheng Jingxuan, a consultant leading the central troops adjutant, to lead troops south in haste and also deliver military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Later they heard that hostilities had not ceased at Xunyang and that Yuan Yi had also answered the call. Xun Bianzhi, the acting recorder and adjutant of the Ying Prefecture office, was greatly afraid that Deng Wan would hold him accountable. He immediately sent Zheng Jingxuan, a consultant and commander of the central troops, to lead an army south in haste and deliver military provisions as well.

sentences.zh: 琬乃稱說符瑞，造乘輿御服，云松滋縣生豹自來，柴桑縣送竹有「來奉天子」字，又云青龍見東淮，白鹿出西岡。

translations.literal: Wan then spoke of portents and omens, had imperial carriages and regalia made, saying that a leopard born in Songzi County had come of itself, that bamboo sent from Chaisang County bore the characters 'coming to serve the Son of Heaven,' and also that a green dragon had appeared in the Eastern Huai and a white deer had emerged from the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan then proclaimed auspicious omens and had imperial carriages and regalia made. He claimed that a leopard born in Songzi County had come of its own accord, that bamboo sent from Chaisang County bore the characters "coming to serve the Son of Heaven," and that a green dragon had appeared in the Eastern Huai region and a white deer had emerged from the western hills.

sentences.zh: 令顧昭之撰為《瑞命記》。

translations.literal: He ordered Gu Zhaozhi to compile this as the Record of Auspicious Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gu Zhaozhi to compile a work entitled Record of the Auspicious Mandate.

sentences.zh: 立宗廟，設壇埸，矯作崇憲太后璽，令群僚上偽號於子勛。

translations.literal: He established an ancestral temple, set up altars and ceremonial grounds, forged the seal of Empress Dowager Chongxian, and had the officials bestow a usurped title upon Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: He established an ancestral temple and set up altars and ceremonial grounds, forged the seal of Empress Dowager Chongxian, and had the officials bestow a usurped imperial title upon Liu Zixun.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月七日，即位於尋陽城，改景和二年為義嘉元年。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi, he ascended the throne in Xunyang city and changed the second year of Jinghe to the first year of Yijia.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month in the second year of Taishi, Liu Zixun ascended the throne in Xunyang city and changed the second year of Jinghe to the first year of Yijia.

sentences.zh: 以安陸王子綏為司徒、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史，尋陽王子房車騎將軍，臨海王子頊衛將軍，並開府儀同三司，邵陵王子元撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Prince Zishou of Anlu as Minister over the Masses, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Yang Province; Prince Zifang of Xunyang as General of Chariots and Cavalry; Prince Zixu of Linhai as General of the Guard; all with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies; and Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling as General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince Zishou of Anlu as Minister over the Masses, General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Yang Province; Prince Zifang of Xunyang as General of Chariots and Cavalry; Prince Zixu of Linhai as General of the Guard—all with offices equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies—and Prince Ziyuan of Shaoling as General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 其日雲雨晦合，行禮忘稱萬歲。

translations.literal: That day clouds and rain darkened together, and in performing the rites they forgot to proclaim 'ten thousand years.'
translations.idiomatic: That day clouds and rain merged into gloom, and during the ceremony they forgot to shout "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 取子勛所乘車，除腳以為輦，置偽殿之西。

translations.literal: They took the carriage Zixun had ridden, removed its axle-mounts to make a palanquin, and placed it west of the false hall.
translations.idiomatic: They took the carriage Liu Zixun had ridden, removed its axle-mounts to make a palanquin, and placed it west of the usurper's hall.

sentences.zh: 其夕，有鳩棲其中，鴞鳥集其幰；

translations.literal: That evening, pigeons roosted inside it, and owls gathered on its canopy.
translations.idiomatic: That evening pigeons roosted inside it, and owls gathered on its canopy.

sentences.zh: 又有禿鶖集城上。

translations.literal: There were also bald storks perched atop the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Bald storks also perched atop the city walls.

sentences.zh: 子綏拜司徒日，雷電晦冥，震其黃閣柱，鴟尾墮地；

translations.literal: On the day Zishou was appointed Minister over the Masses, thunder and lightning darkened the sky, striking the Yellow Pavilion pillar, and the owl-tail ornaments fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Prince Zishou was appointed Minister over the Masses, thunder and lightning darkened the sky, struck a pillar of the Yellow Pavilion, and sent the owl-tail roof ornaments crashing to the ground.

sentences.zh: 又有鴟棲其帳上。

translations.literal: There was also an owl roosting on his tent.
translations.idiomatic: An owl also roosted on his tent.

sentences.zh: 以鄧琬為左將軍、尚書右僕射，張悅領軍將軍、吏部尚書，征虜將軍如故；

translations.literal: Deng Wan was made General of the Left and Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing; Zhang Yue was made General Who Leads the Army and Minister of Personnel, retaining his title as General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was appointed General of the Left and Vice Minister of the Right of the Masters of Writing. Zhang Yue was appointed General Who Leads the Army and Minister of Personnel, while retaining his title as General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 進袁顗號安北將軍，加尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi's title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, with the additional post of Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi's title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North, with the additional appointment as Vice Minister of the Left of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 臨川內史張淹為侍中。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan, the Interior Minister of Linchuan, was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan, Interior Minister of Linchuan, was appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 府主簿顧昭之、武昌太守劉弼並為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Gu Zhaozhi, the chief clerk of the prefecture, and Liu Bi, Governor of Wuchang, were both made Attendants of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhaozhi, chief clerk of the prefecture, and Liu Bi, Governor of Wuchang, were both appointed Attendants of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守王子仲委郡奔尋陽，亦為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Wang Zizhong, Governor of Lujiang, abandoned his commandery and fled to Xunyang, and was also made Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhong, Governor of Lujiang, abandoned his commandery and fled to Xunyang, where he too was appointed Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽內史丘景先、廬陵內史殷損、西陽太守謝稚、後軍府記室參軍孫詵、長沙內史孔靈產、參軍事沈伯玉、荀道林並為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Qiu Jingxian, Interior Minister of Poyang; Yin Sun, Interior Minister of Luling; Xie Zhi, Governor of Xiyang; Sun Shen, secretary of the Rear Army office; Kong Lingchan, Interior Minister of Changsha; Shen Boyu and Xun Daolin, staff officers—all were made Attendants of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jingxian, Interior Minister of Poyang; Yin Sun, Interior Minister of Luling; Xie Zhi, Governor of Xiyang; Sun Shen, secretary of the Rear Army office; Kong Lingchan, Interior Minister of Changsha; and the staff officers Shen Boyu and Xun Daolin were all appointed Attendants of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 荀卞之為尚書左丞，府主簿江乂為右丞，府主簿蕭寶欣為通直郎。

translations.literal: Xun Bianzhi was made Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing; Jiang Yi, chief clerk of the prefecture, was made Right Assistant; and Xiao Baoxin, chief clerk of the prefecture, was made Direct Transmission Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bianzhi was appointed Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing. Jiang Yi, chief clerk of the prefecture, was appointed Right Assistant, and Xiao Baoxin, also chief clerk of the prefecture, was appointed Direct Transmission Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 琬大息粹、悅息洵並正員郎，粹領衛尉，洵弟洌司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Wan's eldest son Cui and Yue's eldest son Xun were both made regular gentlemen; Cui also headed the Court of the Imperial Clan, and Xun's younger brother Lie was made chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan's eldest son Cui and Zhang Yue's eldest son Xun were both appointed regular gentlemen. Cui also headed the Court of the Imperial Clan, and Xun's younger brother Lie was appointed chief clerk to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 建武將軍、領軍主、晉熙太守閻湛之加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: Yan Wanzhi, General Who Establishes Martial Power, commander of the army staff, and Governor of Jinxi, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Wanzhi, General Who Establishes Martial Power, commander of the army staff, and Governor of Jinxi, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 廬陵內史王僧胤為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Wang Sengyin, Interior Minister of Luling, was made Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengyin, Interior Minister of Luling, was appointed Secretary.

sentences.zh: 桂陽太守劉卷為尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Liu Juan, Governor of Guiyang, was made Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Juan, Governor of Guiyang, was appointed Palace Attendant of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 褚靈嗣、潘欣之、沈光祖，中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Chu Lingsi, Pan Xinzhi, and Shen Guangzu were made Attendants-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Lingsi, Pan Xinzhi, and Shen Guangzu were appointed Attendants-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 餘諸州郡，並加爵號。

translations.literal: The remaining provinces and commanderies all received additional titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the remaining provinces and commanderies all received additional titles and ranks.

sentences.zh: 琬性鄙闇，貪吝過甚，財貨酒食，皆身自量校。

translations.literal: Wan's nature was crude and dull, and his greed and stinginess were excessive; for wealth, goods, wine, and food he personally measured and checked everything.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was crude and obtuse by nature, and excessively greedy and miserly. He personally measured and checked every item of wealth, goods, wine, and food.

sentences.zh: 至是父子並賣官鬻爵，使婢僕出市道販賣，酣歌博奕，日夜不休。

translations.literal: At this time father and sons alike sold offices and titles, had maidservants and servants go out into the streets to peddle them, and sang, drank, gambled, and played games day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: By then father and sons alike were selling offices and titles, sending maidservants and servants into the streets to peddle them while they sang, drank, gambled, and played games day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 大自矜遇，賓客到門者，歷旬不得前。

translations.literal: He greatly prided himself on his importance; guests who came to his door could not get in for ten days at a stretch.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself in the highest esteem. Guests who came to his door might wait ten days without being admitted.

sentences.zh: 內事悉委褚靈嗣等三人，群小橫恣，競為威福，士庶忿怨，內外離心矣。

translations.literal: Internal affairs were entirely entrusted to Chu Lingsi and the other two men; petty men ran rampant, each vying to wield power and favor, and officials and commoners resented them—the court and the people were estranged at heart.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted all internal affairs entirely to Chu Lingsi and the other two men. Petty officials ran rampant, each vying for power and privilege, until officials and commoners alike seethed with resentment. Court and country were estranged at heart.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣散騎常侍、領軍將軍王玄謨領水軍南討，吳興太守張永為其後繼；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Wang Xuanmo, Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and General Who Leads the Army, to lead the navy on a southern punitive campaign, with Zhang Yong, Governor of Wuxing, as his rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Wang Xuanmo, Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and General Who Leads the Army, to lead the navy on a southern punitive campaign, with Zhang Yong, Governor of Wuxing, following in support.

sentences.zh: 又遣寧朔將軍尋陽內史沈攸之、寧朔將軍江方興、龍驤將軍劉靈遺率眾屯虎檻。

translations.literal: He also sent Shen Youzhi, General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Xunyang; Jiang Fangxing, General Who Pacifies the North; and Liu Lingyi, General of the Flying Dragon, to lead troops and encamp at Hujian.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shen Youzhi, General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Xunyang; Jiang Fangxing, General Who Pacifies the North; and Liu Lingyi, General of the Flying Dragon, to lead troops and encamp at Hujian.

sentences.zh: 時東賊甚急，張永、江方興回軍東討。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern rebels were pressing hard, and Zhang Yong and Jiang Fangxing turned their armies east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eastern rebels were pressing hard, so Zhang Yong and Jiang Fangxing turned their armies east to attack.

sentences.zh: 尚書下符曰：

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing issued an order saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing issued an order stating:

sentences.zh: 夫晦明遞運，崇替相沿，帝宋之基，懋業維永，聖祖重光，氤氳上業。

translations.literal: Darkness and light alternate in succession, elevation and replacement follow one upon another; the foundation of the Song dynasty is established, its glorious enterprise enduring; the sacred ancestor's light shines again, and the supreme enterprise gathers like mist.
translations.idiomatic: Darkness and light succeed one another; dynasties rise and fall in turn. The foundation of the Song dynasty stands firm, its glorious enterprise meant to endure forever. The sacred ancestor's light shines anew, and the supreme enterprise gathers like rising mist.

sentences.zh: 狂昏承祀，國維以紊，毒流九縣，釁穢三靈，搢紳戮辱，黔庶塗炭，人神同憤，朝野泣血。

translations.literal: A mad and benighted ruler inherited the sacrifice, and the state's pillars were thrown into disorder; poison flowed through the nine provinces, offense defiled the three spirits; gentry were slaughtered and shamed, and the common people were scorched in misery; men and gods alike raged, and court and countryside wept blood.
translations.idiomatic: A mad and benighted ruler inherited the throne, and the pillars of the state were thrown into chaos. Poison spread through the nine provinces and offense defiled Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral spirits. Gentry were slaughtered and humiliated, and the common people were scorched in misery. Men and gods alike burned with rage, and court and countryside wept blood.

sentences.zh: 聖上明睿在躬，膺符握曜，眷懷家國，夙夜劬勞，懼社稷湮蕪，彝倫左衽。

translations.literal: The sage emperor is bright and wise in person, received the mandate and grasped the celestial glory, cherishing the family and state, toiling day and night, fearing that the altars of soil and grain would be ruined and the moral order turned aside.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor is bright and wise in his own person. He received the mandate and grasped the celestial glory, cherishing family and state and toiling day and night, fearing that the altars of soil and grain would fall to ruin and the moral order be overturned.

sentences.zh: 天威雷發，氛沴冰消，殄凶譙門，不俟鳴條之旅；

translations.literal: Heaven's majesty burst forth like thunder, and malignant vapors melted like ice; the wicked were destroyed at Qiao Gate without waiting for the army that marched at the sound of the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's majesty burst forth like thunder, and malignant vapors melted like ice. The wicked were destroyed at Qiao Gate without waiting for the army that marches at the crack of the whip.

sentences.zh: 殲虐牧野，無勞孟津之鉞。

translations.literal: The cruel were annihilated at Muye, with no need for the battle-axes of Mengjin.
translations.idiomatic: The cruel were annihilated at Muye, with no need for the battle-axes of Mengjin.

sentences.zh: 華、夷即晏，晷緯還光，鏗鏘聞於管弦，趨翔被於冠冕，同軌仰化，異域懷風。

translations.literal: China and the barbarians were at once at peace, the sun's shadow and the stars' light returned; music resounded in pipes and strings, and splendor spread over caps and robes; those on the same road looked up to be transformed, and distant lands cherished the wind of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: China and the barbarians were at once at peace, and the light of sun and stars returned. Music resounded from pipes and strings, and splendor spread over caps and robes. Those within the realm looked up to be transformed, and distant lands cherished the wind of virtue.

sentences.zh: 劉子勛昏世稱兵，義同翦惡，明朝不戟，罔識邪正。

translations.literal: Liu Zixun, in a benighted age, raised troops; in name it was the same as cutting off evil, but in the bright court he did not halt his weapons and knew neither the crooked nor the straight.
translations.idiomatic: In a benighted age Liu Zixun raised troops. In name his cause was the same as cutting off evil, yet in the bright court he would not lay down his arms and could not tell right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 窺窬畿甸，逼遏兩江，陵上無君，暴於遐邇。

translations.literal: He peeped and encroached upon the capital region, pressed and blocked the two rivers, showed no lord above him, and displayed his violence near and far.
translations.idiomatic: He encroached upon the capital region and blocked the two Yangzi rivers. He acknowledged no sovereign above him and displayed his violence for all to see, near and far.

sentences.zh: 王赫斯怒，興言討違，命彼上將，治兵薄伐。

translations.literal: The king was greatly angered, raised the cry to punish rebellion, and ordered those great generals to ready the troops for a punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered. He raised the cry to punish rebellion and ordered his great generals to ready their troops for a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 今遣寧朔將軍、尋陽內史沈攸之，輕銳七千，飛舟先邁。

translations.literal: Now we send Shen Youzhi, General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Xunyang, with seven thousand light elite troops, swift boats advancing first.
translations.idiomatic: We now send Shen Youzhi, General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Xunyang, with seven thousand light elite troops in swift boats to advance first.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉靈遺，羽林虎旅，連鋒繼造。

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi, General of the Flying Dragon, with the imperial guard and tiger brigades, follows in continuous advance with linked spearpoints.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi, General of the Flying Dragon, follows with the imperial guard and tiger brigades, advancing in continuous waves with linked spearpoints.

sentences.zh: 假節、督南討前鋒諸軍事、冠軍將軍、兗州刺史殷孝祖，驅濟、河勁卒，電擊雷動。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu, holding temporary credentials, supervising the vanguard of the southern punitive army, General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Yan Province, drives the strong soldiers of Ji and the Yellow River in a strike like lightning and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu, holding temporary credentials as supervisor of the vanguard of the southern punitive army, General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Yan Province, drives the strong soldiers of Ji and the Yellow River in a strike like lightning and thunder.

sentences.zh: 使持節、車騎將軍、江州刺史曲江縣開國侯王玄謨，烝徒五萬，董統前師。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo, Bearer of Credentials, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Marquis of Qujiang County with a state of ten thousand households, with fifty thousand troops, supervises and commands the forward army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, Bearer of Credentials, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Marquis of Qujiang County with a state of ten thousand households, leads fifty thousand troops as overall commander of the forward army.

sentences.zh: 使持節、侍中、司徒、揚州刺史建安王休仁，擁神州之眾，揔督群帥。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuren, Bearer of Credentials, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Yang Province, the Prince of Jian'an, with the masses of the central provinces, supervises all the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren, Bearer of Credentials, Palace Attendant, Minister over the Masses, and Inspector of Yang Province, the Prince of Jian'an, commands the armies of the central provinces as supreme commander of all the generals.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍劉勔、寧朔將軍劉懷珍，步騎五千，直指大雷。

translations.literal: Liu Qin, General of the Flying Dragon, and Liu Huaizhen, General Who Pacifies the North, with five thousand infantry and cavalry, advance directly on Dalei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qin, General of the Flying Dragon, and Liu Huaizhen, General Who Pacifies the North, with five thousand infantry and cavalry, advance directly on Dalei.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍柳倫、司州刺史龐孟虯，淮、潁突騎，邪趣西陽。

translations.literal: Liu Lun, General Who Pacifies the North, and Pang Mengjiao, Inspector of Si Province, with the shock cavalry of Huai and Ying, strike obliquely toward Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lun, General Who Pacifies the North, and Pang Mengjiao, Inspector of Si Province, with the shock cavalry of Huai and Ying, strike obliquely toward Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 使持節、驃騎大將軍、豫州刺史山陽王休祐，揔勒步師，連旗百萬，河舟代馬，遄鶩江濆，越棘吳鉤，交曜畿服，笳鼓動坤維，金甲震雲漢，掎角相望，水陸俱發。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuyou, Bearer of Credentials, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Yu Province, the Prince of Shanyang, supervises the infantry divisions; a hundred myriad banners in succession, river boats and northern horses, rush like wild ducks to the river banks; with Wu blades and Yue hooks crossing gleams over the capital region, horn drums shake the earth's corners, golden armor thunders in the clouds, pincers face one another, and land and water both advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuyou, Bearer of Credentials, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Yu Province, the Prince of Shanyang, commands the infantry divisions. A million banners follow in succession; river boats and northern horses rush like wild ducks to the river banks. With Wu blades and Yue hooks flashing across the capital region, horn drums shake the earth's corners and golden armor thunders in the clouds. Pincer forces face one another as land and water both advance.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍武念，率雍、司之銳，已據樊、沔。

translations.literal: Wu Nian, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, leading the elite of Yong and Si, has already occupied Fan and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nian, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, leading the elite troops of Yong and Si, has already occupied Fan and Mian.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史申令孫，提彭、宋剽勇，陵塗焱奮。

translations.literal: Shen Lingsun, Inspector of Xu Province, leading the swift warriors of Peng and Song, advances over the roads blazing with fury.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Lingsun, Inspector of Xu Province, leading the swift warriors of Peng and Song, advances over the roads blazing with fury.

sentences.zh: 皇上當親馭六師，降臨江服，旌旆掩雲，舳艫咽海。

translations.literal: The emperor himself will drive the six armies, descend upon the Jiang region, banners covering the clouds, and warships choking the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself will lead the six armies, descend upon the Jiang region, his banners covering the clouds and his warships choking the sea.

sentences.zh: 昔吳、楚連衡，燕、淮勁悍，塵擾區內，聲沸秦中，霧散埃滅，豈非先鑒。

translations.literal: In the past Wu and Chu joined in alliance, Yan and Huai were fierce and strong; dust stirred within the realm, and their fame boiled in Qin; yet mist scattered and dust vanished—is this not a lesson from the past?
translations.idiomatic: In the past Wu and Chu joined in alliance, and Yan and Huai were fierce and strong. Dust stirred within the realm and their fame resounded as far as Qin—yet mist scattered and dust vanished. Is this not a lesson from the past?

sentences.zh: 而嬰彼孤城，以待該天之網，迫此烏合，以抗絡宇之師。

translations.literal: Yet to rely on that isolated city and wait for the net that covers heaven, to press this mob gathered like crows and resist the army that binds the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they rely on that isolated city and wait for the net that covers heaven, pressing this mob gathered like crows to resist the army that binds the realm.

sentences.zh: 雲羅四掩，霜鋒交集，猶勁飆之拂細草，烈火之掃寒原，燋卷之形，昭然已著。

translations.literal: Cloud-nets close in on four sides, frost-blades cross and gather; it is still like a fierce gale brushing fine grass, or a raging fire sweeping a cold plain—the shape of being burned and rolled up is already clearly shown.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud-nets close in on four sides and frost-sharp blades cross and gather. It is like a fierce gale brushing fine grass, or a raging fire sweeping a cold plain—the shape of being burned and swept away is already plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 朝廷惻愍我僚吏，哀矜我士民，並亦何辜，拘誤迷黨。

translations.literal: The court pities our officials and clerks and pities our gentry and people; what crime have they all committed, that they were detained and misled into the wrong faction?
translations.idiomatic: The court pities our officials and clerks and pities our gentry and people. What crime have they committed, that they were detained and misled into the wrong faction?

sentences.zh: 故加宣示，令得自新。

translations.literal: Therefore we add this proclamation, so that they may obtain self-renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we issue this further proclamation so that they may reform themselves.

sentences.zh: 如其淪惑不改，抵冒王威，同焚既至，雖悔奚補。

translations.literal: If they sink into delusion and do not change, or offend against the royal majesty, when the common burning arrives, though they repent, what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: If they remain sunk in delusion and do not change, or offend against the imperial majesty, when the common fire arrives, repentance will be of no avail.

sentences.zh: 奉詔以四王幼弱，不幸陷難，兵交之日，不得妄加侵犯，若有逼損，誅翦無貸。

translations.literal: In accordance with the edict, because the four princes are young and weak and have unfortunately fallen into hardship, on the day arms are crossed they must not be rashly violated or harmed; if anyone forces or injures them, execution and extermination will be without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: In accordance with the edict, because the four princes are young and weak and have unfortunately fallen into hardship, on the day battle is joined they must not be rashly harmed. If anyone forces or injures them, execution will be without pardon.

sentences.zh: 左右主帥，嚴相衛奉，詿誤之罪，一無所問。

translations.literal: The commanders on left and right must strictly guard and protect them; the crime of being misled will not be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders on left and right must strictly guard and protect them. The crime of having been misled will not be questioned at all.

sentences.zh: 琬遣孫沖之率陳紹宗、胡靈秀、薛常寶、張繼伯、焦度等前鋒一萬，來據赭圻。

translations.literal: Wan sent Sun Chongzhi to lead Chen Shaozong, Hu Lingxiu, Xue Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Jiao Du, and others with ten thousand vanguard troops to come and hold Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent Sun Chongzhi to lead Chen Shaozong, Hu Lingxiu, Xue Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Jiao Du, and others with ten thousand vanguard troops to seize and hold Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 沖之於道與子勛書曰：「舟楫已辦，器械亦整，三軍踴躍，人爭效命，便欲沿流掛颿，直取白下。

translations.literal: Chongzhi wrote to Zixun on the road saying: 'The boats are already prepared, the weapons are also in order, the three armies leap with joy, and men compete to give their lives; we wish at once to follow the current, raise sails, and take Baixia directly.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Chongzhi wrote to Liu Zixun: "The boats are ready and the weapons are in order. The three armies leap with joy and every man competes to give his life. We intend at once to sail downriver, raise our sails, and strike directly at Baixia.

sentences.zh: 願速遣陶亮眾軍，兼行相接，分據新亭、南州，則一麾定矣。」

translations.literal: We hope you will quickly send Tao Liang's army as well, advancing together to join us, and separately hold Xinting and Nanzhou; then one wave of the banner will settle it.'
translations.idiomatic: Please send Tao Liang's army quickly as well, advancing together to join us and separately holding Xinting and Nanzhou. Then one wave of the banner will settle everything.

sentences.zh: 乃加沖之左衛將軍，以陶亮為右衛將軍，統諸州兵俱下。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to Left Guard General, and Tao Liang was made Right Guard General, commanding all the provincial troops to descend together.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi was then promoted to Left Guard General, and Tao Liang was appointed Right Guard General to command all the provincial troops southward together.

sentences.zh: 郢州軍主鄭景玄、荊州軍主劉亮、湘州軍主何昌、梁州軍主柳登、雍州軍主宗庶等合二萬人，一時俱下。

translations.literal: Zheng Jingxuan, army commander of Ying Province; Liu Liang, army commander of Jing Province; He Chang, army commander of Xiang Province; Liu Deng, army commander of Liang Province; and Zong Shu, army commander of Yong Province, together totaled twenty thousand men, all descending at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jingxuan, army commander of Ying Province; Liu Liang, army commander of Jing Province; He Chang, army commander of Xiang Province; Liu Deng, army commander of Liang Province; and Zong Shu, army commander of Yong Province—together twenty thousand men—all descended at once.

sentences.zh: 亮本無幹略，聞建安王休仁自上，殷孝祖又至，不敢進，屯軍鵲洲。

translations.literal: Liang originally had no capacity or strategy; hearing that the Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren was coming from above, and that Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he did not dare advance and encamped his army at Quezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang had no real capacity or strategy. Hearing that the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, was coming from the north and that Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he did not dare advance and encamped at Quezhou.

sentences.zh: 時琬遣閻湛之來寇廬江，臺軍主、龍驤將軍段佛榮受命討之。

translations.literal: At that time Wan sent Yan Wanzhi to raid Lujiang; Duan Furong, army commander of the imperial army and General of the Flying Dragon, received orders to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deng Wan sent Yan Wanzhi to raid Lujiang. Duan Furong, an imperial army commander and General of the Flying Dragon, received orders to attack him.

sentences.zh: 更使佛榮領鐵騎一千，回軍南討。

translations.literal: He further had Furong lead one thousand iron cavalry and turn the army south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He further ordered Furong to lead one thousand armored cavalry and turn his army south to attack.

sentences.zh: 三月三日，水陸攻赭圻，亮等率眾來救，殷孝祖為流矢所中死，軍主朱輔之、申謙之、張靈符竝失利，輔之副正員將軍皇甫仲遠、謙之副虎賁中郎將徐稚賓並沒。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month, land and water forces attacked Zheqi; Liang and the others led troops to rescue; Yin Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died; the army commanders Zhu Fuzhi, Shen Qianzhi, and Zhang Lingfu all suffered defeat; Fuzhi's deputy, regular general Huangfu Zhongyuan, and Qianzhi's deputy, Tiger Guard Commandant Xu Zhibin, both perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month, land and water forces attacked Zheqi. Liu Liang and the others led troops to the rescue. Yin Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died. The army commanders Zhu Fuzhi, Shen Qianzhi, and Zhang Lingfu all suffered defeat. Fuzhi's deputy, Regular General Huangfu Zhongyuan, and Qianzhi's deputy, Tiger Guard Commandant Xu Zhibin, both perished.

sentences.zh: 孝祖支軍主范潛率五百人投亮。

translations.literal: Fan Qian, a subordinate army commander of Xiaozu, led five hundred men and surrendered to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qian, a subordinate army commander under Yin Xiaozu, led five hundred men and surrendered to Liu Liang.

sentences.zh: 時東軍已捷，江方興復還虎檻，建安王休仁遣方興、劉靈遺各領三千人助赭圻，以方興領孝祖軍，沈攸之代孝祖為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern army had already won; Jiang Fangxing returned again to Hujian; the Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren sent Fangxing and Liu Lingyi each to lead three thousand men to assist at Zheqi; Fangxing took command of Xiaozu's army, and Shen Youzhi replaced Xiaozu as commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: By then the eastern army had already won. Jiang Fangxing returned to Hujian. The Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, sent Fangxing and Liu Lingyi each with three thousand men to reinforce Zheqi. Fangxing took command of Yin Xiaozu's army, and Shen Youzhi replaced Xiaozu as commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 沖之謂陶亮曰：「孝祖梟將，一戰便死。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said to Tao Liang: 'Xiaozu was a fierce general; in one battle he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi said to Tao Liang: "Yin Xiaozu was a fierce general, and he died in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 天下事定矣，不須復戰，便當直取京都。」

translations.literal: The affairs of the realm are settled; there is no need to fight again—we should at once take the capital directly.'
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of the realm are settled. There is no need to fight again—we should march directly on the capital.

sentences.zh: 亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang did not agree.
