translations.idiomatic: Liang did not agree.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣員外散騎侍郎王道隆至赭圻督戰。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Wang Daolong, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, to Zheqi to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Wang Daolong, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, to Zheqi to supervise the battle.

sentences.zh: 孝祖死之明日，建安王休仁又遣軍主郭季之馬步三千就攸之，攸之乃率季之及輔國將軍步兵校尉杜幼文、寧朔將軍屯騎校尉垣恭祖、龍驤將軍朱輔之、員外散騎侍郎高遵世、馬軍主龍驤將軍頓生、段佛榮等三萬人，詰旦進戰，奮擊，大破之，斬獲數千，追奔至姥山而反。

translations.literal: On the day after Xiaozu's death, the Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren again sent the army commander Guo Jizhi with three thousand horse and foot to join Youzhi; Youzhi then led Jizhi and the Auxiliary General Du Youwen, General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of Foot Soldiers; Yuan Gongzu, General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of Garrison Cavalry; Zhu Fuzhi, General of the Flying Dragon; Gao Zunshi, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry; Dun Sheng, cavalry commander and General of the Flying Dragon; and Duan Furong—thirty thousand men in all—to advance to battle at dawn, strike fiercely, and rout them greatly, beheading and capturing several thousand; they pursued the fleeing enemy to Laoshan and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Yin Xiaozu's death, the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, again sent the army commander Guo Jizhi with three thousand horse and foot to join Shen Youzhi. Youzhi then led Jizhi along with the Auxiliary General Du Youwen, General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of Foot Soldiers; Yuan Gongzu, General Who Pacifies the North and Commandant of Garrison Cavalry; Zhu Fuzhi, General of the Flying Dragon; Gao Zunshi, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry; Dun Sheng, cavalry commander and General of the Flying Dragon; and Duan Furong—thirty thousand men in all—to advance to battle at dawn. They struck fiercely and routed the enemy, beheading and capturing several thousand. They pursued the fleeing enemy to Laoshan and then returned.

sentences.zh: 沖之等於湖、白口築二城，為軍主張興世所拔。

translations.literal: Chongzhi and the others built two cities at Hu and Baikou, and they were captured by the army commander Zhang Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi and the others built two fortresses at Hu and Baikou, and both were captured by the army commander Zhang Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 陶亮聞湖、白二城陷沒，大懼，急呼沖之還鵲尾，留薛常寶代沖之守赭圻。

translations.literal: Tao Liang heard that the two cities of Hu and Bai had fallen, was greatly afraid, and urgently called Chongzhi back to Quewei, leaving Xue Changbao to replace Chongzhi in guarding Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Liang heard that the two fortresses at Hu and Baikou had fallen, he was greatly afraid. He urgently called Chongzhi back to Quewei and left Xue Changbao to replace him in guarding Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 先於姥山及諸岡分立營寨，亦悉敗還，共保濃湖。

translations.literal: They had earlier set up separate camps at Laoshan and various hillocks, but all were defeated and retreated, jointly holding Nonghu.
translations.idiomatic: They had earlier set up separate camps at Laoshan and on various hillocks, but all were defeated and fell back, jointly holding Nonghu.

sentences.zh: 濃湖即在鵲尾。

translations.literal: Nonghu is right at Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Nonghu is right at Quewei.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅大起，國用不足，募民上米二百斛，錢五萬，雜穀五百斛，同賜荒縣除。

translations.literal: At that time the armies were greatly raised and state revenue was insufficient; they recruited the people to contribute two hundred hu of rice, fifty thousand coins, and five hundred hu of mixed grain, granting in return appointment to an impoverished county.
translations.idiomatic: At that time armies were being raised on a vast scale and state revenue was insufficient. The court recruited civilians to contribute two hundred hu of rice, fifty thousand coins, and five hundred hu of mixed grain, granting in return appointment to an impoverished county.

sentences.zh: 上米三百斛，錢八萬，雜穀千斛，同賜四品正令史；

translations.literal: Three hundred hu of rice, eighty thousand coins, and one thousand hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment to a regular clerk of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred hu of rice, eighty thousand coins, and one thousand hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment as a regular clerk of the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署四品在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: When the quota was filled, if one wished to be appointed fourth rank while remaining at home, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the quota was filled, if one wished to receive a fourth-rank appointment while remaining at home, that was also permitted.

sentences.zh: 上米四百斛，錢十二萬，雜穀一千三百斛，同賜四品正令史；

translations.literal: Four hundred hu of rice, one hundred twenty thousand coins, and one thousand three hundred hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment to a regular clerk of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred hu of rice, one hundred twenty thousand coins, and one thousand three hundred hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment as a regular clerk of the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署三品在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: When the quota was filled, if one wished to be appointed third rank while remaining at home, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the quota was filled, if one wished to receive a third-rank appointment while remaining at home, that was also permitted.

sentences.zh: 上米五百斛，錢十五萬，雜穀一千五百斛，同賜三品令史；

translations.literal: Five hundred hu of rice, one hundred fifty thousand coins, and one hundred fifty hundred hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment to a clerk of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred hu of rice, one hundred fifty thousand coins, and one thousand five hundred hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment as a clerk of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 滿報，若欲署內監在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: When the quota was filled, if one wished to be appointed to the inner palace supervisor while remaining at home, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the quota was filled, if one wished to receive appointment as inner palace supervisor while remaining at home, that was also permitted.

sentences.zh: 上米七百斛，錢二十萬，雜穀二千斛，同賜荒郡除；

translations.literal: Seven hundred hu of rice, two hundred thousand coins, and two thousand hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment to an impoverished commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred hu of rice, two hundred thousand coins, and two thousand hu of mixed grain granted in return appointment to an impoverished commandery.

sentences.zh: 若欲署諸王國三令在家，亦聽。

translations.literal: If one wished to be appointed third clerk of a princely kingdom while remaining at home, that was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If one wished to receive appointment as third clerk of a princely kingdom while remaining at home, that was also permitted.

sentences.zh: 琬又遣輔國將軍、豫州刺史劉胡率眾三萬，鐵騎二千，來屯鵲尾。

translations.literal: Wan again sent Liu Hu, General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yu Province, to lead thirty thousand troops and two thousand iron cavalry to encamp at Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan again sent Liu Hu, General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yu Province, to lead thirty thousand troops and two thousand armored cavalry to encamp at Quewei.

sentences.zh: 胡宿將，屢有戰功，素多狡詐，為眾推伏，攸之等甚憚之。

translations.literal: Hu was a veteran general, repeatedly victorious in battle, always very crafty and deceitful, and was respected and submitted to by the masses; Youzhi and the others greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu was a veteran general with repeated victories in battle. He was notoriously crafty and deceitful, and the troops respected and submitted to him. Shen Youzhi and the others greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 時胡鄉人蔡那、佼長生、張敬兒各領軍隸攸之在赭圻，胡以書招之，那等並拒絕。

translations.literal: At that time Hu's fellow townsmen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er each led armies under Youzhi at Zheqi; Hu sent letters to recruit them, and Na and the others all refused.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Hu's fellow townsmen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er each led armies under Shen Youzhi at Zheqi. Liu Hu sent letters to recruit them, but Na and the others all refused.

sentences.zh: 胡因要那等共語，陳說平生，那等詰誚，說令歸順。

translations.literal: Hu therefore invited Na and the others to speak together, recounting their lives from youth; Na and the others questioned and mocked him, urging him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu therefore invited Na and the others to meet and talk, recounting their shared past. Na and the others questioned and mocked him, urging him to surrender instead.

sentences.zh: 胡回軍入鵲尾，無他權略。

translations.literal: Hu returned his army into Quewei, with no other stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu withdrew his army into Quewei, with no other stratagem to offer.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍吳喜平定三吳，率所領五千人，并運資實，至於赭圻，於戰鳥山築壘，分遣千人，乘輕舸二百，與佼長生為游軍。

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State Wu Xi had pacified the Three Wu; leading the five thousand men under his command, together with transporting supplies and goods, he reached Zheqi, built a fort on Zhan'niao Mountain, dispatched a thousand men, and with two hundred light boats, together with Jiao Changsheng, served as a mobile force.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State Wu Xi, having pacified the Three Wu, led his five thousand troops to Zheqi with supplies and provisions. He built a fort on Zhan'niao Mountain, detached a thousand men aboard two hundred light boats, and with Jiao Changsheng formed a mobile strike force.

sentences.zh: 薛常寶糧盡，告胡求援。

translations.literal: Xue Changbao's grain was exhausted, and he sent word to Hu requesting aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Changbao's supplies ran out, and he sent word to Liu Hu begging for relief.

sentences.zh: 三月二十九日，胡率步卒一萬，夜斫山開道，以布囊運米，來餉赭圻。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month, Hu led ten thousand foot soldiers, cut through the mountains by night to open a road, and transported rice in cloth sacks to provision Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth day of the third month, Liu Hu led ten thousand infantry. By night they hewed through the mountains to open a path and carried rice in cloth sacks to supply Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 平旦至城下，猶隔小塹，未能得入。

translations.literal: At daybreak they reached below the city, but were still separated by a small moat and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they reached the foot of the city, but a small trench still lay between them and the walls, and they could not get in.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之率眾軍攻之，軍主郭季之、荀僧韶、幢主韓欣宗等，率眾三千，為攸之勢援。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi led the mass of armies to attack them; the army commanders Guo Jizhi, Xun Sengshao, and banner commander Han Xinzong and others led three thousand men to reinforce Youzhi's momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi led the main force to attack them. Army commanders Guo Jizhi, Xun Sengshao, and banner commander Han Xinzong, with three thousand men, came up to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 胡發所由橋道，僧韶等接楯行戰，復橋得渡。

translations.literal: Hu set fire to the bridge along which they had come; Sengshao and the others fought with shields joined, recovered the bridge, and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu burned the bridge by which he had come. Sengshao and the others fought shield to shield, retook the bridge, and got across.

sentences.zh: 軍主劉沙彌輕騎深入，至胡麾下，遂見殺。

translations.literal: The army commander Liu Shami, with light cavalry, plunged deep in and reached beneath Hu's command; he was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Liu Shami led light cavalry deep into the enemy lines until he reached Liu Hu's own standard, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 攸之策馬陷陳，回還，為追騎所刺；

translations.literal: Youzhi spurred his horse into the formation; turning back, he was stabbed by pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi spurred his horse into the enemy ranks; as he wheeled about, pursuing horsemen stabbed him.

sentences.zh: 馬軍主段佛榮、武保救之得免。

translations.literal: The cavalry army commander Duan Furong and Wu Bao rescued him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry army commander Duan Furong and Wu Bao pulled him out, and he escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 並殊死戰，多所傷殺。

translations.literal: Both sides fought to the death, wounding and killing many.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides fought with desperate fury, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 胡眾大敗，捨糧棄甲，緣山遁走，乘勝追之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Hu's masses were greatly defeated; they abandoned grain and cast off armor, fled along the mountains, were pursued in victory, and very many were beheaded or captured.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu's army was routed. The men threw away grain and armor and fled along the mountain paths. The victors pressed the pursuit and killed or captured a great number.

sentences.zh: 胡被創，僅得還營。

translations.literal: Hu was wounded and barely made it back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu was wounded and barely made it back to camp alive.

sentences.zh: 常寶惶懼無計，遣信告胡，欲突圍奔出。

translations.literal: Changbao was fearful and without a plan; he sent a messenger to tell Hu that he wished to break out and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Changbao, terrified and at his wits' end, sent word to Liu Hu that he wanted to break out of the city and escape.

sentences.zh: 四月四日，胡自率數千人迎之，常寶等開城突圍走。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fourth month, Hu personally led several thousand men to meet him; Changbao and the others opened the city, broke out, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fourth month, Liu Hu personally led several thousand men to meet them. Changbao and his companions opened the gates, broke out, and fled.

sentences.zh: 攸之率輔國將軍沈懷明、軍主周普孫、江方興、申謙之等諸軍悉力擊之。

translations.literal: Youzhi led General Who Assists the State Shen Huaiming, army commanders Zhou Pusun, Jiang Fangxing, Shen Qianzhi, and the rest of the armies to strike them with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi led General Who Assists the State Shen Huaiming, army commanders Zhou Pusun, Jiang Fangxing, Shen Qianzhi, and the rest of the force in an all-out attack.

sentences.zh: 吳喜率眾來赴，為胡別軍所圍，甚急。

translations.literal: Wu Xi led the masses to come to the rescue and was surrounded by a detached force of Hu's; the situation was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi hurried up with reinforcements, but a detached unit of Liu Hu's army surrounded him, and the situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 有人來捉喜馬，將蔡保以刀斫之，斷手，然後得免。

translations.literal: Someone came to seize Xi's horse; the officer Cai Bao hacked at him with a blade, severed his hand, and only then did Xi escape.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy soldier seized Wu Xi's bridle; officer Cai Bao hacked at the man with his blade and cut off his hand, and only then did Xi get free.

sentences.zh: 正員將軍幢主卜伯宗、江夏國侍郎幢主張渙力戰沒陳。

translations.literal: Regular general and banner commander Bu Bozong, and Attendant of the Principality of Jiangxia and banner commander Zhang Huan, fought fiercely and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Regular general and banner commander Bu Bozong, and Attendant of the Principality of Jiangxia and banner commander Zhang Huan, fought to the last and fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 伯宗，益州刺史天與子也。

translations.literal: Bozong was the son of Tian Yu, Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong was the son of Tian Yu, Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 攸之、喜等苦戰移日，常寶、張繼伯、胡靈秀、焦度等皆被重創，走還胡軍。

translations.literal: Youzhi, Xi, and the others fought bitterly for a whole day; Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Hu Lingxiu, Jiao Du, and the rest were all heavily wounded and fled back to Hu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, and the others battled bitterly all day. Changbao, Zhang Jibo, Hu Lingxiu, Jiao Du, and the rest were all gravely wounded and fled back to Liu Hu's lines.

sentences.zh: 赭圻城陷，斬偽寧朔將軍南陽太守沈懷寶、偽奉朝請領中舍人督戰謝道遇，納降數千。

translations.literal: Zheqi city fell; the usurping General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Nanyang Shen Huaibao and the usurping Gentleman at Court Attendance, Chief Master of the Household directing battle Xie Daoyu were beheaded, and several thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zheqi fell. The rebel General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Nanyang Shen Huaibao, and the rebel Gentleman at Court Attendance and Chief Master of the Household who directed the defense, Xie Daoyu, were beheaded, and several thousand men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 陳紹宗單舸奔西岸，與其部曲俱還鵲尾。

translations.literal: Chen Shaozong, in a single boat, fled to the western bank and, together with his personal troops, all returned to Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaozong fled alone in one boat to the western shore and, with his personal followers, withdrew to Quewei.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁自虎檻進據赭圻。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, advanced from Hujian and took possession of Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, advanced from Hujian and occupied Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 劉胡遣陳紹宗、陳慶率輕艓二百，大艦五十，出鵲外挑戰；

translations.literal: Liu Hu sent Chen Shaozong and Chen Qing to lead two hundred light warships and fifty large ships to sally forth outside Que and offer battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent Chen Shaozong and Chen Qing with two hundred light warships and fifty large ships to sail out beyond Que and offer battle.

sentences.zh: 吳喜、張興世、佼長生等擊之。

translations.literal: Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, Jiao Changsheng, and the others attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi, Zhang Xingshi, Jiao Changsheng, and the others attacked them.

sentences.zh: 喜支軍主吳獻之飛舸衝突，所向摧陷，斬獲及投水死甚多，追至鵲裏而還。

translations.literal: Xi's detached army commander Wu Xianzhi, in flying boats, charged and broke through; wherever he turned he smashed the enemy; very many were beheaded, captured, or drowned; he pursued as far as Queli and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's detached commander Wu Xianzhi drove his swift boats headlong into the enemy, crushing all before him. Very many were killed, captured, or drowned. He pursued the fugitives to Queli and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮胡等或於步路向京邑，使寧朔將軍、廣德令王蘊千人防魯顯。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming feared that Hu and the others might march overland toward the capital and sent General Who Pacifies the North and Magistrate of Guangde Wang Yun with a thousand men to guard Luxian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming feared that Liu Hu and his allies might march overland on the capital, and sent General Who Pacifies the North and Magistrate of Guangde Wang Yun with a thousand men to hold Luxian.

sentences.zh: 時胡等兵眾強盛，遠近疑惑。

translations.literal: At that time Hu and the others' troops were powerful and flourishing, and near and far were filled with doubt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Hu's army was strong, and men near and far were uncertain which side would prevail.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲綏慰人情，遣吏部尚書褚淵至虎檻選用將帥以下，申謙之、杜幼文因此求黃門郎，沈懷明、劉亮求中書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wished to soothe popular sentiment and sent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan to Hujian to select and appoint men from army commanders downward; Shen Qianzhi and Du Youwen therefore requested appointment as Attendants of the Yellow Gate, and Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang requested appointment as Attendants of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wished to reassure the people and sent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yuan to Hujian to appoint officers from army commanders on down. Shen Qianzhi and Du Youwen used the occasion to ask for posts as Attendants of the Yellow Gate; Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang asked for posts as Attendants of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁即使褚淵擬選，上不許，曰：「忠臣殉國，不謀其報，臨難以干朝典，豈臣下之節邪？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Liu Xiuren then had Chu Yuan draw up the selections, but the emperor did not approve, saying: "Loyal ministers die for the state and do not calculate their reward; to importune for court honors in the midst of hardship—how is that the conduct of a subject?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, had Chu Yuan draw up the appointments, but the emperor refused, saying, "Loyal ministers die for the state without thought of reward. To press for court honors in the midst of battle—what sort of conduct is that for a subject?"

sentences.zh: 始安內史王職之、建安內史趙道生、安成太守劉襲，並舉郡奉順。

translations.literal: The Interior Minister of Shian Wang Zhizhi, the Interior Minister of Jian'an Zhao Daosheng, and the Governor of Ancheng Liu Xi all raised their commanderies in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhizhi, Interior Minister of Shian; Zhao Daosheng, Interior Minister of Jian'an; and Liu Xi, Governor of Ancheng, all brought their commanderies over to the court.

sentences.zh: 琬遣龍驤將軍廖琰率數千人，并發廬陵白丁攻襲。

translations.literal: Wan sent General of the Flying Dragon Liao Yan to lead several thousand men and also mobilized corvée laborers from Luling to attack Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent General of the Flying Dragon Liao Yan with several thousand men and also drafted corvée laborers from Luling to attack Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 襲與郡丞檀玢拒戰，大敗，玢臨陳見殺，襲棄郡走，據險自守。

translations.literal: Xi, together with the commandery aide Tan Bin, resisted in battle and was greatly defeated; Bin was killed in battle, Xi abandoned the commandery and fled, and held difficult terrain to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi and the commandery aide Tan Bin met them in battle and were routed. Tan Bin was killed on the field; Liu Xi abandoned the commandery and fled, then held rough country and defended himself.

sentences.zh: 琰虜掠而退，襲復出據郡。

translations.literal: Yan plundered and withdrew; Xi again came out and took possession of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Yan looted the region and withdrew, and Liu Xi came back out and reoccupied the commandery.

sentences.zh: 時齊王率眾東北征討，而齊王世子為南康贛令，琬遣使收世子；

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi was leading the masses on a northeastern campaign, while the Prince of Qi's heir was Magistrate of Gan in Nankang commandery; Wan sent envoys to seize the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qi was campaigning northeast with his army, while the prince's heir served as Magistrate of Gan in Nankang. Deng Wan sent men to seize the heir.

sentences.zh: 世子腹心蕭欣祖、桓康等數十人，奉世子長子奔竄草澤，召募得百餘人，攻郡出世子。

translations.literal: Several dozen of the heir's closest confidants, including Xiao Xinzu and Huan Kang, escorted the heir's eldest son and fled into the marshes; they recruited a little more than a hundred men and attacked the commandery to free the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of the heir's closest followers, including Xiao Xinzu and Huan Kang, took the heir's eldest son and fled into the wild marshes. They raised a little over a hundred men and stormed the commandery seat to rescue the heir.

sentences.zh: 世子自號寧朔將軍，與南康相沈用之、前南海太守何曇直、晉康太守劉紹祖、北地傅浩、東莞童禽等，據郡起義。

translations.literal: The heir styled himself General Who Pacifies the North and, together with the Chancellor of Nankang Shen Yongzhi, former Governor of Nanhai He Tanzhi, Governor of Jinkang Liu Shaozu, Fu Hao of Beidi, and Tong Qin of Dongguan and others, seized the commandery and raised the banner of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The heir took for himself the title General Who Pacifies the North and, with the Chancellor of Nankang Shen Yongzhi, former Governor of Nanhai He Tanzhi, Governor of Jinkang Liu Shaozu, Fu Hao of Beidi, Tong Qin of Dongguan, and others, seized the commandery and rose in arms for the court.

sentences.zh: 琬徴始興相殷孚為御史中丞，并令率郡人俱下。

translations.literal: Wan summoned the Chancellor of Shixing Yin Fu to be Censor-in-Chief and also ordered him to lead the men of the commandery down together.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan summoned Yin Fu, Chancellor of Shixing, to serve as Censor-in-Chief and ordered him to bring the commandery levies south with him.

sentences.zh: 孚眾盛，世子避之於揭陽山。

translations.literal: Fu's masses were strong, and the heir avoided him on Jieyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Fu's force was large, and the heir withdrew to Jieyang Mountain to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 琬遣武昌戴凱之為南康相，世子率眾攻之，凱之戰敗遁走。

translations.literal: Wan sent Dai Kaizhi of Wuchang to be Chancellor of Nankang; the heir led the masses to attack him, and Kaizhi was defeated in battle and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent Dai Kaizhi of Wuchang to serve as Chancellor of Nankang. The heir attacked him with his force; Kaizhi was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 世子遣幢主檀文起千人戍西昌，與襲相應。

translations.literal: The heir sent banner commander Tan Wenqi with a thousand men to garrison Xichang in coordination with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The heir sent banner commander Tan Wenqi with a thousand men to garrison Xichang in concert with Liu Xi.

sentences.zh: 琬又遣廖琰與其中兵參軍胡昭等築壘於西昌，堅壁相守。

translations.literal: Wan again sent Liao Yan together with his Central Guard Staff Officer Hu Zhao and others to build a fort at Xichang and hold fast behind strong walls.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan again sent Liao Yan, together with his Central Guard Staff Officer Hu Zhao and others, to build a fort at Xichang and stand on the defensive behind stout walls.

sentences.zh: 琬召豫章太守劉衍以為右將軍、中護軍，殷孚代為豫章太守，督上流五郡，以防襲等。

translations.literal: Wan summoned Liu Yan, Governor of Yuzhang, to be General of the Right and Central Guard Commander; Yin Fu replaced him as Governor of Yuzhang and supervised the five upstream commanderies to guard against Xi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan summoned Liu Yan, Governor of Yuzhang, to serve as General of the Right and Central Guard Commander. Yin Fu replaced him as Governor of Yuzhang and took charge of the five upstream commanderies to guard against Liu Xi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 衡陽內史王應之率郡文武五百許人，起義兵襲何慧文於長沙，徑至城下。

translations.literal: Wang Yingzhi, Interior Minister of Hengyang, led about five hundred civil and military men of the commandery, raised a volunteer force, and attacked He Huiwen at Changsha, going straight to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhi, Interior Minister of Hengyang, led some five hundred of the commandery's civil and military officials, raised a volunteer force, and struck at He Huiwen at Changsha, reaching the city walls at once.

sentences.zh: 慧文率左右出城與戰，應之勇氣奮發，擊殺數人，遂與慧文交手戰，斫慧文八創，慧文斫應之斷足，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Huiwen led his close attendants out of the city to fight; Yingzhi's courage flared, he struck and killed several men, then crossed blades with Huiwen in hand-to-hand combat, hacking Huiwen eight wounds; Huiwen hacked Yingzhi and severed his foot, then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen came out with his personal guard to fight. Yingzhi's courage surged; he killed several men, then closed with Huiwen and traded blows, cutting him eight times. Huiwen struck back, severed Yingzhi's foot, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時湘東國侍郎虞洽為太宗督國秩，在湘東，勸太守顏躍發兵應朝廷，躍不從。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Qia, Attendant of the Principality of Xiangdong, was supervising the prince's fief revenues for Emperor Ming and was in Xiangdong; he urged Governor Yan Yue to raise troops in response to the court, but Yue would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Qia, Attendant of the Principality of Xiangdong, was in Xiangdong supervising the fief revenues on Emperor Ming's behalf. He urged Governor Yan Yue to raise troops for the court, but Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 洽乃投桂陽，收募得數百人，還欲攻躍，躍懼求和，許之；

translations.literal: Qia then went to Guiyang, recruited several hundred men, returned intending to attack Yue; Yue feared this and sought peace, and Qia agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qia then went to Guiyang, raised several hundred men, and returned intending to attack Yan Yue. Yue, afraid, sued for peace, and Qia agreed.

sentences.zh: 有眾二千。

translations.literal: He had two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He now had two thousand men under his command.

sentences.zh: 時琬徵慧文率眾下尋陽，發長沙，已行數百里，聞洽起兵，乃回還攻洽，洽尋戰敗奔走。

translations.literal: At that time Wan had summoned Huiwen to lead the masses down to Xunyang; he set out from Changsha and had already gone several hundred li when he heard that Qia had raised troops; he then turned back to attack Qia, and Qia was soon defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan had already summoned He Huiwen to lead his force down to Xunyang. Huiwen had set out from Changsha and marched several hundred li when he heard that Yu Qia had risen in arms. He turned back to attack Qia, who was soon defeated and put to flight.

sentences.zh: 殷孚既去始興，以郡五官掾譚伯初留知郡事。

translations.literal: After Yin Fu had left Shixing, he left Tan Bochu, Clerk of the Five Offices, behind to manage commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin Fu left Shixing, he left Tan Bochu, Clerk of the Five Offices, behind to administer the commandery.

sentences.zh: 士人劉嗣祖等斬伯初，據郡起義。

translations.literal: The scholar Liu Sizu and others beheaded Bochu and seized the commandery to raise the banner of revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentleman Liu Sizu and others killed Tan Bochu, seized the commandery, and rose in arms for the court.

sentences.zh: 琬遣始興太守韋希真、鷹揚將軍楊弘之領眾一千討嗣祖。

translations.literal: Wan sent Governor of Shixing Wei Xizhen and General Who Raises the Hawk Yang Hongzhi to command a thousand men to suppress Sizu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan sent Wei Xizhen, Governor of Shixing, and General Who Raises the Hawk Yang Hongzhi with a thousand men to suppress Liu Sizu.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖亦遣眾出南康，與齊王世子合。

translations.literal: Sizu also sent troops out through Nankang to join the Prince of Qi's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sizu also sent troops out through Nankang to join the Prince of Qi's heir.

sentences.zh: 希真等以義徒強盛，住廬陵不敢進。

translations.literal: Xizhen and the others, because the volunteer force was strong, halted at Luling and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xizhen and his men, finding the rebel force too strong, halted at Luling and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史袁曇遠聞始興起義，遣將李萬周、陳伯紹率眾討嗣祖。

translations.literal: Yuan Tanyuan, Inspector of Guang Province, heard that Shixing had risen in revolt and sent generals Li Wanzhou and Chen Bozhao to lead troops to suppress Sizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tanyuan, Inspector of Guang Province, heard that Shixing had risen and sent generals Li Wanzhou and Chen Bozhao to suppress Liu Sizu.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖遣兵戍湞陽，萬周亦築壘相守。

translations.literal: Sizu sent troops to garrison Zhenyang, and Wanzhou also built a fort and stood on the defensive.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sizu sent troops to garrison Zhenyang, and Li Wanzhou likewise built a fort and held his ground.

sentences.zh: 嗣祖遣人誑萬周曰：「尋陽已平，臺遣劉勔為廣州，垂至。」

translations.literal: Sizu sent a man to deceive Wanzhou, saying: "Xunyang has already been pacified; the Court has dispatched Liu Mian as Governor of Guang Province, and he is about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sizu sent a man to deceive Li Wanzhou, saying, "Xunyang has already been pacified. The court has dispatched Liu Mian as Governor of Guang Province, and he is nearly here."

sentences.zh: 萬周信之，便回還襲番禺，夜以長梯入城；

translations.literal: Wanzhou believed it and at once turned back to raid Panyu, entering the city at night by long ladders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanzhou believed it, turned back at once, and raided Panyu, entering the city at night on long ladders.

sentences.zh: 曇遠怯弱無防，聞萬周反，便徒跣出奔，萬周追斬之於城內。

translations.literal: Tanyuan was timid and weak and without defense; hearing that Wanzhou had rebelled, he fled barefoot; Wanzhou pursued and beheaded him inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tanyuan was timid and unprepared. When he heard that Li Wanzhou had turned against him, he fled barefoot. Wanzhou pursued him and cut him down inside the city.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史檀翼被代還至廣州，資貨鉅萬，萬周誣以為逆，襲而殺之。

translations.literal: Tan Yi, Inspector of Jiao Province, had been replaced and was returning to Guang Province with goods worth tens of thousands; Wanzhou falsely accused him of rebellion, attacked him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yi, Inspector of Jiao Province, had been recalled and was returning to Guang Province with goods worth tens of thousands. Li Wanzhou falsely accused him of treason, attacked him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遂劫掠公私銀帛，藉略袁、檀珍寶，悉以自入。

translations.literal: He then plundered public and private silver and silk, seized the treasures of Yuan and Tan, and kept them all for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then looted public and private stores of silver and silk, seized the treasures of Yuan and Tan, and kept everything for himself.

sentences.zh: 袁顗悉雍州之眾，來赴尋陽。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi mustered all the masses of Yong Province and came to join Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi gathered the full strength of Yong Province and marched to join the force at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 時孔道存為衛軍長史，行荊州事。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Daocun was Chief Clerk to the Guard General and was acting for Jing Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Daocun was Chief Clerk to the Guard General and was acting governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 琬以黃門侍郎劉道憲代之，以道存為侍中，行雍州事。

translations.literal: Wan had Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Liu Daoxian replace him, and made Daocun Palace Attendant acting for Yong Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan had Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Liu Daoxian replace him and appointed Kong Daocun Palace Attendant, acting for Yong Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 柳元景之誅也，元景弟子世隆為上庸太守，民吏共藏匿之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuanjing was executed, Yuanjing's brother's son Shilong was Governor of Shangyong, and the people and officials together hid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanjing was executed, his brother's son Liu Shilong, then Governor of Shangyong, was hidden by the local officials and people.

sentences.zh: 顗起兵，召世隆，不至。

translations.literal: When Yi raised troops, he summoned Shilong, but Shilong did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi rose in arms, he summoned Liu Shilong, but Shilong did not come.

sentences.zh: 顗既下，世隆乃合率蠻、宋二千餘人，起義於上庸，來襲襄陽。

translations.literal: After Yi had marched south, Shilong then gathered and led more than two thousand Man and Song troops, raised the banner of revolt at Shangyong, and came to attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Yi marched south, Shilong gathered more than two thousand Man tribesmen and local Song troops, rose in arms at Shangyong, and marched to attack Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 道存遣將王式民、康元隆等迎擊於萬山，世隆大敗，還郡自守。

translations.literal: Daocun sent generals Wang Shimin, Kang Yuanlong, and others to meet and strike them at Wanshan; Shilong was greatly defeated and returned to the commandery to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daocun sent generals Wang Shimin, Kang Yuanlong, and others to meet them at Wanshan. Shilong was routed and withdrew to his commandery to hold out.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之等與劉胡相持久不決，上又遣強弩將軍任農夫、振武將軍武會倉、冗從僕射全景文、軍主劉伯符等領兵繼至。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and the others faced Liu Hu in a prolonged stalemate without decision; the emperor again sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu, General Who Quells the Barbarians Wu Huicang, Supernumerary Master of Ceremonies Quan Jingwen, army commander Liu Bofu, and others to lead troops in succession to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi and the others remained locked in a stalemate with Liu Hu. The emperor sent Strong Crossbow General Ren Nongfu, General Who Quells the Barbarians Wu Huicang, Supernumerary Master of Ceremonies Quan Jingwen, army commander Liu Bofu, and others with reinforcements in succession.

sentences.zh: 攸之繕治船舸，材板不周，計無所出。

translations.literal: Youzhi repaired boats and ships, but timber and planks were insufficient, and he had no plan to resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi set about repairing his fleet, but timber and planking were short, and he could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 會琬送五千片榜供胡軍用，俄而風潮奔迅，榜捍突柵出江，胡等力不能制，自撞船艦，殺沒數十人，赴流而下，來泊攸之等營，於是材板大足。

translations.literal: Just then Wan sent five thousand planks for Hu's army's use; shortly afterward wind and waves surged swiftly, the planks broke through the palisade and went out into the river; Hu and the others could not control them; they themselves collided with the ships, and several tens were killed or drowned; they went downstream and came to moor at Youzhi's and the others' camp; thus timber and planks became greatly sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Deng Wan sent five thousand planks for Liu Hu's army. Suddenly wind and tide surged; the planks burst through the stockade and swept out into the river. Hu's men could not stop them—the rafts crashed into their own ships and drowned several dozen men—then drifted downstream and fetched up at Shen Youzhi's camp. Suddenly he had timber and planking in abundance.

sentences.zh: 琬進袁顗都督征討諸軍事，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Wan promoted Yuan Yi to Grand Marshal directing all armies on campaign and granted one set of war drums and horns.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan promoted Yuan Yi to Grand Marshal directing all armies on campaign and granted him one set of war drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 六月十八日，顗率樓船千艘，來入鵲尾，張興世建議越鵲尾上據錢溪，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, Yi led a thousand tower ships and entered Quewei; Zhang Xingshi proposed crossing above Quewei to seize Qianxi and cut their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the sixth month, Yuan Yi led a thousand tower ships into Quewei. Zhang Xingshi proposed crossing upstream of Quewei to seize Qianxi and cut the enemy's supply line.

sentences.zh: 胡累攻之，不能克，事在興世傳。

translations.literal: Hu repeatedly attacked him but could not overcome him; the affair is recorded in Xingshi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu attacked him again and again but could not break him; the affair is told in Zhang Xingshi's biography.

sentences.zh: 劉亮率所領至胡寨下，胡遣其副孫犀及張靈、焦度鐵騎五匹，越磵取亮，不能得，犀回馬去，亮使左右善射者夾射之，墜馬，斬犀首。

translations.literal: Liu Liang led those under his command to below Hu's camp; Hu sent his deputy Sun Xi together with Zhang Ling and Jiao Du, five armored horsemen, to cross the stream and seize Liang but could not get him; Xi turned his horse to leave; Liang had skilled archers on either side shoot at him in volley; Xi fell from his horse and his head was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang led his command to the foot of Liu Hu's camp. Hu sent his deputy Sun Xi with Zhang Ling and Jiao Du—five armored horsemen—to cross the stream and capture Liang, but they failed. As Xi wheeled to withdraw, Liang had skilled archers on either side shoot him down from his horse and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 張繼伯副馬可率所領來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Jibo's deputy Ma Ke led those under his command to come over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jibo's deputy Ma Ke led his command in surrender.

sentences.zh: 劉亮營寨，深入賊地，袁顗畏憚之，曰：「賊入我肝臟裏，何由得活！」

translations.literal: Liu Liang's camp was deep in enemy territory; Yuan Yi feared and dreaded him, saying: "The rebels are inside our very liver and entrails—how can we survive!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang's camp lay deep in enemy country. Yuan Yi was alarmed and said, "The enemy is inside our very liver and guts—how are we to live?"

sentences.zh: 劉胡率輕舸四百，由鵲頭內路，欲攻錢溪。

translations.literal: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats, taking the inner route from Quetou, intending to attack Qianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu led four hundred light boats by the inner route from Quetou, intending to attack Qianxi.

sentences.zh: 既而謂其長史王念叔曰：「吾少習步戰，未閑水鬥。

translations.literal: Then he said to his Chief Clerk Wang Nianshu: "I have practiced infantry fighting since youth and am not skilled in naval combat.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to his Chief Clerk Wang Nianshu, "I have trained in infantry fighting since youth and am not versed in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 若步戰，恆在數萬人中，水戰在一舸之上，舸舸各進，不復相關，正在三十人中取，此非萬全之計，吾不為也。」

translations.literal: In infantry battle one is always among tens of thousands of men; in naval battle one is on a single boat—each boat advances separately, no longer connected to the others—the issue is decided among thirty men. This is not a plan of complete safety; I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: On land one fights among tens of thousands; on the water one stands on a single boat. Boat follows boat, each on its own, with no mutual support—the fight comes down to thirty men. That is no sure plan, and I will not undertake it."

sentences.zh: 乃託瘧疾，住鵲頭不進。

translations.literal: He then feigned malaria and halted at Quetou without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: With that he pleaded malaria and halted at Quetou without advancing.

sentences.zh: 遣龍驤將軍陳慶領三百舸向錢溪，戒慶不須戰：「張興世、武會倉，吾之所悉，自當走耳。」

translations.literal: He sent General of the Flying Dragon Chen Qing to lead three hundred boats toward Qianxi, instructing Qing not to fight: "Zhang Xingshi and Wu Huicang—I know them well—they will flee on their own."
translations.idiomatic: He sent General of the Flying Dragon Chen Qing with three hundred boats toward Qianxi, telling him not to fight: "Zhang Xingshi and Wu Huicang—I know them—they will run on their own."

sentences.zh: 陳慶至錢溪，不敢攻。

translations.literal: Chen Qing reached Qianxi but did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing reached Qianxi but did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 越錢溪，於梅根立寨。

translations.literal: He crossed beyond Qianxi and built a camp at Meigan.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed past Qianxi and built a camp at Meigan.

sentences.zh: 胡別遣將王起領百舸攻興世，興世擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Hu separately sent general Wang Qi to lead a hundred boats to attack Xingshi; Xingshi struck them and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu separately sent general Wang Qi with a hundred boats to attack Zhang Xingshi. Xingshi counterattacked and routed him.

sentences.zh: 胡率其餘舸馳還，謂顗曰：「興世營寨已立，不可卒攻，昨日小戰，未足為損。

translations.literal: Hu led the remaining boats in a galloping return and said to Yi: "Xingshi's camp is already established and cannot be taken in a sudden attack; yesterday's small battle was no great loss.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu raced back with the remaining boats and told Yuan Yi, "Xingshi's camp is already set—it cannot be stormed at once. Yesterday's skirmish was no serious harm.

sentences.zh: 陳慶已與南陵、大雷諸軍共遏其上，大軍在此，鵲頭諸將又斷其下流，已墮圍中，不足復慮。」

translations.literal: Chen Qing has already joined the Nanling and Dalei armies in blocking them upstream; the main army is here, and the Quetou generals have also cut their downstream route—they have already fallen into an encirclement, and there is no need to worry further."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing has already joined the Nanling and Dalei forces to block them upstream. The main army is here, and the Quetou generals have cut their line downstream. They are already trapped—there is nothing more to fear."

sentences.zh: 顗怒胡不戰，謂曰：「糧運梗塞，當如此何？」

translations.literal: Yi, angry that Hu would not fight, said: "Grain transport is blocked—what are we to do about this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, furious that Liu Hu would not fight, said, "Our grain route is cut off—what are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 胡曰：「彼尚得泝流越我而上，此運何以不得沿流越彼而下邪！」

translations.literal: Hu said: "They could still ascend upstream past us—why cannot this transport descend downstream past them!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu replied, "If they could still fight their way upstream past us, why cannot our supplies go downstream past them?"

sentences.zh: 顗更使胡率步卒二萬，鐵馬一千，往攻興世。

translations.literal: Yi again ordered Hu to lead twenty thousand foot soldiers and a thousand iron cavalry to go attack Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi again ordered Liu Hu to lead twenty thousand infantry and a thousand armored cavalry against Zhang Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 休仁因此命沈攸之、吳喜、佼長生、劉靈遺、劉伯符等進攻濃湖，造皮艦十乘，拔其營柵，苦戰移日，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiuren therefore ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, Liu Bofu, and the others to advance and attack Nonghu; they built ten leather-covered warships, pulled up their camp palisades, fought bitterly for a whole day, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuren therefore ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, Liu Bofu, and the others to advance on Nonghu. They built ten leather-covered assault boats, tore up the enemy palisades, fought bitterly all day, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 顗被攻既急，馳信召胡令還。

translations.literal: Yi, pressed hard in the attack, sent a messenger in haste summoning Hu to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, hard pressed in the attack, sent an urgent message summoning Liu Hu back.

sentences.zh: 張興世既據錢溪，江路岨斷，胡軍乏食，琬大送資糧，畏興世不敢下。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi had already seized Qianxi; the river route was steep and cut off; Hu's army lacked food; Wan sent supplies in great quantity but feared Xingshi and did not dare descend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi already held Qianxi, and the river route was steep and blocked. Liu Hu's army went hungry. Deng Wan sent large quantities of supplies, but the convoys feared Xingshi and did not dare come downstream.

sentences.zh: 胡遣將迎之，為錢溪所破，資實覆沒都盡，燒米三十萬斛，胡眾駭懼。

translations.literal: Hu sent generals to meet them; they were defeated at Qianxi; supplies and goods were overturned and lost entirely; three hundred thousand hu of rice were burned; Hu's masses were terrified and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu sent generals to escort the convoy, but they were broken at Qianxi. The supplies were lost entirely, three hundred thousand hu of rice were burned, and Hu's army was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 胡副張喜來降，說胡欲叛。

translations.literal: Hu's deputy Zhang Xi came over in surrender and reported that Hu intended to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu's deputy Zhang Xi came over in surrender and reported that Hu meant to defect.

sentences.zh: 八月二十四日，胡誑顗云：「更率步騎二萬，上取興世，兼下大雷餘餫。」

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month, Hu deceived Yi, saying: "I will again lead twenty thousand foot and cavalry to take Xingshi upstream, and also descend to collect the remaining provisions at Dalei."
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month, Liu Hu deceived Yuan Yi, saying, "I will again lead twenty thousand foot and horse to take Xingshi upstream and also go downstream to gather the remaining stores at Dalei."

sentences.zh: 令顗悉度馬配之，其夜，委顗奔走，徑趣梅根。

translations.literal: He ordered Yi to assign all horses to Hu; that night he abandoned Yi and fled, heading straight for Meigan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yuan Yi to turn over every horse to him. That night he abandoned Yi and fled straight for Meigan.

sentences.zh: 先令薛常寶辦船舸，悉撥南陵諸軍，燒大雷諸城而走。

translations.literal: He had first ordered Xue Changbao to prepare boats and ships, fully redeployed the Nanling armies, burned the cities of Dalei, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He had already ordered Xue Changbao to ready the boats, pulled out every unit at Nanling, burned the towns at Dalei, and fled.

sentences.zh: 顗聞胡走，亦棄眾西奔，至青林見殺。

translations.literal: Yi heard that Hu had fled and also abandoned his masses and fled west; he reached Qinglin and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi heard that Liu Hu had fled, he too abandoned his army and fled west. He reached Qinglin and was killed.

sentences.zh: 胡率數百舸二萬人向尋陽，報子勛詐云：「袁顗已降，軍皆散，唯己率所領獨反。

translations.literal: Hu led several hundred boats and twenty thousand men toward Xunyang and reported falsely to Liu Zixun, saying: "Yuan Yi has already surrendered, the armies have all scattered, and only I have led my own command in rebellion alone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu led several hundred boats and twenty thousand men toward Xunyang and sent Liu Zixun a false report: "Yuan Yi has already surrendered, the armies have all dispersed, and only I have turned my own command against you.

sentences.zh: 宜速處分，為一戰之資，當停據盆城，誓死不貳。」

translations.literal: You ought to act quickly to make dispositions and prepare resources for a single decisive battle; halt and hold Pengcheng, swearing death without wavering in loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Act quickly to make arrangements for one last decisive battle—halt at Pengcheng and hold it to the death, with undivided loyalty."

sentences.zh: 乃於江外夜取沔口。

translations.literal: Then at night on the outer river he took Minkou.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on the river's outer reaches, he seized Minkou.

sentences.zh: 琬聞胡去，惶擾無復計，呼褚靈嗣等謀之，並不知所出，唯云更集兵力，加賞五階，或云三階者。

translations.literal: When Wan heard that Hu had gone, he was thrown into panic and could think of no plan; he summoned Chu Lingsi and the others to counsel together, but none knew what to do. Some said only to gather more troops and add rewards of five ranks, or of three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Wan heard that Liu Hu had fled, he panicked and could think of nothing. He summoned Chu Lingsi and the others to counsel, but none knew what to do. Some said only to gather more troops and raise rewards by five ranks—or by three.

sentences.zh: 張悅始發兄子浩喪，乃稱疾呼琬計事，令左右伏甲帳後，戒之：「若聞索酒，便出。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue had just begun mourning for the death of his elder brother's son Hao; he then feigned illness and summoned Wan to discuss affairs, had his attendants hide armed men behind the curtain, and instructed them: "If you hear me ask for wine, come out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue had just begun mourning for his nephew Hao. He then feigned illness and summoned Deng Wan to discuss affairs, had armed men hidden behind the curtain, and instructed them, "When you hear me call for wine, come out."

sentences.zh: 琬既至，悅曰：「卿首唱此謀，今事已急，計將安出？」

translations.literal: When Wan arrived, Yue said: "You were the first to launch this plot; now affairs are urgent—what plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wan arrived, Yue said, "You were the first to launch this plot. Affairs are urgent—what plan do you propose?"

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「正當斬晉安王，封府庫，以謝罪耳。」

translations.literal: Wan said: "The proper course is simply to behead the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and thus confess guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "The proper course is to behead the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and confess our guilt."

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「今日寧可賣殿下求活邪？」

translations.literal: Yue said: "Today could we sell His Highness to save our lives?
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Would we sell His Highness today to save our own lives?"

sentences.zh: 因呼求酒，再呼，左右震懾不能應。

translations.literal: He then called for wine; he called again, but his attendants, terrified, could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He then called for wine, and called again, but his attendants were too terrified to respond.

sentences.zh: 第二子洵提刀走出，餘人續至，即斬琬。

translations.literal: His second son Xun came out with a blade in hand; the others followed, and Wan was beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xun came out with a drawn blade; the others followed, and Deng Wan was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 琬死時，年六十。

translations.literal: When Wan died, he was sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was sixty when he died.

sentences.zh: 時中護軍劉順在座，驚起抱悅，左右人欲殺之，悅顧曰：「無關護軍。」

translations.literal: At that time Central Guard General Liu Shun was present; startled, he rose and embraced Yue. The attendants wanted to kill him, but Yue looked back and said: "This has nothing to do with the Protector General."
translations.idiomatic: Central Guard General Liu Shun was present. Startled, he rose and embraced Zhang Yue. The attendants wanted to kill him, but Yue said, "This has nothing to do with the Protector General."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They then stopped.

sentences.zh: 潘欣之聞琬死，勒兵而至，悅使人語之曰：「鄧琬謀反，即已梟戮。」

translations.literal: When Pan Xinzhi heard that Wan was dead, he led troops up; Yue sent a man to tell him: "Deng Wan plotted rebellion and has already been executed."
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Xinzhi heard that Deng Wan was dead, he led troops up. Yue sent a man to tell him, "Deng Wan plotted rebellion and has already been executed."

sentences.zh: 欣之乃回還，取琬兒並殺之。

translations.literal: Xinzhi then turned back, seized Wan's sons, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi then turned back, seized Deng Wan's sons, and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 悅因單舸齎琬首馳下，詣建安王休仁降。

translations.literal: Yue then, in a single boat carrying Wan's head, rushed downstream and went to the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue then took a single boat, carrying Deng Wan's head, rushed downstream, and surrendered to the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 蔡那子道淵，以父為太宗效力，被繫作部，因亂脫鏁入城，執子勛囚之。

translations.literal: Cai Na's son Daoyuan, because his father had served Emperor Ming, had been imprisoned as a corvée worker; amid the turmoil he broke his shackles, entered the city, seized Zixun, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Na's son Daoyuan, whose father had served Emperor Ming, had been imprisoned as a corvée laborer. Amid the turmoil he broke his shackles, entered the city, seized Liu Zixun, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之諸軍至江州，斬子勛於桑尾牙下，傳首京都。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's armies reached Jiang Province, they beheaded Zixun beneath the command flag at Sangwei and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's armies reached Jiang Province, they beheaded Liu Zixun beneath the command flag at Sangwei and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉順及餘同逆，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Liu Shun and the rest of the co-rebels were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shun and the other co-conspirators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 吳喜、張興世進向荊州，沈懷明向郢州，劉亮、張敬兒向雍州，孫超之向湘州，沈思仁、任農夫向豫章，所至皆平定。

translations.literal: Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi advanced toward Jing Province; Shen Huaiming toward Ying Province; Liu Liang and Zhang Jing'er toward Yong Province; Sun Chaozhi toward Xiang Province; Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu toward Yuzhang. Wherever they went, all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi and Zhang Xingshi advanced on Jing Province; Shen Huaiming on Ying Province; Liu Liang and Zhang Jing'er on Yong Province; Sun Chaozhi on Xiang Province; and Shen Siren and Ren Nongfu on Yuzhang. Everywhere they went was pacified.

sentences.zh: 劉胡走入沔，眾稍散，比至石城，裁餘數騎。

translations.literal: Liu Hu fled into the Mian region; his followers gradually scattered, and by the time he reached Shicheng he had barely a few horsemen left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu fled into the Han River region. His followers gradually scattered, and by the time he reached Shicheng he had barely a few horsemen left.

sentences.zh: 竟陵郡丞陳懷真，憲子也，聞胡經過，率數十人斷道邀之。

translations.literal: Chen Huaizhen, aide of Jingling commandery and son of Chen Xian, heard that Hu was passing through and led several dozen men to block the road and intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huaizhen, aide of Jingling commandery and son of Chen Xian, heard that Liu Hu was passing through and led several dozen men to block the road and intercept him.

sentences.zh: 胡人馬既疲，自度不免，因隨懷真入城，告渴，與之酒，胡飲酒畢，引佩刀自刺，不死，斬首送京邑。

translations.literal: Hu's men and horses were already exhausted; judging that he could not escape, he followed Huaizhen into the city, said he was thirsty, and was given wine. When Hu had finished drinking, he drew his sword and stabbed himself, but did not die; he was beheaded and his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu's men and horses were exhausted. Judging that he could not escape, he followed Chen Huaizhen into the city, said he was thirsty, and was given wine. When he had finished drinking, he drew his sword and stabbed himself but failed to die. He was then beheaded, and his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 張興世弟僧產追胡，未至石城數十里，逢送胡首信，將還竟陵，殺懷真，竊有其功。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi's younger brother Sengchan pursued Hu; before he had gone several tens of li from Shicheng, he met the messenger carrying Hu's head. As he was about to return to Jingling, he killed Huaizhen and stole the credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi's younger brother Sengchan was pursuing Liu Hu when, still several tens of li short of Shicheng, he met the messenger carrying Hu's head. On his way back to Jingling he killed Chen Huaizhen and stole the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 郢州行事張沈、偽竟陵太守丘景先聞敗，變形為沙門逃走，追擒伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhang Shen, acting governor of Ying Province, and Qiu Jingxian, the usurping governor of Jingling, heard of the defeat, disguised themselves as monks, and fled; they were pursued, captured, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shen, acting governor of Ying Province, and Qiu Jingxian, the rebel governor of Jingling, heard of the defeat, disguised themselves as monks, and fled. They were pursued, captured, and executed.

sentences.zh: 荊州聞濃湖平，議欲更遣軍與郢州合勢，又欲斷據巴陵，經日不決。

translations.literal: When Jing Province heard that Nonghu had been pacified, it debated whether to send more troops to join forces with Ying Province, and also whether to hold and cut off Baling; for days no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Province heard that Nonghu had been pacified, it debated sending more troops to join Ying Province and also whether to hold and cut off Baling. Days passed with no decision.

sentences.zh: 乃遣將趙道始於江津築壘，任演戍沙橋，諸門津要，皆有屯兵。

translations.literal: It then sent the general Zhao Daoshi to build a fort at Jiangjin, Ren Yan to garrison Shaqiao, and stationed troops at every pass and strategic crossing.
translations.idiomatic: It then sent the general Zhao Daoshi to build a fort at Jiangjin and Ren Yan to garrison Shaqiao. Troops were posted at every pass and strategic crossing.

sentences.zh: 人情轉離，將士漸逃散。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment turned away, and soldiers gradually fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Popular sentiment turned against them, and soldiers gradually deserted.

sentences.zh: 更議奉子頊奔益州，就蕭惠開，典籤阮道預、邵宰不同，曰：「近奉別詔，諸藩若改迷歸順者，悉復本爵。

translations.literal: They debated again escorting Zixu to Yi Province to join Xiao Huikai, but the chief clerks Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai disagreed, saying: "We have recently received a separate edict stating that all princely domains that reform their errors and return to allegiance shall have their original ranks fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: They debated again escorting Liu Zixu to Yi Province to join Xiao Huikai, but the chief clerks Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai disagreed. "We have recently received a separate edict," they said, "that all princely domains which reform their errors and return to allegiance shall have their original ranks fully restored.

sentences.zh: 且任叔兒已斷白帝，楊僧嗣據梁州，雖復欲西，豈可得至。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Ren Shuer has already cut off Baidi, and Yang Sengsi holds Liang Province; even if we wished to go west, how could we get there?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Ren Shuer has already cut off Baidi, and Yang Sengsi holds Liang Province. Even if we wished to go west, how could we get there?"

sentences.zh: 道預、邵宰即與劉道憲解遣白丁，遣使歸罪。

translations.literal: Daoyu and Shao Zai then, together with Liu Daoxian, dismissed the corvée laborers and sent envoys to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai then, together with Liu Daoxian, dismissed the corvée laborers and sent envoys to confess guilt.

sentences.zh: 荊州治中宗景、土人姚儉等勒兵入城，殺道憲、預、記室參軍鮑照，劫掠府庫，無復孑遺，執子頊以降。

translations.literal: Zong Jing, aide of Jing Province, and the local magnate Yao Jian and others led troops into the city, killed Daoxian and Yu, and the recorder Bao Zhao, looted the treasury until nothing remained, seized Zixu, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jing, aide of Jing Province, and the local magnate Yao Jian and others led troops into the city. They killed Liu Daoxian, Ruan Daoyu, and the recorder Bao Zhao, looted the treasury until nothing remained, seized Liu Zixu, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧琬徵兵巴東，巴東太守羅寶稱辭以郡接凶蠻，兵力不足分。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Deng Wan had summoned troops from Badong, the Governor of Badong, Luo Bao, pleaded as his excuse that the commandery bordered fierce barbarians and its forces were insufficient to divide.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Deng Wan had summoned troops from Badong, the Governor of Badong, Luo Bao, pleaded that the commandery bordered fierce barbarians and its forces were too few to spare.

sentences.zh: 巴東人任叔兒聚徒起義，遣信要寶稱，寶稱持疑未決，暴疾死。

translations.literal: Ren Shuer of Badong gathered followers and raised a revolt; he sent a message inviting Bao, but Bao hesitated and could not decide, then died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shuer of Badong gathered followers and rose in revolt. He sent a message inviting Luo Bao to join, but Bao hesitated and could not decide, then died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 叔兒乃自號輔國將軍，引兵據白帝，殺寶稱二子，阻守三陝。

translations.literal: Shuer then styled himself General Who Assists the State, led troops to hold Baidi, killed Bao's two sons, and blocked and defended the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shuer then styled himself General Who Assists the State, led troops to hold Baidi, killed Luo Bao's two sons, and blocked and defended the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開遣費欣壽等五千人攻叔兒，叔兒與戰，大破之，斬欣壽。

translations.literal: Xiao Huikai sent Fei Xinshou and five thousand men to attack Shuer; Shuer fought them, routed them completely, and beheaded Xinshou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Huikai sent Fei Xinshou with five thousand men to attack Ren Shuer. Shuer fought them, routed them completely, and beheaded Xinshou.

sentences.zh: 子頊又遣中兵參軍何康之領宜都太守，討叔兒。

translations.literal: Zixu also sent the army office officer He Kangzhi, acting as Governor of Yidu, to suppress Shuer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixu also sent the army office officer He Kangzhi, acting as Governor of Yidu, to suppress Ren Shuer.

sentences.zh: 軍至陝口，為夷帥向子通所破，挺身走還。

translations.literal: When the army reached Shanjing Pass, it was defeated by the barbarian chief Xiang Zitong; Kangzhi fled back alone.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Shanjing Pass, it was defeated by the barbarian chief Xiang Zitong. He Kangzhi fled back alone.

sentences.zh: 叔兒遂固白帝。

translations.literal: Shuer then firmly held Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shuer then firmly held Baidi.

sentences.zh: 孔道存知尋陽已平，遣使歸順。

translations.literal: When Kong Daocun learned that Xunyang had been pacified, he sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Daocun learned that Xunyang had been pacified, he sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 尋聞柳世隆、劉亮當至，眾悉奔逃，道存及三子同時自殺。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he heard that Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were about to arrive; the masses all fled in panic. Daocun and his three sons all committed suicide at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he heard that Liu Shilong and Liu Liang were about to arrive. The people all fled in panic. Kong Daocun and his three sons committed suicide together.

sentences.zh: 何慧文始謀同逆，其母禁之不從，母乃攜女歸江陵，遽嫁之。

translations.literal: He Huiwen had at first plotted to join the rebellion; his mother forbade him, but he would not listen. His mother then took her daughter back to Jiangling and hastily married her off.
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen had at first plotted to join the rebellion. His mother forbade him, but he would not listen. She then took her daughter back to Jiangling and hastily married her off.

sentences.zh: 慧文才兼將吏，幹略有施，雖害王應之，上特加原宥，吳喜宣旨赦之。

translations.literal: Huiwen combined the talents of general and official and had ability in planning and execution. Though he had killed Wang Yingzhi, the emperor specially pardoned him, and Wu Xi announced the decree of amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen combined the talents of a general and an official and had real ability in planning and execution. Though he had killed Wang Yingzhi, the emperor specially pardoned him, and Wu Xi announced the decree of amnesty.

sentences.zh: 慧文曰：「既陷逆節，手害忠義，天網雖復恢恢，何面目以見天下之士。」

translations.literal: Huiwen said: "Having fallen into rebellion and with my own hand killed the loyal, though heaven's net is vast, with what face could I meet the men of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: He Huiwen said, "Having fallen into rebellion and killed the loyal with my own hand—though heaven's net is vast, with what face could I meet the men of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 和藥將飲，門生覆之，乃不食而死。

translations.literal: He mixed poison and was about to drink it, but his disciples overturned the cup; he then starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: He mixed poison and was about to drink it, but his disciples overturned the cup. He then starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 顏躍慮虞洽還都，說其始時同逆，密使人殺之。

translations.literal: Yan Yue feared that when Yu Qia returned to the capital he would speak of how Yan had initially joined the rebellion, and secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yue feared that when Yu Qia returned to the capital he would reveal how Yan had initially joined the rebellion, and secretly sent men to kill him.

sentences.zh: 初，淮南定陵人賈襲宗本縣已為劉胡所得，率二十人投沈攸之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jia Xizong of Dingling in Huainan—his home commandery had already been taken by Liu Hu—led twenty men to join Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jia Xizong of Dingling in Huainan—his home commandery had already been taken by Liu Hu—led twenty men to join Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之言之建安王休仁，休仁版為司徒參軍督護，使還鄉里招集，為胡所禽，以火炙之，問臺軍消息，一無所言，瞋目謂胡曰：「君稱兵內侮，窺覦神器，未聞奇謀遠略，而為炮烙之刑。

translations.literal: Youzhi spoke of him to the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren; Xiuren commissioned him as Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses and Supervisor, and sent him back to his home district to recruit men. He was captured by Hu, who roasted him with fire and questioned him about the imperial armies, but he said not a word. Glaring at Hu, he said: "You raised troops and insulted the court within, coveting the imperial throne; I have not heard of any clever plan or far-reaching strategy from you, yet you use roasting torture.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi spoke of him to the Prince of Jian'an, Liu Xiuren, who commissioned him as Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses and Supervisor and sent him back to his home district to recruit men. Liu Hu captured him, roasted him with fire, and questioned him about the imperial armies, but he said not a word. Glaring at Hu, he said, "You raised troops against the court and covet the throne. I have heard no clever plan or far-reaching strategy from you, yet you use roasting torture.

sentences.zh: 僕本以身奉義，死亦何有。」

translations.literal: I originally devoted my body to righteousness—what is death to me?"
translations.idiomatic: I devoted my body to righteousness from the start—what is death to me?"

sentences.zh: 胡乃斬之。

translations.literal: Hu then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 前軍典籤範道興志不同逆，為琬所誅，其餘奉順見害者，並為上所愍。

translations.literal: The forward army chief clerk Fan Daoxing's will was not the same as the rebellion; he was executed by Wan. The rest who obeyed the court and were harmed were all pitied by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The forward army chief clerk Fan Daoxing had refused to join the rebellion and was executed by Deng Wan. The others who had remained loyal and were harmed were all pitied by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「前鎮軍參軍督護范道興，朕之舊隸，經從北藩，徒役南畿，遭離命會，抱恩固節，受害群凶，言念純誠，良有憫愴。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Fan Daoxing, former Staff Officer and Supervisor of the Forward Army, was my old attendant. He followed me on the northern frontier and served in corvée in the southern capital region; encountering this crisis of fate, he held fast to gratitude and fixed loyalty, and was harmed by the rebels. When I think of his pure sincerity, I am deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Fan Daoxing, former Staff Officer and Supervisor of the Forward Army, was my old attendant. He followed me on the northern frontier and served in corvée in the southern capital region. Encountering this crisis of fate, he held fast to gratitude and steadfast loyalty and was killed by the rebels. When I think of his pure sincerity, I am deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 可贈員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously granted Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 南城令鮑法度、後軍典籤馮次民、永新令應生、新建令庫延寶、上饒令黃難等，違逆識順，同被誅滅，言念既往，宜在追榮。

translations.literal: Bao Fadu, Magistrate of Nancheng; Feng Cimin, chief clerk of the Rear Army; Ying Sheng, Magistrate of Yongxin; Ku Yanbao, Magistrate of Xinjian; and Huang Nan, Magistrate of Shangrao—all recognized the rebellion for what it was, obeyed the right course, and were executed together. When I think of what they did, they deserve posthumous honor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fadu, Magistrate of Nancheng; Feng Cimin, chief clerk of the Rear Army; Ying Sheng, Magistrate of Yongxin; Ku Yanbao, Magistrate of Xinjian; and Huang Nan, Magistrate of Shangrao—all recognized the rebellion for what it was, held to the right course, and were executed together. When I think of what they did, they deserve posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 可贈生奉朝請，法度南臺御史，次民、延寶、難並員外將軍。」

translations.literal: Sheng may be granted Gentleman at Court Attendance; Fadu, Censor of the Southern Office; and Cimin, Yanbao, and Nan may all be granted Supernumerary Generals."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Sheng is granted Gentleman at Court Attendance; Bao Fadu, Censor of the Southern Office; and Feng Cimin, Ku Yanbao, and Huang Nan are all granted Supernumerary Generals."

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「寧朔將軍、督豫州之梁郡諸軍事、豫州刺史、領南梁郡太守竟陵張興世，都統水軍，屢戰克捷，仍進斷賊上流錢溪，貴口苦戰，平定凶逆，今封南平郡作唐縣開國侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized: "Zhang Xingshi of Jingling, General Who Pacifies the North, Commander of all military affairs in Liang commandery of Yu Province, Inspector of Yu Province, and Administrator of Nanliang commandery, commanded the navy as a whole, repeatedly fought and won victories, then advanced to cut off the rebels' upstream position at Qianxi, fought bitterly at Guikou, and pacified the rebellion. He is now enfeoffed as Marquis of Tang in Nanping commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office memorialized: "Zhang Xingshi of Jingling, General Who Pacifies the North, Commander of all military affairs in Liang commandery of Yu Province, Inspector of Yu Province, and Administrator of Nanliang commandery, commanded the navy as a whole, won repeated victories, then advanced to cut off the rebels' upstream position at Qianxi, fought bitterly at Guikou, and pacified the rebellion. He is now enfeoffed as Marquis of Tang in Nanping commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、參司徒中直兵軍事廣平佼長生，同統水軍屢戰，及興世上據錢溪，長生獨距賊衝要，功次興世，今封武陵郡遷陵縣開國侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Jiao Changsheng of Guangping, General Who Pacifies the North and staff officer of the Direct Army of the Minister over the Masses, likewise commanded the navy in repeated battles; when Xingshi advanced to hold Qianxi, Changsheng alone blocked the rebels' critical point. His merit was second to Xingshi's. He is now enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianling in Wuling commandery, with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Changsheng of Guangping, General Who Pacifies the North and staff officer of the Direct Army of the Minister over the Masses, likewise commanded the navy in repeated battles. When Xingshi advanced to hold Qianxi, Changsheng alone blocked the rebels' critical point. His merit was second only to Xingshi's. He is now enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianling in Wuling commandery, with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍、試守西陽太守吳興全景文、尚書比部郎吳縣孫超之、假輔國將軍、右衛將軍南彭城劉亮等三人，並經晉陵苦戰，景文、超之仍又北討破釜，水軍斷賊糧運，及經葛塚、石梁二處破賊，亮南伐經大戰，又最處險劇。

translations.literal: Quan Jingwen of Wuxing, acting Governor of Xiyang; Sun Chaozhi of Wu county, Director of the Ministry of Justice; and Liu Liang of Nan Pengcheng, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Right Guard—these three all fought bitterly at Jinling. Jingwen and Chaozhi also marched north and broke the rebels at Potou; the navy cut the rebels' grain transport, and at Gezhong and Shiliang they again defeated the rebels. Liang marched south and fought great battles, and was in the most perilous and arduous positions.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingwen of Wuxing, acting Governor of Xiyang; Sun Chaozhi of Wu county, Director of the Ministry of Justice; and Liu Liang of Nan Pengcheng, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Right Guard—these three all fought bitterly at Jinling. Jingwen and Chaozhi also marched north and broke the rebels at Potou; the navy cut the rebels' grain transport, and at Gezhong and Shiliang they again defeated the rebels. Liang marched south and fought great battles in the most perilous and arduous positions.

sentences.zh: 景文今封西陽郡孝寧縣，超之封長沙郡羅縣，亮封順陽縣，並開國侯，食邑各六百戶。

translations.literal: Jingwen is now enfeoffed in Xiaoning county of Xiyang commandery; Chaozhi in Luoxian of Changsha commandery; and Liang in Shunyang county—all as marquises, each with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen is now enfeoffed in Xiaoning county of Xiyang commandery; Chaozhi in Luoxian of Changsha commandery; and Liang in Shunyang county—all as marquises, each with a fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、驃騎司馬劉靈遺、寧朔將軍、右軍蔡那、寧朔將軍、屯騎校尉段佛榮等三人，統治攻道，並經苦戰，靈遺今封新野郡新野縣，那封始平郡平陽縣，佛榮封湘東郡臨蒸縣，並開國伯，食邑各五百戶。

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi, acting General Who Assists the State and Marshal of the Flying Cavalry; Cai Na, General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry; and Duan Furong, General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry—these three commanded the assault routes and all fought bitter battles. Lingyi is now enfeoffed in Xinye county of Xinye commandery; Na in Pingyang county of Shiping commandery; and Furong in Linzheng county of Xiangdong commandery—all as earls, each with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi, acting General Who Assists the State and Marshal of the Flying Cavalry; Cai Na, General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry; and Duan Furong, General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry—these three commanded the assault routes and all fought bitter battles. Lingyi is now enfeoffed in Xinye county of Xinye commandery; Na in Pingyang county of Shiping commandery; and Furong in Linzheng county of Xiangdong commandery—all as earls, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、左軍吳興沈懷明、龍驤將軍、積射將軍東平周盤龍、司徒參軍南彭城李安民等三人，懷明經晉陵破賊，又水軍南伐，統治攻道，盤龍雖不統軍，並經大戰，先登陷陳，安民又隨張興世遏斷錢溪，別統軍貴口破賊，今封懷明建安郡吳興縣，盤龍封晉安郡晉安縣，安民封建安郡邵武縣，並開國子，食邑各四百戶。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Left; Zhou Panlong of Dongping, General of the Flying Dragon and General of the Rapid-shooting Archers; and Li Anmin of Nan Pengcheng, Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses—these three: Huaiming fought through Jinling and defeated the rebels, then led the navy south in punitive campaign and commanded the assault routes; though Panlong did not command an army as a whole, he fought in great battles and was first to scale the walls and break the enemy lines; Anmin also followed Zhang Xingshi in blocking and cutting off Qianxi, and separately commanded an army that defeated the rebels at Guikou. Huaiming is now enfeoffed in Wuxing county of Jian'an commandery; Panlong in Jin'an county of Jin'an commandery; and Anmin in Shaowu county of Jian'an commandery—all as viscounts, each with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming of Wuxing, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Left; Zhou Panlong of Dongping, General of the Flying Dragon and General of the Rapid-shooting Archers; and Li Anmin of Nan Pengcheng, Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses—these three: Huaiming fought through Jinling and defeated the rebels, then led the navy south and commanded the assault routes; though Panlong did not command an army as a whole, he fought in great battles and was first to scale the walls and break the enemy lines; Anmin also followed Zhang Xingshi in blocking and cutting off Qianxi, and separately commanded an army that defeated the rebels at Guikou. Huaiming is now enfeoffed in Wuxing county of Jian'an commandery; Panlong in Jin'an county of Jin'an commandery; and Anmin in Shaowu county of Jian'an commandery—all as viscounts, each with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 假輔國將軍、游擊將軍彭城杜幼文、龍驤將軍、羽林監太原王穆之、龍驤將軍、羽林監濟北頓生、龍驤將軍、羽林監沛郡周普孫、員外散騎侍郎朱重恩等五人，幼文經晉陵破賊，在軍統攻道，南伐濃湖，普孫副沈攸之都統眾軍，穆之、生、重恩並南伐有功。

translations.literal: Du Youwen of Pengcheng, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Mobile Corps; Wang Muzhi of Taiyuan, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; Dun Sheng of Jibei, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; Zhou Pusun of Pei commandery, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; and Zhu Chong'en, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry—these five: Youwen fought through Jinling and defeated the rebels and commanded the assault routes on the southern campaign to Nonghu; Pusun served as deputy to Shen Youzhi in commanding all the armies; Muzhi, Sheng, and Chong'en all had merit on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Du Youwen of Pengcheng, acting General Who Assists the State and General of the Mobile Corps; Wang Muzhi of Taiyuan, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; Dun Sheng of Jibei, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; Zhou Pusun of Pei commandery, General of the Flying Dragon and Superintendent of the Feathered Forest; and Zhu Chong'en, Supernumerary Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry—these five: Youwen fought through Jinling and defeated the rebels and commanded the assault routes on the southern campaign to Nonghu; Pusun served as deputy to Shen Youzhi in commanding all the armies; Muzhi, Sheng, and Chong'en all had merit on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 今封幼文邵陵郡邵陽縣，穆之封衡陽郡衡山縣，生封始平郡武功縣，普孫封順陽郡清水縣，重恩封南海郡龍川縣，並開國男，食邑各三百戶。」

translations.literal: Youwen is now enfeoffed in Shaoyang county of Shaoling commandery; Muzhi in Hengshan county of Hengyang commandery; Sheng in Wugong county of Shiping commandery; Pusun in Qingshui county of Shunyang commandery; and Chong'en in Longchuan county of Nanhai commandery—all as barons, each with a fief of three hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Youwen is now enfeoffed in Shaoyang county of Shaoling commandery; Muzhi in Hengshan county of Hengyang commandery; Sheng in Wugong county of Shiping commandery; Pusun in Qingshui county of Shunyang commandery; and Chong'en in Longchuan county of Nanhai commandery—all as barons, each with a fief of three hundred households."

sentences.zh: 江方興以戰功為太子左衛率，賊未平，病卒，追封武當縣侯，食邑五百戶。
