translations.literal: Jiang Fangxing was made Left Guard of the Heir Apparent for his military merit; before the rebels were fully pacified, he died of illness. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wudang, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fangxing was made Left Guard of the Heir Apparent for his military merit. Before the rebels were fully pacified, he died of illness. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wudang, with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 方興，濟陽考城人，衣冠之舊也。

translations.literal: Fangxing was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang and came from an old official family.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fangxing was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang and came from an old official family.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍、虎賁中郎將董凱之，隨張興世破胡、白城，先登，封河隆縣子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Dong Kaizhi, General of the Flying Dragon and Central Rapid Tiger General, followed Zhang Xingshi in defeating Hu at Baicheng, was first to scale the walls, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Helong, with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Kaizhi, General of the Flying Dragon and Central Rapid Tiger General, followed Zhang Xingshi in defeating Liu Hu at Baicheng, was first to scale the walls, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Helong, with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 軍主張靈符，東南征討有功，封上饒縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Army commander Zhang Lingfu had merit in the southeastern punitive campaign and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shangrao, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Zhang Lingfu had merit in the southeastern punitive campaign and was enfeoffed as Baron of Shangrao, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 前征北長兼行參軍楊覆，以貴口有功，封綏城縣男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, former acting Forward Army staff officer, had merit at Guikou and was enfeoffed as Baron of Suicheng, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, former acting Forward Army staff officer, had merit at Guikou and was enfeoffed as Baron of Suicheng, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 追贈虞洽、檀玢給事中。

translations.literal: Yu Qia and Tan Bin were posthumously granted Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qia and Tan Bin were posthumously granted Attendants.

sentences.zh: 以李萬周為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Li Wanzhou was made Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanzhou was made Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 陳懷真以斬劉胡功，追封永豐縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Chen Huaizhen, for the merit of beheading Liu Hu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Yongfeng, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huaizhen, for the merit of beheading Liu Hu, was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Yongfeng, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 段佛榮

translations.literal: Duan Furong
translations.idiomatic: Duan Furong

sentences.zh: 段佛榮，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Duan Furong was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Furong was a man of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，自游擊將軍為輔師將軍、豫州刺史，蒞任清謹，為西土所安。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, he was made General Who Assists the Army and Inspector of Yu Province from General of the Mobile Corps; his administration was pure and careful, and the western regions were reassured by him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi, he was promoted from General of the Mobile Corps to General Who Assists the Army and Inspector of Yu Province. His administration was pure and careful, and the western regions were reassured by him.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，徵為散騎常侍，領長水校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui of the deposed emperor, he was summoned to be Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui under the deposed emperor, he was summoned to serve as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry and Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷衛尉，領右軍將軍，未拜，復出為冠軍將軍、南豫州刺史、歷陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of the Guard and General of the Right, but before he received the appointment he was again sent out as General Who Conquers the Enemy, Inspector of Southern Yu Province, and Governor of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Minister of the Guard and General of the Right, but before he received the appointment he was again sent out as General Who Conquers the Enemy, Inspector of Southern Yu Province, and Governor of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，追贈前將軍，改封雲杜縣，諡曰烈侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; he was posthumously granted General of the Front and his fief was changed to Yun Du county. His posthumous title was Marquis Lie.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died. He was posthumously granted General of the Front and his fief was changed to Yun Du county. His posthumous title was Marquis Lie.

sentences.zh: 劉靈遺

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi

sentences.zh: 劉靈遺，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Lingyi was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingyi was a man of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 元徽元年，自輔師將軍、淮南太守，為南豫州刺史、歷陽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhui, he was made Inspector of Southern Yu Province and Governor of Liyang from General Who Assists the Army and Governor of Huainan, retaining his generalship.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui, he was promoted from General Who Assists the Army and Governor of Huainan to Inspector of Southern Yu Province and Governor of Liyang, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵為散騎常侍，領步兵校尉、南蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned to be Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and Governor of Nanlanling.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned to serve as Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and Governor of Nanlanling.

sentences.zh: 病卒，諡曰壯侯。

translations.literal: He died of illness; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness. His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 袁顗，字景章，陳郡陽夏人，太尉淑兄子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi, courtesy name Jingzhang, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery and the son of the Grand Commandant Shu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, courtesy name Jingzhang, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery and the nephew of Grand Commandant Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 父洵，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Xun was Governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Xun was Governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 顗初為豫州主簿，舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: Yi at first served as chief clerk of Yu Province, was nominated as Outstanding Talent, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi at first served as chief clerk of Yu Province and was nominated as Outstanding Talent, but declined.

sentences.zh: 後補始興王濬後軍行參軍，著作佐郎，廬陵王紹南中郎主簿，世祖征虜、撫軍主簿，廬江太守，尚書都官郎，江夏王義恭驃騎記室參軍，汝陰王文學，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He was later appointed acting Rear Army staff officer to Prince Jun of Shixing, Assistant Director of the Palace Library, chief clerk to Prince Shao of Luling, staff officer to the Heir Apparent's Pacification and Pacification of the Barbarians offices under Emperor Xiaowu, Governor of Lujiang, Director of the Ministry of Punishments, recorder to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, literary aide to Prince Wen of Runan, and Groom of the Heir Apparent's Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed acting Rear Army staff officer to Prince Jun of Shixing, Assistant Director of the Palace Library, chief clerk to Prince Shao of Luling, staff officer to Emperor Xiaowu's Pacification and Pacification of the Barbarians offices, Governor of Lujiang, Director of the Ministry of Punishments, recorder to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, literary aide to Prince Wen of Runan, and Groom of the Heir Apparent's Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 時顗父為吳郡，顗隨父在官。

translations.literal: At that time Yi's father was Governor of Wu commandery, and Yi followed his father in office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Yi's father was Governor of Wu commandery, and Yi followed his father in office.

sentences.zh: 值元兇弑立，安東將軍隨王誕舉兵入討，板顗為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the assassin prince seized the throne, General Who Pacifies the East Prince Dan of Sui raised troops to punish him; Yi was commissioned as Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassin prince seized the throne, Prince Dan of Sui, General Who Pacifies the East, raised troops to punish him. Yuan Yi was commissioned as Adviser.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除正員郎，晉陵太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was appointed Regular Gentleman and Governor of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were settled, he was appointed Regular Gentleman and Governor of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，服闋，為中書侍郎，又除晉陵太守，襲南昌縣五等子。

translations.literal: Upon the death of his father, after the mourning period ended he was made Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and again appointed Governor of Jinling, inheriting the fifth-rank viscountcy of Nanchang county.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death, when the mourning period ended he was made Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and again appointed Governor of Jinling, inheriting the fifth-rank viscountcy of Nanchang county.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，除東海王禕平南司馬、尋陽太守，行江州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he was appointed Pacification Marshal to Prince Yi of Donghai and Governor of Xunyang, acting for the affairs of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming, he was appointed Pacification Marshal to Prince Yi of Donghai and Governor of Xunyang, acting for the affairs of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 復為義陽王昶前軍司馬，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Forward Army Marshal to Prince Chang of Yiyang, retaining his governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Forward Army Marshal to Prince Chang of Yiyang, retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 昶尋罷府，司馬職解，加寧朔將軍，改太守為內史。

translations.literal: When Chang's princely establishment was abolished, his marshal's post was dissolved; he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North and his governorship was changed to an interior ministership.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chang's princely establishment was abolished, his marshal's post was dissolved. He was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North and his governorship was changed to an interior ministership.

sentences.zh: 復為尋陽王子房冠軍司馬，將軍如故，行淮南、宣城二郡事。

translations.literal: He was again made Champion Army Marshal to Prince Fang of Xunyang, retaining his generalship, and acted for the affairs of Huainan and Xuancheng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Champion Army Marshal to Prince Fang of Xunyang, retaining his generalship, and acted for the affairs of Huainan and Xuancheng commanderies.

sentences.zh: 五年，召為太子中庶子，御史中丞，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to be Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Censor-in-Chief, and also held the chief assessor's post for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned to serve as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Censor-in-Chief, and also held the chief assessor's post for his native province.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷侍中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，除晉安王子勛鎮軍長史、襄陽太守，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Chief of Staff to Prince Xun of Jin'an and Governor of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Chief of Staff to Prince Xun of Jin'an and Governor of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 未行，復為永嘉王子仁左軍長史、廣陵太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he was again made Left Army Chief of Staff to Prince Ren of Yongjia and Governor of Guangling, retaining his generalship.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, he was again made Left Army Chief of Staff to Prince Ren of Yongjia and Governor of Guangling, retaining his generalship.

sentences.zh: 未拜，復為侍中，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before he received the appointment, he was again made Palace Attendant and General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he received the appointment, he was again made Palace Attendant and General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 大明末，新安王子鸞以母嬖有盛寵，太子在東宮多過失，上微有廢太子立子鸞之意，從容頗言之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era, Prince Luan of Xin'an, because his mother was a favored consort enjoying great favor, and because the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace had many faults, the emperor subtly revealed an intention to depose the Crown Prince and establish Luan in his place, and in relaxed conversation spoke of this somewhat openly.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era, Prince Luan of Xin'an, because his mother was a favored consort who enjoyed great favor, and because the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace had many faults, the emperor subtly revealed an intention to depose the Crown Prince and establish Luan in his place, and in relaxed conversation spoke of this somewhat openly.

sentences.zh: 顗盛稱太子好學，有日新之美。

translations.literal: Yi greatly praised the Crown Prince's love of learning and his daily renewal in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi greatly praised the Crown Prince's love of learning and his daily renewal in virtue.

sentences.zh: 世祖又以沈慶之才用不多，言論頗相蚩毀，顗又陳慶之忠勤有幹略，堪當重任。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu also held that Shen Qingzhi lacked much talent and spoke with considerable ridicule and disparagement; Yi again declared that Qingzhi was loyal, diligent, and possessed of strategic ability, fit to bear heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu also dismissed Shen Qingzhi as a man of limited talent and spoke of him with open ridicule. Yuan Yi countered by praising Qingzhi's loyalty, diligence, and strategic ability as qualities fit for weighty command.

sentences.zh: 由是前廢帝深感顗，慶之亦懷其德。

translations.literal: Because of this the Former Deposed Emperor deeply valued Yi, and Qingzhi also cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Former Deposed Emperor came to hold Yuan Yi in deep regard, and Qingzhi too was grateful for his kindness.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，誅群公，欲引進顗，任以朝政，遷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe, after executing the senior officials, he wished to promote Yi and entrust him with state affairs, and transferred him to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe, after executing the senior officials, the emperor wished to promote Yuan Yi and entrust him with state affairs, appointing him Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 又下詔曰：「宗社多故，釁因冢司，景命未淪，神祚再乂，自非忠謀密契，豈伊克殄。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict saying: "The altars of state have suffered many calamities, the outbreak coming from the chief minister; yet the Mandate has not fallen, and divine favor has been restored—without loyal counsel in secret concert, how could it have been extinguished?
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an edict proclaiming: "The altars of state have suffered many calamities, the outbreak springing from the chief minister; yet the Mandate has not fallen, and divine favor has been restored. Without loyal counsel in secret concert, how could the evil have been extinguished?

sentences.zh: 侍中祭酒、領前軍將軍、新除吏部尚書顗，游擊將軍、領著作郎、兼尚書左丞徐爰，誠心內款，參聞嘉策，匡贊之效，寔監朕懷。

translations.literal: Yi, Grand Preceptor of the Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of the Vanguard Army, and newly appointed Minister of Personnel, and Xu Ai, General of Mobile Attack, Director of the Compilation Bureau, and concurrent Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat, have offered sincere allegiance from within and shared in excellent plans; their aid in setting things right rests ever before Our mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, Grand Preceptor of the Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of the Vanguard Army, and newly appointed Minister of Personnel, and Xu Ai, General of Mobile Attack, Director of the Compilation Bureau, and concurrent Left Assistant Director in the Secretariat, have offered sincere allegiance from the heart and shared in excellent plans. Their aid in setting things right rests ever before Our mind.

sentences.zh: 宜甄茅社，以獎義槩。

translations.literal: They should be granted feudal enfeoffment to reward righteous resolve.
translations.idiomatic: They should be granted feudal enfeoffment to reward their righteous resolve.

sentences.zh: 顗可封新隆縣子，爰可封吳平縣子，食邑各五百戶。」

translations.literal: Yi may be enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinlong and Ai as Viscount of Wuping, each with a fief of five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi is to be enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinlong and Xu Ai as Viscount of Wuping, each with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 俄而意趣乖異，寵待頓衰。

translations.literal: Before long their aims diverged, and imperial favor abruptly waned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long their aims diverged, and imperial favor abruptly waned.

sentences.zh: 始令顗與沈慶之、徐爰參知選事，尋復反以為罪，使有司糾奏，坐白衣領職。

translations.literal: At first Yi was ordered to assist Shen Qingzhi and Xu Ai in personnel matters, but soon he was charged on the contrary with offense; the relevant offices were made to impeach him, and he was demoted to commoner status while retaining his post.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yuan Yi was ordered to assist Shen Qingzhi and Xu Ai in personnel matters, but soon he was charged with offense on the contrary. The relevant offices were made to impeach him, and he was stripped of rank while retaining his post.

sentences.zh: 從幸湖熟，往反數日，不被喚召。

translations.literal: On an imperial visit to Hushu, he went back and forth for several days without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to Hushu, he went back and forth for several days without being summoned.

sentences.zh: 顗慮及禍，詭辭求出，沈慶之為顗固陳，乃見許。

translations.literal: Yi, fearing disaster, pleaded under pretext to leave the capital; Shen Qingzhi strongly interceded for Yi, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, fearing disaster, pleaded under pretext to leave the capital. Shen Qingzhi strongly interceded for him, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 除建安王休仁安西長史、襄陽太守，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Administrator to Prince Xiuren of Jian'an in the Army of the West and Governor of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Administrator to Prince Xiuren of Jian'an in the Army of the West and Governor of Xiangyang, with the additional rank of Champion General.

sentences.zh: 休仁不行，即以顗為使持節、督雍、梁、南北秦四州、郢州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、領寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: As Xiuren did not take up the post, Yi was appointed directly as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Liang, South Qin, and North Qin and in the commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Ying Province, Commander Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong Province, retaining his general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiuren did not take up the post, Yuan Yi was appointed directly as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Liang, South Qin, and North Qin and in the commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Ying Province, Commander Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yong Province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 顗舅蔡興宗謂之曰：「襄陽星惡，豈可冒邪？」

translations.literal: Yi's uncle Cai Xingzong said to him: "The stars over Xiangyang are ill-omened—how can you take such a risk?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi's uncle Cai Xingzong said to him: "The stars over Xiangyang are ill-omened—how can you take such a risk?

sentences.zh: 顗曰：「白刃交前，不救流矢，事有緩急故也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "When bright blades cross before one's face, one does not parry a stray arrow—because matters have their moments of urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi replied: "When bright blades cross before one's face, one does not parry a stray arrow—because matters have their moments of urgency.

sentences.zh: 今者之行，本願生出虎口。

translations.literal: My journey now springs from the wish to escape the tiger's maw alive.
translations.idiomatic: My journey now springs from the wish to escape the tiger's maw alive.

sentences.zh: 且天道遼遠，何必皆驗，如其有徵，當脩德以禳之耳。」

translations.literal: Besides, the Way of Heaven is vast and remote—why must every sign come true? If there is indeed a portent, one need only cultivate virtue to avert it."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Way of Heaven is vast and remote—why must every sign come true? If there is indeed a portent, one need only cultivate virtue to avert it."

sentences.zh: 於是狼狽上路，恆慮見追，行至尋陽，喜曰：「今始免矣！」

translations.literal: Thus he set out in disarray, constantly fearing pursuit. When he reached Xunyang, he rejoiced: "At last I am safe!"
translations.idiomatic: Thus he set out in disarray, constantly fearing pursuit. When he reached Xunyang, he rejoiced: "At last I am safe!

sentences.zh: 與鄧琬款狎相過，常請間，必盡日窮夜。

translations.literal: He grew intimate with Deng Wan, often requesting private meetings that lasted from dawn till the depths of night.
translations.idiomatic: He grew intimate with Deng Wan, often requesting private meetings that lasted from dawn till the depths of night.

sentences.zh: 顗與琬人地本殊，眾知其有異志矣。

translations.literal: Yi and Wan came from utterly different stations in life; the world knew they harbored separate designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi and Wan came from utterly different stations in life, and the world knew they harbored separate designs.

sentences.zh: 太宗使朝士與顗書曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had court officials write to Yi, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had court officials write to Yuan Yi, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫夷陂相因，興革遞數，或多難而固其國，或殷憂而啟聖明，此既著於前史，亦彰於聞見。

translations.literal: Plains and marshes succeed one another; rise and reform follow in turn. Some states are strengthened through many tribulations, some sage rulers are awakened through deep sorrow—this is recorded in history and plain to all who have lived to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Plains and marshes succeed one another; rise and reform follow in turn. Some states are strengthened through many tribulations, some sage rulers are awakened through deep sorrow—this is recorded in history and plain to all who have lived to see it.

sentences.zh: 王室不造，昏凶肆虐，神鼎將淪，宗稷幾泯，幸天未亡宋，乾曆有歸。

translations.literal: The royal house had fallen on evil times; the benighted and cruel ran rampant. The sacred vessel was nearly lost, the altars of state all but extinguished—yet fortunately Heaven had not abandoned Song, and the Mandate found its bearer.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house had fallen on evil times; the benighted and cruel ran rampant. The sacred vessel was nearly lost, the altars of state all but extinguished—yet fortunately Heaven had not abandoned Song, and the Mandate found its bearer.

sentences.zh: 主上體自聖文，繼明作睿，而辱均牖里，屯逾夏臺。

translations.literal: Our sovereign is endowed with sacred brilliance, succeeding to enlightenment and wisdom, yet he suffered shame equal to imprisonment at Youli, hardships surpassing confinement on Mount Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is endowed with sacred brilliance, succeeding to enlightenment and wisdom, yet he suffered shame equal to imprisonment at Youli and hardships surpassing confinement on Mount Xia.

sentences.zh: 既天地俱憤，義勇同奮，克殄鯨鯢，三靈更造，應天順民，爰集寶命，四海屬息肩之歡，華戎見來蘇之泰。

translations.literal: When heaven and earth alike seethed with outrage, the righteous rose as one, destroyed the sea monsters, and the Three Powers were remade. Fitting heaven and following the people's will, the precious Mandate was gathered in. Within the four seas came the joy of resting one's shoulders; among all the peoples, Chinese and barbarian, came the peace of revival.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven and earth alike seethed with outrage, the righteous rose as one, destroyed the sea monsters, and the Three Powers were remade. Fitting heaven and following the people's will, the precious Mandate was gathered in. Within the four seas came the joy of resting one's shoulders; among all the peoples, Chinese and barbarian, came the peace of revival.

sentences.zh: 吾等獲免刀鋸，僅全首領，復身奉惟新，命承亨運，緩帶談笑，擊壤聖世。

translations.literal: We were spared the sword and saw, our heads barely preserved; we again serve the newly renewed order, our fates joined to a flourishing age—loosening our belts, laughing in ease, playing at earth-beating in a sage reign.
translations.idiomatic: We were spared the sword and saw, our heads barely preserved. We again serve the newly renewed order, our fates joined to a flourishing age—loosening our belts, laughing in ease, playing at earth-beating in a sage reign.

sentences.zh: 汝雖劬勞於外，跡阻京師，然心期所寄，江、漢何遠。

translations.literal: Though you toil abroad and your path to the capital is blocked, the heart's pledge you hold is near—how far, after all, are the Yangzi and the Han?
translations.idiomatic: Though you toil abroad and your path to the capital is blocked, the heart's pledge you hold is near—how far, after all, are the Yangzi and the Han?

sentences.zh: 自九江告變，皆謂鄧氏狂惑，比日國言藉藉，頗塵吾子。

translations.literal: Since the uprising was announced at Jiujiang, all have called the Deng clan mad and deluded; lately rumor has spread through the realm, and it has somewhat tarnished you, our friend.
translations.idiomatic: Since the uprising was announced at Jiujiang, all have called the Deng clan mad and deluded. Lately rumor has spread through the realm, and it has somewhat tarnished you, our friend.

sentences.zh: 道路之議，豈其或然，聞此之日，能無駭惋。

translations.literal: Can the talk along the roads truly be so? On the day we heard it, how could we not be stunned and grieved?
translations.idiomatic: Can the talk along the roads truly be so? On the day we heard it, how could we not be stunned and grieved?

sentences.zh: 凶人反道敗德，日夜滋深，昵近狡慝，取謀豺虎，非惟毒流外物，惡積中朝，乃欲毀陵邑，虐崇憲，燒宗廟，鹵御物，然後蕩覆京都，必使蘭蕕俱盡。

translations.literal: The wicked man perverts the Way and debases virtue, growing worse day by day. He draws close to the cunning and vicious, taking counsel from jackals and tigers. His poison flows not only abroad—it festers at the very heart of the court. He would destroy the imperial tombs, defile the high laws, burn the ancestral temples, and despoil the imperial treasures, and then overthrow the capital, bringing noble and base alike to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked man perverts the Way and debases virtue, growing worse day by day. He draws close to the cunning and vicious, taking counsel from jackals and tigers. His poison flows not only abroad—it festers at the very heart of the court. He would destroy the imperial tombs, defile the high laws, burn the ancestral temples, and despoil the imperial treasures, and then overthrow the capital, bringing noble and base alike to ruin.

sentences.zh: 自非聖上廟筭靈圖，俛眉遜避，維持內外，擁衛臣下，則赤縣為戎，百姓其魚矣。

translations.literal: Had not the sovereign, in the divine counsel of the ancestral temple, bowed and yielded for a time, holding inner and outer realms together and shielding his ministers, the Central Land would have become a battlefield and the common people fish gasping in the shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Had not the sovereign, in the divine counsel of the ancestral temple, bowed and yielded for a time, holding inner and outer realms together and shielding his ministers, the Central Land would have become a battlefield and the common people fish gasping in the shallows.

sentences.zh: 此事此理，寧可孰念！

translations.literal: Can you truly contemplate this affair and this reasoning without care!
translations.idiomatic: Can you truly contemplate this affair and this reasoning without care!

sentences.zh: 既天道輔順，謳歌有奉，高祖之孫，文皇之子，德洞九幽，功貫三曜，匡拯家國，提毓黔首，若不子民南面，將使神器何歸。

translations.literal: Heaven already aids the rightful cause, and songs of praise already have their object. He is the grandson of the High Ancestor, the son of the Cultivated Emperor—virtue reaching to the nine dark realms, merit spanning the three luminaries, saving house and state and nurturing the black-haired people. If he does not face south as father to the people, to whom should the sacred vessel pass?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven already aids the rightful cause, and songs of praise already have their object. He is the grandson of the High Ancestor, the son of the Cultivated Emperor—virtue reaching to the nine dark realms, merit spanning the three luminaries, saving house and state and nurturing the black-haired people. If he does not face south as father to the people, to whom should the sacred vessel pass?

sentences.zh: 而群小構慝，妄生窺覬，成軫惑燕，貫高亂趙，讒人罔極，自古有之。

translations.literal: Yet petty men weave wicked schemes and vainly harbor designs of usurpation—like Cheng Zhen misleading Yan, like Guan Gao stirring rebellion in Zhao. Slanderers know no limit; this has been so since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men weave wicked schemes and vainly harbor designs of usurpation—like Cheng Zhen misleading Yan, like Guan Gao stirring rebellion in Zhao. Slanderers know no limit; this has been so since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 汝中京冠冕，儒雅世襲，多見前載，縣鑒忠邪，何遠遺郎中之清軌，近忘太尉之純槩。

translations.literal: You are a crown of the central capital, heir to a line of Confucian learning, well read in the records of old, your mirror hung to distinguish loyal from treacherous—why forget the clear path of the Director of Attendants and set aside the pure integrity of the Grand Commandant?
translations.idiomatic: You are a crown of the central capital, heir to a line of Confucian learning, well read in the records of old, your mirror hung to distinguish loyal from treacherous—why forget the clear path of the Director of Attendants and set aside the pure integrity of the Grand Commandant?

sentences.zh: 相與，或群從舅甥，或姻婭周款，一旦胡、越，能無悵恨。

translations.literal: We, your peers—some cousins, uncle and nephew, some bound by marriage in close affection—if we were suddenly parted like Hu from Yue, how could we not feel sorrow and resentment?
translations.idiomatic: We, your peers—some cousins, uncle and nephew, some bound by marriage in close affection—if we were suddenly parted like Hu from Yue, how could we not feel sorrow and resentment?

sentences.zh: 若疑誑所至，邪詖無窮，汝當誓眾奮戈，翦此朝食。

translations.literal: If doubt and deception have clouded your path and perverse slander knows no end, you should swear your forces to arms and destroy this foe before breakfast.
translations.idiomatic: If doubt and deception have clouded your path and perverse slander knows no end, you should swear your forces to arms and destroy this foe before breakfast.

sentences.zh: 若自延過聽，迷塗未遠，聖上臨物以仁，接下以愛，豈直雍齒先封，乃當射鉤見相矣！

translations.literal: If you have lingered too long in credulous listening and strayed not far from the wrong road—the sovereign treats things with humanity and receives his subjects with love. Would he merely emulate Duke Wen's early enfeoffment of Yong Chi? He would even appoint as minister one who once shot at him!
translations.idiomatic: If you have lingered too long in credulous listening and strayed not far from the wrong road—the sovereign treats things with humanity and receives his subjects with love. Would he merely emulate Duke Wen's early enfeoffment of Yong Chi? He would even appoint as minister one who once shot at him!

sentences.zh: 當由力窘跡屈，丹誠未亮邪。

translations.literal: Is it that your strength is exhausted and your path constrained, and your loyal heart not yet made clear?
translations.idiomatic: Is it that your strength is exhausted and your path constrained, and your loyal heart not yet made clear?

sentences.zh: 跂予南服，寤寐延首，若反棹沿流，歸誠鳳闕，錫珪開宇，非爾而誰。

translations.literal: We gaze southward, waking and sleeping with outstretched necks. If you turn your oars and follow the current homeward, returning in loyalty to the Phoenix Gate, who but you should receive the jade tablet and open dominion?
translations.idiomatic: We gaze southward, waking and sleeping with outstretched necks. If you turn your oars and follow the current homeward, returning in loyalty to the Phoenix Gate, who but you should receive the jade tablet and open dominion?

sentences.zh: 吾等並過荷曲慈，俱叨非服，紆金拖玉，改觀蓬門，入奉舜、禹之渥，出見羲、唐之化，雍容揄揚，信白駒空谷之時也。

translations.literal: We have all undeservedly received special kindness, all been granted honors beyond our due—sashes of gold and pendants of jade have transformed the humble gate. In audience we receive the bounty of Shun and Yu; abroad we witness the transformation of Xi and Tang. At ease in dignity and praise, this is truly the hour when the white colt grazes in the empty valley.
translations.idiomatic: We have all undeservedly received special kindness, all been granted honors beyond our due—sashes of gold and pendants of jade have transformed the humble gate. In audience we receive the bounty of Shun and Yu; abroad we witness the transformation of Xi and Tang. At ease in dignity and praise, this is truly the hour when the white colt grazes in the empty valley.

sentences.zh: 奈何毀擲先基，自蹈凶戾，山門蕭瑟，松庭誰掃，言念楚路，豈不思父母之邦。

translations.literal: Why then abandon the foundations laid by your ancestors and tread the path of violence? Your mountain gate stands desolate; who will sweep the pine courtyard? At the thought of the road to Chu, how can you not yearn for the land of your fathers?
translations.idiomatic: Why then abandon the foundations laid by your ancestors and tread the path of violence? Your mountain gate stands desolate; who will sweep the pine courtyard? At the thought of the road to Chu, how can you not yearn for the land of your fathers?

sentences.zh: 幸納惡石，以蠲美疹。

translations.literal: We pray you will accept this harsh counsel and cleanse the blight upon your fair name.
translations.idiomatic: We pray you will accept this harsh counsel and cleanse the blight upon your fair name.

sentences.zh: 裁書表意，爾其圖之。

translations.literal: This letter sets forth our meaning; ponder it well.
translations.idiomatic: This letter sets forth our meaning; ponder it well.

sentences.zh: 時尚書右僕射蔡興宗是顗舅，領軍將軍袁粲是顗從父弟，故書云群從舅甥也。

translations.literal: At the time, Cai Xingzong, Right Vice Director in the Masters of Writing, was Yi's uncle, and Yuan Can, General Who Leads the Army, was Yi's paternal cousin; hence the letter speaks of "cousins, uncle and nephew."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Cai Xingzong, Right Vice Director in the Masters of Writing, was Yuan Yi's uncle, and Yuan Can, General Who Leads the Army, was Yuan Yi's paternal cousin; hence the letter speaks of "cousins, uncle and nephew."

sentences.zh: 子勛徵顗下尋陽，遣侍中孔道存行雍州事。

translations.literal: Liu Zixun summoned Yi down to Xunyang and dispatched Kong Daocun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, to administer Yong Province in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zixun summoned Yuan Yi down to Xunyang and dispatched Kong Daocun, Attendant-in-Ordinary, to administer Yong Province in his stead.

sentences.zh: 顗乃率眾馳下，使子戩領家累俱還。

translations.literal: Yi then led his followers south in haste and sent his son Kan to bring the household back with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi then led his followers south in haste and sent his son Kan to bring the household back with him.

sentences.zh: 時劉胡屯鵲尾，久不決。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Hu was encamped at Quewei, and victory long remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Hu was encamped at Quewei, and victory long remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年夏，加顗都督征討諸軍事，給鼓吹一部，率樓船千艘，戰士二萬，來入鵲尾。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Taishi, Yi was made Supervisor of All Military Affairs on the punitive campaign; he was given one set of martial pipes and drums and led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand fighting men into Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Taishi, Yuan Yi was made Supervisor of All Military Affairs on the punitive campaign. He was given one set of martial pipes and drums and led a thousand tower ships and twenty thousand fighting men into Quewei.

sentences.zh: 顗本無將略，性又怯橈，在軍中未嘗戎服，語不及戰陳，唯賦詩談義而已。

translations.literal: Yi had no talent for command by nature and was timid and yielding; in camp he never wore martial dress, his talk never touched on battle, and he did nothing but compose poetry and discuss doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi had no talent for command by nature and was timid and yielding. In camp he never wore martial dress, his talk never touched on battle, and he did nothing but compose poetry and discuss doctrine.

sentences.zh: 不能撫接諸將，劉胡每論事，酬對甚簡，由此大失人情，胡常切齒恚恨。

translations.literal: He could not win over his generals; when Liu Hu discussed affairs, his replies were very curt, and by this he lost hearts on a grand scale. Hu often gnashed his teeth in fury.
translations.idiomatic: He could not win over his generals. When Liu Hu discussed affairs, his replies were very curt, and by this he lost hearts on a grand scale. Hu often gnashed his teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 胡以南運未至，軍士匱乏，就顗換襄陽之資。

translations.literal: As supplies from the south had not arrived and the soldiers were in want, Hu asked Yi to draw on the resources of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: As supplies from the south had not arrived and the soldiers were in want, Hu asked Yuan Yi to draw on the resources of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 顗答曰：「都下兩宅未成，亦應經理，不可損徹。」

translations.literal: Yi replied: "My two residences in the capital are not yet finished and also require upkeep—they cannot be stripped bare."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi replied: "My two residences in the capital are not yet finished and also require upkeep—they cannot be stripped bare."

sentences.zh: 又信往來之言，京師米貴，斗至數百，以為不勞攻伐，行自離散，於是擁甲以待之。

translations.literal: He also believed rumors from the capital that grain in the capital region had grown dear, costing hundreds per dou, and assumed the enemy would disperse without need of fighting; thus he held his armor idle and waited.
translations.idiomatic: He also believed rumors from the capital that grain in the capital region had grown dear, costing hundreds per dou, and assumed the enemy would disperse without need of fighting. Thus he held his armor idle and waited.

sentences.zh: 太宗使顗舊門生徐碩奉手詔譬顗曰：「卿歷觀古今，嶮之與強，何嘗可恃。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent Xu Shuo, Yi's former student, to deliver an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand and reason with him: "You have seen all of history—have rugged terrain and raw strength ever been reliable?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Xu Shuo, Yuan Yi's former student, to deliver an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand and reason with him: "You have seen all of history—have rugged terrain and raw strength ever been reliable?

sentences.zh: 自朕踐阼，塗路梗塞，卿無由奉表，未經為臣。

translations.literal: Since We ascended the throne, roads have been blocked and you could not submit memorials—you have yet to formally become Our subject.
translations.idiomatic: Since We ascended the throne, roads have been blocked and you could not submit memorials—you have yet to formally become Our subject.

sentences.zh: 今追蹤竇融，猶未為晚也。」

translations.literal: To follow in the footsteps of Dou Rong now would not yet be too late."
translations.idiomatic: To follow in the footsteps of Dou Rong now would not yet be too late."

sentences.zh: 顗子戩，為偽黃門侍郎，加輔國將軍，戍盆城。

translations.literal: Yi's son Kan served as Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate at the rebel court, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State, garrisoning Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi's son Kan served as Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate at the rebel court, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State, garrisoning Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 尋陽敗，戩棄城走，討禽伏誅。

translations.literal: When Xunyang fell, Kan abandoned the city and fled; he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xunyang fell, Kan abandoned the city and fled. He was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 孔覬，字思遠，會稽山陰人，太常琳之孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Ji, styled Siyuan, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery, grandson of the Minister of Ceremonials Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery, grandson of the Minister of Ceremonials Lin.

sentences.zh: 父邈，揚州治中。

translations.literal: His father Miao was an Administrator-Assistant of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao was an Administrator-Assistant of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 覬少骨梗有風力，以是非為己任。

translations.literal: Ji from youth was stern and forceful in character, making right and wrong his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji was stern and forceful in character, making right and wrong his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 口吃，好讀書，早知名。

translations.literal: He had a stammer, loved books, and gained early renown.
translations.idiomatic: He had a stammer, loved books, and gained early renown.

sentences.zh: 初舉揚州秀才，補主簿，長沙王義欣鎮軍功曹，衡陽王義季安西主簿，戶曹參軍，領南義陽太守，轉署記室，奉箋固辭，曰：「記室之局，實惟華要，自非文行秀敏，莫或居之。

translations.literal: Initially nominated as Yangzhou distinguished scholar, he served as chief clerk, as Army Merit Officer on the headquarters staff of Prince Yixin of Changsha as General Who Garrisons the Army, as Chief Clerk on the Army of the West staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang, as Registrar in the Household Bureau, and concurrently as Governor of South Yiyang; when transferred to serve as Chief of the Records Office, he submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "The post of Records Office is truly a splendid and important one; unless one's literary and moral attainments are outstanding and keen, none should hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially nominated as Yangzhou distinguished scholar, he served as chief clerk, as Army Merit Officer on the headquarters staff of Prince Yixin of Changsha as General Who Garrisons the Army, as Chief Clerk on the Army of the West staff of Prince Yiji of Hengyang, as Registrar in the Household Bureau, and concurrently as Governor of South Yiyang. When transferred to serve as Chief of the Records Office, he submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "The post of Records Office is truly a splendid and important one; unless one's literary and moral attainments are outstanding and keen, none should hold it.

sentences.zh: 覬遜業之舉，無聞於鄉部；

translations.literal: I have no reputation in my native district for achievements in the examinations;
translations.idiomatic: I have no reputation in my native district for achievements in the examinations;

sentences.zh: 惰遊之貶，有編於疲農。

translations.literal: a record of idle wandering is enrolled among the weary farmers.
translations.idiomatic: a record of idle wandering is enrolled among the weary farmers.

sentences.zh: 直山淵藏引，用不遐棄，故得抃風舞潤，憑附彌年。

translations.literal: Yet your lordship, like a mountain straight and deep in reserve, has not cast me off from afar, so that I have danced on the breeze and drunk the dew, clinging to your service these many years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your lordship, like a mountain straight and deep in reserve, has not cast me off from afar, so that I have danced on the breeze and drunk the dew, clinging to your service these many years.

sentences.zh: 今日之命，非所敢冒。

translations.literal: Today's appointment is not one I dare presumptuously accept.
translations.idiomatic: Today's appointment is not one I dare presumptuously accept.

sentences.zh: 昔之學優藝富，猶尚斯難，況覬能薄質魯，亦何容易。

translations.literal: In former days, those rich in learning and talent still found such a post daunting—how much less should I, Ji, of slender ability and dull substance, take it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In former days, those rich in learning and talent still found such a post daunting—how much less should I, Ji, of slender ability and dull substance, take it lightly.

sentences.zh: 覬聞居方辨物，君人所以官才；

translations.literal: I have heard that the ruler appoints talent by assigning each to his proper place and discerning things by their kind;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ruler appoints talent by assigning each to his proper place and discerning things by their kind;

sentences.zh: 陳力就列，自下所以奉上。

translations.literal: it is the subject's part to display his strength in the assigned rank and thereby serve his lord above.
translations.idiomatic: it is the subject's part to display his strength in the assigned rank and thereby serve his lord above.

sentences.zh: 覬雖不敏，常服斯言。

translations.literal: Though I, Ji, am not clever, I have always held fast to these words.
translations.idiomatic: Though I, Ji, am not clever, I have always held fast to these words.

sentences.zh: 今寵藉惟舊，舉非尚德，恐無以提衡一隅，僉允視聽者也。

translations.literal: Now favor is granted merely through old acquaintance, the appointment not grounded in virtue—I fear I cannot hold the scales for one corner of the realm and win universal assent in what the eyes and ears perceive.
translations.idiomatic: Now favor is granted merely through old acquaintance, the appointment not grounded in virtue—I fear I cannot hold the scales for one corner of the realm and win universal assent in what the eyes and ears perceive.

sentences.zh: 伏願天明照其心請，乞改今局，授以閑曹，則鳧鶴從方，所憂去矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly pray that your enlightened understanding will see the sincerity of my plea: grant me another post instead of the present one, assign me to an idle bureau—then the goose and the crane would each follow its measure, and my worries would be gone.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that your enlightened understanding will see the sincerity of my plea: grant me another post instead of the present one, assign me to an idle bureau—then the goose and the crane would each follow its measure, and my worries would be gone.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「夫以記室之要，宜須通才敏忠，加性情勤密者。

translations.literal: He also said: "For the importance of the Records Office, one truly needs a comprehensive talent—quick and loyal, with a disposition diligent and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "For the importance of the Records Office, one truly needs a comprehensive talent—quick and loyal, with a disposition diligent and careful.

sentences.zh: 覬學不綜貫，性又疏惰，何可以屬知秘記，秉筆文閨。

translations.literal: Ji lacks comprehensive learning and by nature is lax and indolent—how could he be entrusted with secret records and hold the brush in the literary chamber?
translations.idiomatic: Ji lacks comprehensive learning and by nature is lax and indolent—how could he be entrusted with secret records and hold the brush in the literary chamber?

sentences.zh: 假吹之尤，方斯非濫。

translations.literal: The fault of the incompetent musician—how much more unfit is this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of the incompetent musician—how much more unfit is this appointment.

sentences.zh: 覬少淪常檢，本無遠植，榮進之願，何能忘懷。

translations.literal: Ji had long since fallen below ordinary standards and never possessed lofty standing; the wish for honor and advancement—how could he forget it entirely?
translations.idiomatic: Ji had long since fallen below ordinary standards and never possessed lofty standing; the wish for honor and advancement—how could he forget it entirely?

sentences.zh: 若實有螢爝，增暉光景，固其騰聲之日，飛藻之辰也，豈敢自求從容，保其淡逸。

translations.literal: If I truly had some spark of firefly or reed torch to add gleam to the light, that would indeed be the day to rise in fame and the hour to soar in letters—how then would I dare seek ease and hold to detachment?
translations.idiomatic: If I truly had some spark of firefly or reed torch to add gleam to the light, that would indeed be the day to rise in fame and the hour to soar in letters—how then would I dare seek ease and hold to detachment?

sentences.zh: 伏願矜其魯拙，業之有地，則曲成之施，終始優渥。」

translations.literal: I humbly ask that you pity my dullness and grant a field in which my talent may work—then your grace in completing what is bent would be generous from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that you pity my dullness and grant a field in which my talent may work—then your grace in completing what is bent would be generous from first to last.

sentences.zh: 義季不能奪，遂得免。

translations.literal: Prince Yiji could not override him, and he was spared the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiji could not override him, and he was spared the appointment.

sentences.zh: 召為通直郎，太子中舍人，建平王友，秘書丞，中書侍郎，隨王誕安東諮議參軍，領記室，黃門侍郎，建平王宏中軍長史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Court Gentleman for Direct Communication, Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, Companion to the Prince of Jianping, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, Deputy Director of the Central Secretariat, Advisory Officer on the Eastern Pacification staff of Prince Dan of Sui, Chief of the Records Office, Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate, and Chief Administrator on the Central Army staff of Prince Hong of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Court Gentleman for Direct Communication, Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent, Companion to the Prince of Jianping, Assistant Director of the Secretariat, Deputy Director of the Central Secretariat, Advisory Officer on the Eastern Pacification staff of Prince Dan of Sui, Chief of the Records Office, Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate, and Chief Administrator on the Central Army staff of Prince Hong of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 復為黃門，臨海太守。

translations.literal: He again served as Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate and as Governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate and as Governor of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 初，晉世散騎常侍選望甚重，與侍中不異，其後職任閒散，用人漸輕。

translations.literal: Initially, in Jin times the selection and prestige of Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry was very weighty, no different from Attendant-in-Ordinary; later the duties grew idle and scattered, and appointments gradually became less esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Jin times the selection and prestige of Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry was very weighty, no different from Attendant-in-Ordinary. Later the duties grew idle and scattered, and appointments gradually became less esteemed.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，世祖欲重其選，詔曰：「散騎職為近侍，事居規納，置任之本，實惟親要，而頃選常侍，陵遲未允，宜簡授時良，永置清轍。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian, Emperor Xiaowu wished to restore weight to its selection. An edict proclaimed: "The post of Dispersed Cavalry Attendant is one of close attendance, its business counselling and remonstrance—the foundation of its establishment is truly personal and important. Yet recent appointments to Regular Attendant have fallen in esteem and been unsatisfactory; worthy men of the age should be selected and set on a lasting path of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian, Emperor Xiaowu wished to restore weight to its selection. An edict proclaimed: "The post of Dispersed Cavalry Attendant is one of close attendance, its business counselling and remonstrance—the foundation of its establishment is truly personal and important. Yet recent appointments to Regular Attendant have fallen in esteem and been unsatisfactory. Worthy men of the age should be selected and set on a lasting path of integrity.

sentences.zh: 於是吏部尚書顏竣奏曰：「常侍華選，職任俟才，新除臨海太守孔覬意業閑素，司徒左長史王彧懷尚清理，並任為散騎常侍。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan Jun, Minister of Personnel, memorialized: "Regular Attendant is a splendid selection, the post awaiting worthy talent. Kong Ji, newly appointed Governor of Linhai, is of serene character and plain attainments; Wang Yu, Left Chief Administrator of the Grand Tutor, cherishes clarity and discipline—both are fit for Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yan Jun, Minister of Personnel, memorialized: "Regular Attendant is a splendid selection, the post awaiting worthy talent. Kong Ji, newly appointed Governor of Linhai, is of serene character and plain attainments; Wang Yu, Left Chief Administrator of the Grand Tutor, cherishes clarity and discipline—both are fit for Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世祖不欲威權在下，其後分吏部尚書置二人，以輕其任。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu did not wish authority to rest below him; thereafter the post of Minister of Personnel was split between two appointees to lighten its power.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu did not wish authority to rest below him. Thereafter the post of Minister of Personnel was split between two appointees to lighten its power.

sentences.zh: 侍中蔡興宗謂人曰：「選曹要重，常侍閑淡，改之以名而不以實，雖主意欲為輕重，人心豈可變邪！」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong said to others: "The Personnel Bureau is important and weighty; Regular Attendant is idle and light—changing the name without changing the reality: though the sovereign's intent was to shift the balance, can human perception truly be altered?
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Cai Xingzong said to others: "The Personnel Bureau is important and weighty; Regular Attendant is idle and light—changing the name without changing the reality. Though the sovereign's intent was to shift the balance, can human perception truly be altered?

sentences.zh: 既而常侍之選復卑，選部之貴不異。

translations.literal: Before long the selection for Regular Attendant again sank low, and the prestige of the Personnel Bureau was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the selection for Regular Attendant again sank low, and the prestige of the Personnel Bureau was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 覬領本州大中正。

translations.literal: Ji served as Senior Recruiter for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Ji served as Senior Recruiter for his native province.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，改太子中庶子，領翊軍校尉，轉秘書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Commander of the Guarding Army, and then Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming, he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Commander of the Guarding Army, and then Director of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 欲以為吏部郎，不果。

translations.literal: The court wished to appoint him Director in the Ministry of Personnel, but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to appoint him Director in the Ministry of Personnel, but it did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉卿，御史中丞，坐鞭令史，為有司所糾，原不問。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and then Censor-in-Chief; when he was impeached for flogging a clerical officer, he was pardoned and not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Justice and then Censor-in-Chief. When he was impeached for flogging a clerical officer, he was pardoned and not prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 六年，除義興太守，未之任，為尋陽王子房冠軍長史，加寧朔將軍，行淮南、宣城二郡事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Yixing; before taking up the post he became Chief Administrator to Prince Zifang of Xunyang as Champion General, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North, acting in the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Governor of Yixing. Before taking up the post he became Chief Administrator to Prince Zifang of Xunyang as Champion General, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North, acting in the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 其年，復除安陸王子綏冠軍長史、江夏內史，復隨府轉後軍長史如故。

translations.literal: That same year he was again appointed Chief Administrator to Prince Zisui of Anlu as Champion General and Internal Administrator of Jiangxia; he then transferred with the prince's headquarters to Chief Administrator of the Rear Army, his rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was again appointed Chief Administrator to Prince Zisui of Anlu as Champion General and Internal Administrator of Jiangxia. He then transferred with the prince's headquarters to Chief Administrator of the Rear Army, his rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 為人使酒仗氣，每醉輒彌日不醒，僚類之間，多所凌忽，尤不能曲意權幸，莫不畏而疾之。

translations.literal: By nature he was given to wine and swagger; when drunk he often remained unconscious for whole days. Among his colleagues he frequently showed contempt, and above all he would not bend to the powerful and favored—everyone feared and loathed him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was given to wine and swagger. When drunk he often remained unconscious for whole days. Among his colleagues he frequently showed contempt, and above all he would not bend to the powerful and favored—everyone feared and loathed him.

sentences.zh: 不治產業，居常貧罄，有無豐約，未嘗關懷。

translations.literal: He did not manage property; he lived in constant poverty, and whether he had much or little he never gave it thought.
translations.idiomatic: He did not manage property. He lived in constant poverty, and whether he had much or little he never gave it thought.

sentences.zh: 為二府長史，典籤諮事，不呼不敢前，不令去不敢去。

translations.literal: Serving as chief administrator to two princely headquarters, those who handled official seals and advisory affairs dared not approach unless summoned and dared not leave unless dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as chief administrator to two princely headquarters, those who handled official seals and advisory affairs dared not approach unless summoned and dared not leave unless dismissed.

sentences.zh: 雖醉日居多，而明曉政事，醒時判決，未嘗有壅。

translations.literal: Though drunk more days than not, he was clear in his grasp of affairs; when sober his judgments were never blocked or delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Though drunk more days than not, he was clear in his grasp of affairs. When sober his judgments were never blocked or delayed.

sentences.zh: 眾咸云：「孔公一月二十九日醉，勝他人二十九日醒也。」

translations.literal: All agreed: "Master Kong is drunk for twenty-nine days of the month—and that beats twenty-nine days awake for anyone else."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed: "Master Kong is drunk for twenty-nine days of the month—and that beats twenty-nine days awake for anyone else."

sentences.zh: 世祖每欲引見，先遣人覘其醉醒。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xiaowu wished to summon him for an audience, he first sent someone to observe whether he was drunk or sober.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Xiaowu wished to summon him for an audience, he first sent someone to observe whether he was drunk or sober.

sentences.zh: 性真素，不尚矯飾，遇得寶玩，服用不疑，而他物粗敗，終不改易。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and sincere and did not care for ostentation; when he obtained treasure or curios he wore or used them without hesitation, yet when other things were worn or shabby he never changed them.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and sincere by nature, he had no taste for show. Treasure or curio that came his way he wore or used without a second thought; when other things were worn or shabby, he never replaced them.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡顧覬之亦尚儉素，衣裘器服，皆擇其陋者。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Jizhi of Wu commandery also prized frugality and simplicity; in clothing, furs, vessels, and appointments he always chose the shabbiest.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Jizhi of Wu commandery also lived by frugality and plainness, choosing the shabbiest clothing, furs, vessels, and furnishings he could find.

sentences.zh: 宋世言清約，稱此二人。

translations.literal: In Song times, when men spoke of austere integrity, they named these two.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song, when men spoke of austere integrity, they named these two.

sentences.zh: 覬弟道存，從弟徽，頗營產業。

translations.literal: Kong Ji's younger brother Daocun and his cousin Hui were both rather given to building up property.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji's younger brother Daocun and his cousin Hui were both rather given to building up property.

sentences.zh: 二弟請假東還，覬出渚迎之，輜重十餘船，皆是綿絹紙席之屬。

translations.literal: When the two brothers asked leave to return east, Ji went out to the islet to meet them; their baggage filled more than ten boats, all silk, gauze, paper, and matting of that sort.
translations.idiomatic: When the two brothers asked leave to return east, Ji went out to the islet to meet them. Their baggage filled more than ten boats—silks, gauzes, paper, and matting of every kind.

sentences.zh: 覬見之，偽喜，謂曰：「我比困乏，得此甚要。」

translations.literal: Ji saw it and feigned delight, saying: "I have been much in want lately—getting this is truly needful."
translations.idiomatic: Ji saw it and feigned delight. "I have been much in want lately," he said. "Getting this is truly needful.

sentences.zh: 因命上置岸側，既而正色謂道存等曰：「汝輩忝預士流，何至還東作賈客邪！」

translations.literal: He ordered it unloaded on the bank, then sternly said to Daocun and the others: "You disgrace the ranks of the gentry—how dare you return east to play the merchant!"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it unloaded on the bank, then turned stern. "You disgrace the ranks of the gentry—how dare you return east to play the merchant!"

sentences.zh: 命左右取火燒之，燒盡乃去。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to fetch fire and burn it all; only when it was consumed did he leave.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to fetch fire and burn it all, and only when the flames had consumed everything did he leave.

sentences.zh: 先是，庾徽之為御史中丞，性豪麗，服玩甚華，覬代之，衣冠器用，莫不粗率。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu Huizhi had served as Censor-in-Chief; by nature he was extravagant and his dress and accoutrements were very splendid. When Ji replaced him, clothing, caps, vessels, and furnishings were none of them anything but plain and rough.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Huizhi had served as Censor-in-Chief, a man extravagant by nature whose dress and accoutrements were very splendid. When Ji replaced him, clothing, caps, vessels, and furnishings were all plain and rough without exception.

sentences.zh: 蘭臺令史並三吳富人，咸有輕之之意，覬蓬首緩帶，風貌清嚴，皆重跡屏氣，莫敢欺犯。

translations.literal: The clerks of the Secretariat archives and the wealthy men of the Three Wu regions all looked on him with contempt; but with unkempt hair and a loose sash, his bearing austere and stern, they all walked softly and held their breath, none daring to take liberties.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks of the Secretariat archives and the wealthy men of the Three Wu all looked on him with contempt. Yet with unkempt hair and a loose sash, his bearing austere and stern, they walked softly and held their breath, none daring to take liberties.

sentences.zh: 庾徽之，字景猷，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Huizhi, styled Jingyou, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huizhi, courtesy name Jingyou, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 自中丞出為新安王子鸞北中郎長史、南東海太守，卒官。

translations.literal: After leaving the post of Censor-in-Chief he was appointed Chief Administrator on the Northern Center Army staff of Prince Ziluan of Xin'an and Governor of Southern Donghai; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving the post of Censor-in-Chief he was appointed Chief Administrator on the Northern Center Army staff of Prince Ziluan of Xin'an and Governor of Southern Donghai, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，召覬為太子詹事，遣故佐平西司馬庾業為右軍司馬，代覬行會稽郡事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he summoned Ji as Tutor of the Heir Apparent and dispatched his former aide Yu Ye, Marshall of the Pacifying West Army, as Marshall of the Right Army to act in Kong Ji's stead in the affairs of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he summoned Ji as Tutor of the Heir Apparent and dispatched his former aide Yu Ye, Marshall of the Pacifying West Army, as Marshall of the Right Army to administer Kuaiji commandery in Kong Ji's stead.

sentences.zh: 時上流反叛，上遣都水使者孔璪入東慰勞。

translations.literal: At the time the upper Yangtze region had rebelled; the emperor sent the Commissioner of Waterways Kong Zuan east to offer consolation and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the upper Yangtze region had rebelled, and the emperor sent the Commissioner of Waterways Kong Zuan east to offer consolation and rewards.

sentences.zh: 璪至，說覬以廢帝侈費，倉儲耗盡，都下罄匱，資用已竭。

translations.literal: When Zuan arrived, he urged Ji with the tale that the deposed emperor's extravagance had emptied the storehouses, the capital was drained bare, and supplies were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan arrived, he urged Ji with the tale that the deposed emperor's extravagance had emptied the storehouses, the capital was drained bare, and supplies were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 今南北並起，遠近離叛，若擁五郡之銳，招動三吳，事無不克。

translations.literal: Now rebellion has risen north and south, the near and far have split away; if you gather the sharp edge of five commanderies and rouse the Three Wu, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion has risen north and south; near and far have split away. Gather the sharp edge of five commanderies and rouse the Three Wu, and nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 覬然其言，遂發兵馳檄。

translations.literal: Ji thought well of his words and thereupon raised troops and dispatched a proclamation by post.
translations.idiomatic: Ji thought well of his words and thereupon raised troops and dispatched a proclamation by post.

sentences.zh: 覬子長公、璪二子淹、玄竝在都，馳信密報。

translations.literal: Kong Ji's son Changgong and Zuan's two sons Yan and Xuan were all in the capital; they sent urgent secret reports.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji's son Changgong and Zuan's two sons Yan and Xuan were all in the capital, and they sent urgent secret reports.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月，竝叛逃東歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, all rebelled and fled eastward home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Taishi, all rebelled and fled eastward home.

sentences.zh: 遣書要吳郡太守顧琛，琛以母年篤老，又密邇京邑，與長子寶素謀議，未叛。

translations.literal: He sent letters summoning Gu Chen, Governor of Wu commandery. Chen, because his mother was very old in years and because Wu lay close to the capital, consulted with his eldest son Baosu and did not rebel at first.
translations.idiomatic: He sent letters summoning Gu Chen, Governor of Wu commandery. Chen, whose mother was very old and whose commandery lay close to the capital, consulted with his eldest son Baosu and did not rebel at first.

sentences.zh: 少子寶先時為山陰令，馳書報琛，以南師已近，朝廷孤弱，不時順從，必有覆滅之禍。

translations.literal: His younger son Baoxian, who was then Magistrate of Shanyin, sent a galloping dispatch to Chen warning that the southern army was already near, the court weak and isolated, and that failure to follow suit in time would bring certain ruin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Baoxian, then Magistrate of Shanyin, sent a galloping dispatch warning that the southern army was already near, the court weak and isolated, and that failure to follow suit in time would bring certain ruin.

sentences.zh: 覬前鋒軍已渡浙江，琛遂據郡同反。

translations.literal: Kong Ji's vanguard had already crossed the Zhe River; Chen thereupon held the commandery and joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ji's vanguard had already crossed the Zhe River, and Chen thereupon held the commandery and joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守王曇生、義興太守劉延熙、晉陵太守袁標，一時回應。

translations.literal: Wang Tansheng, Governor of Wuxing; Liu Yanxi, Governor of Yixing; and Yuan Biao, Governor of Jinling—all responded at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tansheng, Governor of Wuxing; Liu Yanxi, Governor of Yixing; and Yuan Biao, Governor of Jinling—all responded at once.

sentences.zh: 庾業既東，太宗即以代延熙為義興，加建威將軍，以延熙為巴陵王休若鎮東長史。

translations.literal: Once Yu Ye had gone east, Emperor Ming appointed him in Liu Yanxi's place as Governor of Yixing, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and made Yanxi Chief Administrator on the Eastern Pacification staff of Prince Xiuruo of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Ye had gone east, Emperor Ming appointed him in Liu Yanxi's place as Governor of Yixing, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and made Yanxi Chief Administrator on the Eastern Pacification staff of Prince Xiuruo of Baling.

sentences.zh: 業至長塘湖，即與延熙合。

translations.literal: Ye reached Changtang Lake and immediately joined forces with Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ye reached Changtang Lake and immediately joined forces with Yanxi.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣建威將軍沈懷明東討，尚書張永係進，鎮東將軍巴陵王休若董統東討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming dispatched General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming on an eastern punitive campaign, with Zhang Yong, Master of Writing, following behind, and Prince Xiuruo of Baling, General Who Pacifies the East, supervising all eastern punitive forces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming dispatched General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming on an eastern punitive campaign, with Zhang Yong, Master of Writing, following behind, and Prince Xiuruo of Baling, General Who Pacifies the East, supervising all eastern punitive forces.

sentences.zh: 移檄東土曰：

translations.literal: A proclamation was sent to the eastern lands, saying:
translations.idiomatic: A proclamation was sent to the eastern lands, saying:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞釁集有兆，禍至無門，倚伏之來，實惟人致。

translations.literal: It is heard that when outrage gathers, omens appear; disaster arrives though no gate is opened; the turn from lean to fat comes—truly men bring it on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that when outrage gathers, omens appear; disaster arrives though no gate is opened; fortune and ruin turn on what men themselves bring about.

sentences.zh: 故囂、述貪亂，終殄宗祀；

translations.literal: Thus Xiao and Shu, greedy for disorder, in the end extinguished their ancestral temples;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Gong Xiao and Xu Shu, greedy for disorder, in the end extinguished their ancestral temples;

sentences.zh: 昌、憲構氛，旋潤斧鉞。

translations.literal: Chang and Xian, brewing rebellion, soon wetted the axe and blade.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang and Wang Xian, brewing rebellion, soon wetted the axe and blade.

sentences.zh: 斯則昭章記牒，炯戒今古者也。

translations.literal: These are cases set forth bright in the records, warnings glaring across ages past and present.
translations.idiomatic: These are cases set forth bright in the records—warnings glaring across ages past and present.

sentences.zh: 自國步時艱，三綱道盡，神歇靈繹，璿業綴旒。

translations.literal: Since the nation's step grew troubled, the three bonds' way was spent, spirit faltered and numen frayed, the jade succession hung by its tassel cord.
translations.idiomatic: Since the nation's step grew troubled, the three bonds were spent, spirit faltered and numen frayed, and the jade succession hung by its tassel cord.

sentences.zh: 皇上仁雄集瑞，英睿應歷，鳳儀熛升，龍輝電舉。

translations.literal: Our Sovereign, benevolence and heroism gathering auspicious signs, brilliance and wisdom answering the calendar—phoenix mien blazes upward, dragon glory leaps like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sovereign, benevolence and heroism gathering auspicious signs, brilliance and wisdom answering the calendar—phoenix mien blazes upward, dragon glory leaps like lightning.

sentences.zh: 蕩穢紫樞，不俟鳴條之誓，凝政中宇，不肆漂杵之威。

translations.literal: He sweeps filth from the purple pivot, not waiting for the oath at Mingtiao; he consolidates governance within the realm, not resorting to the might that floats pestles.
translations.idiomatic: He sweeps filth from the purple pivot without waiting for the oath at Mingtiao; he consolidates governance within the realm without resorting to the might that floats pestles on the waters.

sentences.zh: 是以墜維再造，虧天重構，幽明裁紀，標配斯光。

translations.literal: Thus the fallen cord of heaven was rewrought, the broken arch of sky rebuilt; dark and bright were given their measure, the standard and allotment made radiant.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the fallen cord of heaven was rewrought and the broken arch of sky rebuilt; dark and bright were given their measure, and the standard and allotment made radiant.

sentences.zh: 而群凶恣虐，協扇童孺，蕞爾東垂，復淪醜跡，邪回從慝，蜂動蟻附。

translations.literal: Yet the pack of villains runs riot, stirring even children to their cause; that little eastern fringe again sinks into foul paths, the crooked trailing after evil, swarming like bees, clinging like ants.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pack of villains runs riot, stirring even children to their cause; that little eastern fringe again sinks into foul paths, the crooked trailing after evil, swarming like bees and clinging like ants.

sentences.zh: 聖圖霆發，神威四臨，羽馹所屆，義旅雲屬，欃鉞所麾，逆徒冰泮，勝負之效，皎然已顯。

translations.literal: The sacred design bursts like thunder; divine might presides on four sides; where swift couriers arrive, righteous armies gather like clouds; where the regent's axe is waved, rebels melt like ice—the outcome of victory and defeat already stands plain.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred design bursts like thunder; divine might presides on four sides. Where swift couriers arrive, righteous armies gather like clouds; where the regent's axe is waved, rebels melt like ice—the outcome of victory and defeat already stands plain.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王英猷冠世，董率元戎。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an, Grand Tutor, surpasses the age in heroic design and leads the main host.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jian'an, Grand Tutor, surpasses the age in heroic design and leads the main host.

sentences.zh: 驃騎山陽王風略夙昭，撫厲中陳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shanyang, Cavalry General, whose style and strategy have long shone, rallies the center ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shanyang, Cavalry General, whose style and strategy have long shone, rallies the center ranks.

sentences.zh: 或振霜江、蠡，或騰焱荊、河，金甲燭天庭，囂聲震海浦。

translations.literal: Some shake frost over the Jiang and Li; others blaze over Jing and the Yellow River; golden armor lights the court of heaven, clamor shakes the sea's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Some shake frost over the Yangtze and Lake Li; others blaze over Jing and the Yellow River. Golden armor lights the court of heaven; clamor shakes the sea's edge.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、吳興太守張永，東南標秀，協贊戎機。

translations.literal: Forward General and Governor of Wuxing Zhang Yong—the finest talent of the southeast—assists in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Forward General and Governor of Wuxing Zhang Yong—the finest talent of the southeast—assists in military planning.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍沈懷明、鎮東中兵參軍劉亮、武衛將軍壽寂之，霜銳五千，熊騰虎步。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming, Middle Army Major on the Eastern Pacification staff Liu Liang, and General of Martial Guard Shou Jizhi—five thousand frost-sharp troops, surging like bears, striding like tigers.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Shen Huaiming, Middle Army Major on the Eastern Pacification staff Liu Liang, and General of Martial Guard Shou Jizhi—five thousand frost-sharp troops, surging like bears and striding like tigers.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍王穆之、龍驤將軍頓生，鐵騎連群，風驅電邁。

translations.literal: Dragon-Crouching Generals Wang Muzhi and Dun Sheng—iron cavalry in unbroken masses, driven by wind, racing like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Crouching Generals Wang Muzhi and Dun Sheng—iron cavalry in unbroken masses, driven by wind and racing like lightning.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍齊王、射聲校尉姚道和，樓艦千艘，覆川蓋汜。

translations.literal: General of the Right Army the Prince of Qi and Commandant of Archers Yao Daohe—a thousand tower ships, covering rivers and brimming over the marshes.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Army the Prince of Qi and Commandant of Archers Yao Daohe—a thousand tower ships covering rivers and brimming over the marshes.

sentences.zh: 左軍垣恭祖、步兵校尉杜幼文、冗從僕射全景文、員外散騎侍郎孫超之，並率虎旅，駱驛雲赴。

translations.literal: Left Army Yuan Gongzu, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Supernumerary Chief of Retainers Quan Jingwen, and Supernumerary Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry Sun Chaozhi—all lead tiger brigades, galloping in like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army Yuan Gongzu, Infantry Commandant Du Youwen, Supernumerary Chief of Retainers Quan Jingwen, and Supernumerary Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry Sun Chaozhi—all lead tiger brigades galloping in like clouds.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍杜敬真、殿中將軍陸攸之、建武將軍吳喜，甲楯一萬，分趣義興。

translations.literal: Palace Generals Du Jingzhen and Lu Youzhi and General Who Establishes Martial Wu Xi—ten thousand armored shields—press toward Yixing by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Generals Du Jingzhen and Lu Youzhi and General Who Establishes Martial Wu Xi—ten thousand armored shields—press toward Yixing by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 予猥承人乏，緫司戎統，聳劍東馳，申憤海曲。

translations.literal: I unworthily fill a gap among men, holding overall command of the army, sword raised eastward, giving voice to wrath along the sea's curve.
translations.idiomatic: I unworthily fill a gap among men, holding overall command of the army, sword raised eastward, giving voice to wrath along the sea's curve.

sentences.zh: 噴氣則白日盡晦，刷馬則清江倒流。

translations.literal: A blast of breath and the bright sun turns wholly dim; a sweep of the horses and the clear river flows backward.
translations.idiomatic: A blast of breath and the bright sun turns wholly dim; a sweep of the horses and the clear river flows backward.

sentences.zh: 以此伐叛，何勍不剿，以此柔服，何順不懷。

translations.literal: With this to crush rebellion, what stronghold will not be destroyed? With this to soothe submission, what loyal state will not incline its heart?
translations.idiomatic: With this to crush rebellion, what stronghold will not be destroyed? With this to win submission, what loyal state will not incline its heart?

sentences.zh: 愍彼群迷，弗辨堯、桀，螳黽微命，擬雷霆之衝；

translations.literal: Pity those deluded masses who cannot tell Yao from Jie—mantis and frog clinging to their paltry lives, matching themselves against thunder's charge;
translations.idiomatic: Pity those deluded masses who cannot tell Yao from Jie—mantis and frog clinging to paltry lives, matching themselves against thunder's charge;

sentences.zh: 已枯之葉，當霜飆之隊。

translations.literal: dry leaves already withered, placed in the path of the frost gale.
translations.idiomatic: dry leaves already withered, placed in the path of the frost gale.

sentences.zh: 尺豎所為寒心，匹婦所為歎息。

translations.literal: Every common man shudders at heart; every peasant woman sighs in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Every common man shudders at heart; every peasant woman sighs in grief.

sentences.zh: 夫因禍致慶，資敗為成，前監不忘，後事明筮。

translations.literal: When calamity brings fortune and defeat breeds success, the warnings of the past are not forgotten; the course ahead is clear as divination.
translations.idiomatic: When calamity brings fortune and defeat breeds success, the warnings of the past are not forgotten; the course ahead is clear as divination.

sentences.zh: 若能相率歸順，投兵效款，則福鍾當年，祉覃來裔，孰如身轘宗屠，鬼餧魂泣者哉！

translations.literal: If you can lead one another in submission, lay down arms and offer loyalty, blessings will ring through your years and fortune reach your descendants—what comparison is there to being dismembered alive, your clan slaughtered, your ghost fed on scraps, your soul weeping?
translations.idiomatic: If you can lead one another in submission, lay down arms and offer loyalty, blessings will ring through your years and fortune reach your descendants—what comparison is there to being dismembered alive, your clan slaughtered, your ghost fed on scraps, your soul weeping?

sentences.zh: 詳鏡安危，自求多福。
