translations.literal: Weigh danger and safety carefully and seek your own abundance of blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh danger and safety carefully and seek your own abundance of blessing.

sentences.zh: 購生禽覬千五百戶開國縣侯；

translations.literal: A bounty for capturing Kong Ji alive: Marquis of a county state with a fief of one thousand five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: A bounty for capturing Kong Ji alive: Marquis of a county state with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 生擒琛千戶開國縣侯。

translations.literal: for capturing Gu Chen alive: Marquis of a county state with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing Gu Chen alive: Marquis of a county state with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 斬送者半賞。

translations.literal: Half the reward for delivery of the severed head.
translations.idiomatic: Half the reward for delivery of the severed head.

sentences.zh: 時將士多是東人，父兄子弟皆已附逆，上因送軍普加宣示曰：「朕方務德簡刑，使四罪不相及，助順同逆者，一以所從為斷。

translations.literal: Most of the officers and troops were easterners; fathers, brothers, sons, and younger kin had already joined the rebels. The emperor therefore sent with the army a general proclamation: "We are devoted to virtue and lenient in punishment, so that the guilt of four crimes shall not reach one another; those who aid the loyal or follow the rebels—we judge by the side each chose.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the officers and troops were easterners; fathers, brothers, sons, and younger kin had already joined the rebels. The emperor therefore sent with the army a general proclamation: "We are devoted to virtue and lenient in punishment, so that the guilt of four crimes shall not reach one another. Those who aid the loyal or follow the rebels—we judge by the side each chose.

sentences.zh: 卿等當深達此懷，勿以親戚為慮也。」

translations.literal: You must grasp this intent deeply and not worry on account of kin."
translations.idiomatic: You must grasp this intent deeply and not worry on account of kin."

sentences.zh: 眾於是大悅。

translations.literal: The troops were greatly heartened.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were greatly heartened.

sentences.zh: 覬所遣孫曇瓘等軍，頓晉陵九里，部陳甚盛。

translations.literal: The army Kong Ji had dispatched under Sun Tanhuan and others halted at Jiuli in Jinling; their formation was very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: The army Kong Ji had dispatched under Sun Tanhuan and others halted at Jiuli in Jinling; their formation was very imposing.

sentences.zh: 懷明至奔牛，所領寡弱，乃築壘自固。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming reached Benniu; the force he commanded was small and weak, so he built fortifications and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming reached Benniu. The force he commanded was small and weak, so he built fortifications and held firm.

sentences.zh: 張永至曲阿，未知懷明安否，百姓驚擾，將士咸欲離散。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e; not knowing whether Huaiming was safe or not, the people grew alarmed and the officers and troops all wished to scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong reached Qu'e. Not knowing whether Huaiming was safe, the people grew alarmed and the officers and troops all wished to scatter.

sentences.zh: 永退還延陵，就休若；

translations.literal: Yong withdrew to Yanling and joined Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: Yong withdrew to Yanling and joined Xiuruo.

sentences.zh: 諸將帥咸勸退保破岡。

translations.literal: All the generals urged retreat to hold Pogang.
translations.idiomatic: All the generals urged retreat to hold Pogang.

sentences.zh: 其日大寒，風雪甚猛，塘埭決壞，眾無固心。

translations.literal: That day was bitterly cold; wind and snow were fierce; dykes and embankments burst; the masses had no firm will.
translations.idiomatic: That day was bitterly cold; wind and snow were fierce; dykes and embankments burst; the masses had no firm will.

sentences.zh: 休若宣令：「敢有言退者，斬！」

translations.literal: Xiuruo proclaimed the order: "Whoever speaks of retreat—behead him!
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo proclaimed the order: "Whoever speaks of retreat—behead him!"

sentences.zh: 眾小定，乃築壘息甲。

translations.literal: The crowd steadied a little, and they built fortifications and rested the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd steadied a little, and they built fortifications and rested the troops.

sentences.zh: 尋得懷明書，賊定未進。

translations.literal: Soon they received word from Huaiming: the rebels had halted and not advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they received word from Huaiming: the rebels had halted and not advanced.

sentences.zh: 軍主劉亮又繼至，兵力轉加，人情乃安。

translations.literal: The army commander Liu Liang also arrived in succession; strength grew by degrees, and men's hearts settled.
translations.idiomatic: The army commander Liu Liang also arrived in succession; strength grew by degrees, and men's hearts settled.

sentences.zh: 時永世令孔景宣復反，柵縣西江峴山，斷遏津徑，劉延熙加其寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: At the time Kong Jingxuan, Magistrate of Yongshi, rebelled again, fortifying Xijiang Xianshan in the county and cutting off the ferry roads; Liu Yanxi made him General Who Pacifies the North as well.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kong Jingxuan, Magistrate of Yongshi, rebelled again, fortifying Xijiang Xianshan in the county and cutting off the ferry roads; Liu Yanxi made him General Who Pacifies the North as well.

sentences.zh: 杜敬真、陸攸之、溧陽令劉休文攻景宣別寨，斬其中兵參軍史覽之等十五人。

translations.literal: Du Jingzhen, Lu Youzhi, and Liu Xiuwen, Magistrate of Liyang, attacked one of Jingxuan's outpost forts and beheaded fifteen men including the Middle Army Major Shi Lanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingzhen, Lu Youzhi, and Liu Xiuwen, Magistrate of Liyang, attacked one of Jingxuan's outpost forts and beheaded fifteen men including the Middle Army Major Shi Lanzhi.

sentences.zh: 永世人徐崇之率鄉里起義，攻縣斬景宣。

translations.literal: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi led local volunteers in an uprising, attacked the county seat, and killed Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chongzhi of Yongshi led local volunteers in an uprising, attacked the county seat, and killed Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 吳喜至，板崇之領縣事。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi arrived, he commissioned Chongzhi to administer the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi arrived, he commissioned Chongzhi to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉休文等誠效，除休文寧朔將軍，縣如故；

translations.literal: Emperor Ming praised the loyal service of Xiuwen and the others; he appointed Xiuwen General Who Pacifies the North, with his magistracy unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming praised the loyal service of Xiuwen and the others; he appointed Xiuwen General Who Pacifies the North, with his magistracy unchanged;

sentences.zh: 崇之殿中將軍，行永世縣事，並賜侯爵。

translations.literal: Chongzhi was made Palace General and acted as Magistrate of Yongshi, and both were granted marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi was made Palace General and acted as Magistrate of Yongshi, and both were granted marquisates.

sentences.zh: 喜、敬真及員外散騎侍郎竺超之等至國山縣界，遇東軍於虎檻村，擊大破之。

translations.literal: Xi, Jingzhen, and the Supernumerary Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry Zhu Chaozhi and others reached the border of Guoshan county and encountered the eastern army at Hujian village; they struck and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Jingzhen, and the Supernumerary Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry Zhu Chaozhi and others reached the border of Guoshan county and encountered the eastern army at Hujian village, striking and routing them utterly.

sentences.zh: 自國山進吳城，去義興十五里。

translations.literal: From Guoshan they advanced on Wucheng, fifteen li from Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: From Guoshan they advanced on Wucheng, fifteen li from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 劉延熙遣楊玄、孫矯之、沈靈秀、黃泰四軍拒喜。

translations.literal: Liu Yanxi sent four armies under Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, Shen Lingxiu, and Huang Tai to oppose Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanxi sent four armies under Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, Shen Lingxiu, and Huang Tai to oppose Xi.

sentences.zh: 喜等兵力甚弱，眾寡勢懸，交戰盡日，臨陳斬楊玄、孫矯之、黃泰，餘眾一時奔走，因進義興南郭外。

translations.literal: Xi and the others were very weak in strength; odds were heavily against them. They fought all day; on the field they cut down Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, and Huang Tai, and the remainder fled at once; they then pressed to the outer south wall of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and the others were very weak in strength; the odds were heavily against them. They fought all day, cut down Yang Xuan, Sun Jiaozhi, and Huang Tai on the field, and the remainder fled at once. They then pressed to the outer south wall of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 延熙屯軍南射堂，喜遣步騎擊之，即退還水北，乃柵斷長橋，保郡自守。

translations.literal: Yanxi encamped his army at the South Archery Hall. Xi sent foot and horse to strike him; Yanxi at once withdrew north of the water, then fortified and cut the long bridge, guarding the commandery in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi encamped his army at the South Archery Hall. Xi sent foot and horse to strike him; Yanxi at once withdrew north of the water, fortified and cut the long bridge, and guarded the commandery in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 喜築壘與之相持。

translations.literal: Xi built fortifications and faced them in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi built fortifications and faced them in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 庾業於長塘湖口夾岸築城，有眾七千餘人，器甲甚盛，與延熙遙相掎角。

translations.literal: Yu Ye built cities on both banks at the mouth of Changtang Lake with more than seven thousand men and abundant armor, coordinating with Yanxi from afar in a pincer grip.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye built cities on both banks at the mouth of Changtang Lake with more than seven thousand men and abundant armor, coordinating with Yanxi from afar in a pincer grip.

sentences.zh: 沈懷明、張永與晉陵軍相持，久不決。

translations.literal: Shen Huaiming and Zhang Yong were locked in stalemate with the Jinling army; for long they could not settle it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiming and Zhang Yong were locked in stalemate with the Jinling army and for long could not settle it.

sentences.zh: 太宗每遣軍，輒多所求須，不時上道。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Ming dispatched troops they made many demands and requirements and did not set out on time.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Ming dispatched troops they made many demands and did not set out on time.

sentences.zh: 外監朱幼舉司徒參軍督護任農夫，驍果有膽力，性又簡率，資給甚易，乃以千人配之，使助東討。

translations.literal: Outer Supervisor Zhu You recommended Ren Nongfu, a staff officer and overseer on the Grand Tutor's staff—bold and fierce, spirited and courageous, by nature plain and direct, very easy to supply. A thousand men were assigned to him to assist in the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Supervisor Zhu You recommended Ren Nongfu, a staff officer and overseer on the Grand Tutor's staff—bold and fierce, spirited and courageous, plain and direct by nature, and very easy to supply. A thousand men were assigned to him to assist in the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 時庾業兵盛，農夫於延陵出長塘，雖云千兵，至者裁四百。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Ye's army was strong. Nongfu left Yanling for Changtang; though a thousand troops were spoken of, only four hundred actually arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yu Ye's army was strong. Nongfu left Yanling for Changtang; though a thousand troops were spoken of, only four hundred actually arrived.

sentences.zh: 未至數十里，遣人參候，云：「賊築城猶未合。」

translations.literal: Before he had gone several dozen li, he sent scouts ahead, who reported: "The rebels are building fortifications but the walls are not yet joined."
translations.idiomatic: Before he had gone several dozen li, he sent scouts ahead, who reported: "The rebels are building fortifications but the walls are not yet joined.

sentences.zh: 農夫率廣武將軍高志之、永興令徐崇之馳往攻之。

translations.literal: Nongfu led General of Expansive Might Gao Zhizhi and Xu Chongzhi, Magistrate of Yongxing, in a galloping attack.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu led General of Expansive Might Gao Zhizhi and Xu Chongzhi, Magistrate of Yongxing, in a galloping attack.

sentences.zh: 因其城壘未立，農夫親持刀楯，赴城入陳，大破之，庾業棄城走義興。

translations.literal: Because the fortifications were not yet complete, Nongfu himself took up shield and blade, rushed into the wall and into the formation, and routed them utterly; Yu Ye abandoned the city and fled to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Because the fortifications were not yet complete, Nongfu himself took up shield and blade, rushed into the wall and into the formation, and routed them utterly. Yu Ye abandoned the city and fled to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 先是，龍驤將軍阮佃夫募得蜀人數百，多壯勇便戰，皆著犀皮鎧，執短兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dragon-Crouching General Ruan Tianfu had recruited several hundred Shu men—mostly stout, brave, and handy in battle—all wearing rhinoceros-hide armor and wielding short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Dragon-Crouching General Ruan Tianfu had recruited several hundred Shu men—mostly stout, brave, and handy in battle—all wearing rhinoceros-hide armor and wielding short weapons.

sentences.zh: 本應就佃夫向晉陵，未發，會農夫須人，分以配之。

translations.literal: They were originally to join Tianfu and march on Jinling; before they set out, Nongfu needed men and a portion was assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: They were originally to join Tianfu and march on Jinling; before they set out, Nongfu needed men and a portion was assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 及戰，每先登，東人並畏憚，又怪其形飾殊異，舊傳狐獠食人，每見之，輒奔走。

translations.literal: In battle they always led the assault. The easterners all feared them and were also struck by their strange appearance and gear; old tales told that the fox-tribes ate men—whenever they saw them, they would flee.
translations.idiomatic: In battle they always led the assault. The easterners all feared them and were also struck by their strange appearance and gear; old tales told that the fox-tribes ate men, and whenever they saw them they would flee.

sentences.zh: 農夫收其船杖，與高志之進義興援吳喜。

translations.literal: Nongfu took their boats and gear and, with Gao Zhizhi, advanced on Yixing to reinforce Wu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu took their boats and gear and, with Gao Zhizhi, advanced on Yixing to reinforce Wu Xi.

sentences.zh: 二月一日，喜乃度水攻郡，分兵擊諸壘柵。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, Xi crossed the water and attacked the commandery seat, dividing his forces to strike the various fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month, Xi crossed the water and attacked the commandery seat, dividing his forces to strike the various fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 農夫雖至，眾力尚少，兵勢不敵。

translations.literal: Though Nongfu had arrived, their combined strength was still small; their military power did not match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Though Nongfu had arrived, their combined strength was still small and did not match the enemy.

sentences.zh: 喜乃與數騎登高東西指麾，若招引四面俱進者。

translations.literal: Xi then rode up high ground with a few horsemen and directed east and west as if summoning advance from all four sides at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then rode up high ground with a few horsemen and directed east and west as if summoning advance from all four sides at once.

sentences.zh: 東軍大駭，諸營一時奔散，唯龍驤將軍孔叡一柵未拔。

translations.literal: The eastern army was greatly terrified; all camps fled at once. Only the fort of Dragon-Crouching General Kong Rui was not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army was greatly terrified; all camps fled at once. Only the fort of Dragon-Crouching General Kong Rui was not yet taken.

sentences.zh: 喜以殺傷者多，乃開圍緩之。

translations.literal: Xi, because many had been killed and wounded, thereupon lifted the siege and eased pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how many had been killed and wounded, Xi lifted the siege and eased the pressure.

sentences.zh: 其夜，庾業、孔叡相率奔走，義興平。

translations.literal: That night, Yu Ye and Kong Rui fled together in flight; Yixing was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yu Ye and Kong Rui fled together, and Yixing was pacified.

sentences.zh: 劉延熙投水死，有人告之，乃斬尸，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: Liu Yanxi drowned himself; when someone reported it, they beheaded the corpse and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanxi drowned himself. When someone reported it, the body was beheaded and the head sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 義興諸縣唯綏安令巢邃秉節不移，不受偽爵。

translations.literal: Among the counties of Yixing, only Chao Sui, magistrate of Suian, held fast to integrity and would not accept a rebel title.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the counties in Yixing, only Chao Sui, magistrate of Suian, held firm to his integrity and refused a rebel title.

sentences.zh: 時齊王率軍東討，與張永、劉亮、杜幼文、沈懷明等於晉陵九里西結營，與東軍相持。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi led troops eastward in punitive campaign; with Zhang Yong, Liu Liang, Du Youwen, Shen Huaiming, and others he encamped west of Jiuli in Jinling and held stalemate against the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Qi led an army east in punitive campaign. With Zhang Yong, Liu Liang, Du Youwen, Shen Huaiming, and the rest he encamped west of Jiuli in Jinling and held the eastern army at bay.

sentences.zh: 義興軍既為吳喜等所破，奔散者多投晉陵，東軍震恐。

translations.literal: The Yixing army having been broken by Wu Xi and the others, many of the fugitive and scattered troops fled to Jinling, and the eastern army was stricken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Yixing army having been shattered by Wu Xi and the others, many fugitives fled to Jinling, and the eastern army was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 上又遣積射將軍江方興、南臺御史王道隆至晉陵視賊形勢。

translations.literal: The throne also dispatched General Who Shoots at a Distance Jiang Fangxing and Censor of the Southern Bureau Wang Daolong to Jinling to reconnoiter the rebel situation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also sent General Who Shoots at a Distance Jiang Fangxing and Censor of the Southern Bureau Wang Daolong to Jinling to assess the rebel position.

sentences.zh: 賊帥孫曇瓘、程捍宗、陳景遠凡有五城，互相連帶；

translations.literal: The rebel commanders Sun Tanjuan, Cheng Hanzong, and Chen Jingyuan held five walled towns in all, mutually linked in defense;
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commanders Sun Tanjuan, Cheng Hanzong, and Chen Jingyuan held five walled towns in all, linked in mutual defense;

sentences.zh: 捍宗城猶未固。

translations.literal: Hanzong's fort was not yet fully secured.
translations.idiomatic: and Hanzong's fort was not yet fully secured.

sentences.zh: 其月三日，道隆與齊王、張永共議：「捍宗城既未立，可以籍手。

translations.literal: On the third of that month, Daolong consulted with the Prince of Qi and Zhang Yong: "Since Hanzong's fort is not yet established, we can avail ourselves of the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of that month, Daolong consulted with the Prince of Qi and Zhang Yong: "Hanzong's fort is not yet finished—we can seize the chance.

sentences.zh: 上副聖旨，下成眾氣。」

translations.literal: Above it fulfills the sacred charge; below it will consolidate the troops' morale."
translations.idiomatic: Above, it will fulfill the sacred charge; below, it will rally the troops' spirits."

sentences.zh: 道隆便率所領急攻之，俄頃城陷，斬捍宗首。

translations.literal: Daolong then led his command in a swift assault; in a moment the fort fell and Hanzong's head was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong then led his command in a swift assault. In a moment the fort fell and Hanzong's head was taken.

sentences.zh: 劉亮果勁，便刀楯，朝士先不相悉，上亦弗聞，唯尚書左丞徐爰知之，白太宗，稱其驍敢。

translations.literal: Liu Liang was resolute and fierce, skilled with blade and shield. Court officials had not known him before, nor had the throne heard of him; only Xu Ai, Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing, knew him, reported to Emperor Ming, and praised his boldness and daring.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang was resolute and fierce, skilled with blade and shield. Court officials had not known him, nor had the throne heard of him. Only Xu Ai, Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing, knew him, reported to Emperor Ming, and praised his boldness and daring.

sentences.zh: 至是，每戰以刀楯直蕩，往輒陷決，張永嫌其過銳，不令居前。

translations.literal: By this time, in every battle he charged straight ahead with blade and shield and wherever he went the enemy lines gave way; Zhang Yong, finding him too reckless, would not allow him to take the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: By then, in every battle he charged straight ahead with blade and shield, and wherever he went the enemy lines gave way. Zhang Yong, finding him too reckless, would not let him take the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賊連柵周亙，塘道迫狹，將士力不得展，亮乃負楯而進，直入重柵，眾軍因之，即皆摧破。

translations.literal: The rebels' linked palisades stretched all around; the canal paths were narrow and cramped, so the officers and soldiers could not deploy their strength. Liang then advanced bearing his shield on his back, plunged straight into the inner palisades, and the rest of the army followed—at once everything was smashed apart.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' linked palisades stretched all around, and the canal paths were so narrow that the troops could not bring their strength to bear. Liang advanced with his shield on his back, plunged straight into the inner palisades, and the rest of the army followed—at once everything was smashed apart.

sentences.zh: 袁標遣千人繼至，齊王與永等乘勝馳擊，又大破之，屠其兩城。

translations.literal: Yuan Biao sent a thousand men as reinforcements; the Prince of Qi and Yong and the others pressed the victory in a galloping attack, routed them again, and sacked two of their forts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Biao sent a thousand men as reinforcements. The Prince of Qi, Yong, and the others pressed the victory in a galloping attack, routed them again, and sacked two of their forts.

sentences.zh: 曇瓘率眾數百，鼓噪而至，標又遣千人繼之，眾軍駭懼，將欲散矣。

translations.literal: Tanjuan led several hundred men, beating drums and shouting as he came; Biao sent another thousand as reinforcement. The army was terrified and was on the verge of scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Tanjuan led several hundred men, beating drums and shouting as he came, and Biao sent another thousand in support. The army was terrified and on the verge of scattering.

sentences.zh: 江方興率勇士迎射之，應弦倒者相繼，曇瓘因此敗走。

translations.literal: Jiang Fangxing led warriors to meet them and shoot; men fell one after another at the twang of the bowstring, and Tanjuan broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fangxing led his warriors to meet them and shoot. Men fell one after another at the twang of the bowstring, and Tanjuan broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 吳喜軍至義鄉，偽輔國將軍、車騎司馬孔璪屯吳興南亭，太守王曇生詣璪計事，會信還，云：「臺軍已近。」

translations.literal: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang. Kong Zan, rebel General Who Assists the State and Cavalry-and-Chariot Major, was stationed at Nanting in Wuxing. Administrator Wang Tansheng went to Zan to discuss affairs; just then a messenger returned with word: "The court army is near."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's army reached Yixiang. Kong Zan, the rebel General Who Assists the State and Cavalry-and-Chariot Major, was stationed at Nanting in Wuxing. Administrator Wang Tansheng went to Zan to discuss affairs when a messenger returned with word: "The court army is near."

sentences.zh: 璪大懼，墮床，曰：「懸賞所購，唯我而已，今不遽走，將為人禽。」

translations.literal: Zan was greatly terrified, fell from his bed, and said: "The posted bounty is offered for me alone; if I do not flee at once, I shall be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Zan was stricken with terror, fell from his bed, and said, "The posted bounty is for me alone. If I do not flee at once, I shall be taken alive."

sentences.zh: 左右聞之，並各散走。

translations.literal: When those around him heard this, each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When those around him heard this, each scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 璪與曇生焚燒倉庫，東奔錢塘。

translations.literal: Zan and Tansheng burned the granaries and fled east to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and Tansheng burned the granaries and fled east to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 喜至吳興，頓置郡城，倉廩遇雨不然，無所損失。

translations.literal: When Xi reached Wuxing he halted in the commandery seat; the storehouses, though drenched by rain, did not catch fire, and nothing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi reached Wuxing he halted in the commandery seat. The storehouses, though drenched by rain, did not catch fire, and nothing was lost.

sentences.zh: 初，曇生遣寧朔將軍沈靈寵率八千人向黃鵠嶠，欲從候道出蕪湖，迎接南軍。

translations.literal: Earlier Tansheng had dispatched General Who Pacifies the North Shen Lingchong with eight thousand men toward Huangque Ridge, intending to reach Wuhu by a bypath and receive the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tansheng had dispatched General Who Pacifies the North Shen Lingchong with eight thousand men toward Huangque Ridge, intending to reach Wuhu by a bypath and link up with the southern army.

sentences.zh: 廣德令王蘊發兵據嶮，靈寵不得進，屯住故鄣。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, magistrate of Guangde, raised troops and held the passes; Lingchong could not advance and encamped at Guzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, magistrate of Guangde, raised troops and held the passes. Lingchong could not advance and encamped at Guzhang.

sentences.zh: 曇生既走，靈寵乃與弟靈昭、軍副姚天覆率偏裨以下十七軍歸順。

translations.literal: After Tansheng had fled, Lingchong with his younger brother Lingzhao and the army adjutant Yao Tianfu led seventeen subordinate commands and below in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Tansheng fled, Lingchong, together with his younger brother Lingzhao and army adjutant Yao Tianfu, led seventeen subordinate commands and below in surrender.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，擢為鎮東參軍事，因率所領東討。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming commended this and promoted him to Army Staff Officer of the Army That Pacifies the East; he then led his command east in punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming commended this and promoted him to Army Staff Officer of the Army That Pacifies the East, and he then led his command east in punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 喜分遣軍主沈思仁、吳係公追躡璪等。

translations.literal: Xi separately dispatched commanders Shen Siren and Wu Xigong in pursuit of Zan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xi separately dispatched commanders Shen Siren and Wu Xigong in pursuit of Zan and the others.

sentences.zh: 陸攸之、任農夫自東遷進向吳郡，臺遣軍主張靈符即晉陵。

translations.literal: Lu Youzhi and Ren Nongfu advanced from Dongqian toward Wu Commandery; the court sent commander Zhang Lingfu straight to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youzhi and Ren Nongfu advanced from Dongqian toward Wu Commandery, while the court sent commander Zhang Lingfu straight to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 其月四日，齊王急攻之。

translations.literal: On the fourth of that month, the Prince of Qi pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth of that month the Prince of Qi pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 其夜，孫曇瓘、陳景遠一時奔潰。

translations.literal: That night Sun Tanjuan and Chen Jingyuan broke and fled all at once.
translations.idiomatic: That night Sun Tanjuan and Chen Jingyuan broke and fled all at once.

sentences.zh: 諸軍至晉陵，袁標棄郡東走。

translations.literal: When the armies reached Jinling, Yuan Biao abandoned the commandery and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies reached Jinling, Yuan Biao abandoned the commandery and fled east.

sentences.zh: 晉陵既平，吳中震動。

translations.literal: With Jinling pacified, the Wu region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: With Jinling pacified, the Wu region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 吳興軍又將至，顧琛與子寶素攜其老母泛海奔會稽，海鹽令王孚邀討不及。

translations.literal: The Wuxing army was about to arrive as well; Gu Chen, together with his son Baosu, took his elderly mother and fled by sea toward Kuaiji; Wang Fu, magistrate of Haiyan, attempted to intercept them but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing army was about to arrive as well. Gu Chen, together with his son Baosu, took his elderly mother and fled by sea toward Kuaiji. Wang Fu, magistrate of Haiyan, attempted to intercept them but could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 太宗以四郡平定，留吳喜統全景文、沈懷明、劉亮、孫超之、壽寂之等東平會稽，追齊王、張永、姚道和、杜幼文、垣恭祖、張靈符北討，王穆之、頓生、江方興南伐。

translations.literal: Since the four commanderies were pacified, Emperor Ming left Wu Xi to command Quan Jingwen, Shen Huaiming, Liu Liang, Sun Chaozhi, Shou Jizhi, and the rest to pacify Kuaiji in the east; he sent the Prince of Qi, Zhang Yong, Yao Daohuo, Du Youwen, Yuan Gongzu, and Zhang Lingfu north in punitive campaign; and Wang Muzhi, Dun Sheng, and Jiang Fangxing south in conquest.
translations.idiomatic: With the four commanderies pacified, Emperor Ming left Wu Xi to command Quan Jingwen, Shen Huaiming, Liu Liang, Sun Chaozhi, Shou Jizhi, and the rest in the east to pacify Kuaiji, while sending the Prince of Qi, Zhang Yong, Yao Daohuo, Du Youwen, Yuan Gongzu, and Zhang Lingfu north in punitive campaign and Wang Muzhi, Dun Sheng, and Jiang Fangxing south in conquest.

sentences.zh: 其月九日，喜等至錢唐，錢唐令顧昱及孔璪、王曇生等奔渡江東。

translations.literal: On the ninth of that month, Xi and the others reached Qiantang; Gu Yu, magistrate of Qiantang, together with Kong Zan, Wang Tansheng, and the rest fled across the river to the eastern bank.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth of that month Xi and the others reached Qiantang. Gu Yu, magistrate of Qiantang, together with Kong Zan, Wang Tansheng, and the rest fled across the river to the eastern bank.

sentences.zh: 喜仍進軍柳浦，諸暨令傅琰將家歸順。

translations.literal: Xi continued the advance to Liupu; Fu Yan, magistrate of Zhuji, brought his household in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xi continued the advance to Liupu. Fu Yan, magistrate of Zhuji, brought his household in surrender.

sentences.zh: 喜遣鎮北參軍沈思仁、彊弩將軍任農夫、龍驤將軍高志之、南臺御史阮佃夫、揚武將軍盧僧澤等率軍向黃山浦。

translations.literal: Xi dispatched Army Staff Officer of the Army That Pacifies the North Shen Siren, General of Strong Crossbows Ren Nongfu, Dragon-cavalry General Gao Zhizhi, Censor of the Southern Bureau Ruan Dianfu, General Who Displays Martial Might Lu Sengze, and others with troops toward Huangshan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Xi dispatched Army Staff Officer of the Army That Pacifies the North Shen Siren, General of Strong Crossbows Ren Nongfu, Dragon-cavalry General Gao Zhizhi, Censor of the Southern Bureau Ruan Dianfu, General Who Displays Martial Might Lu Sengze, and others with troops toward Huangshan Ford.

sentences.zh: 東軍據岸結寨，農夫等攻破之，乘風舉帆，直趣定山，破其大帥孫會之，於陳斬首。

translations.literal: The eastern army held the shore and built stockades; Nongfu and the others broke them, spread sail with the wind, and drove straight for Dingshan; they defeated their commander-in-chief Sun Huizhi and beheaded him on the field.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army held the shore and built stockades. Nongfu and the others broke them, spread sail with the wind, and drove straight for Dingshan, where they defeated their commander-in-chief Sun Huizhi and beheaded him on the field.

sentences.zh: 自定山進向漁浦，戍主孔叡率千餘人據壘拒戰。

translations.literal: From Dingshan they advanced toward Yupu; the garrison commander Kong Rui led more than a thousand men to hold a fort and resist.
translations.idiomatic: From Dingshan they advanced toward Yupu. Garrison commander Kong Rui led more than a thousand men to hold a fort and resist.

sentences.zh: 佃夫使隊主闕法炬射殺樓上弩手，叡眾驚駭，思仁縱兵攻之，斬其軍主孔奴，於是敗散。

translations.literal: Dianfu had squad leader Que Fajie shoot and kill the crossbowmen on the tower; Rui's troops were stricken with terror; Siren unleashed his troops in assault, beheaded their army commander Kong Nu, and they thereupon broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Dianfu had squad leader Que Fajie shoot and kill the crossbowmen on the tower. Rui's troops were stricken with terror. Siren unleashed his troops in assault, beheaded their army commander Kong Nu, and they thereupon broke and scattered.

sentences.zh: 其月十九日，吳喜使劉亮由鹽官海渡，直指同浦；

translations.literal: On the nineteenth of that month, Wu Xi had Liu Liang cross by sea from Yanguan and drive straight for Tongpu;
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth of that month Wu Xi had Liu Liang cross by sea from Yanguan and drive straight for Tongpu;

sentences.zh: 壽寂之濟自漁浦，邪趣永興；

translations.literal: Shou Jizhi crossed from Yupu and struck obliquely toward Yongxing;
translations.idiomatic: Shou Jizhi crossed from Yupu and struck obliquely toward Yongxing;

sentences.zh: 喜自柳浦渡，趣西陵。

translations.literal: Xi himself crossed from Liupu and made for Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: and Xi himself crossed from Liupu and made for Xiling.

sentences.zh: 西陵諸軍皆悉散潰，斬庾業、顧法直、吳恭，傳首京都。

translations.literal: The armies at Xiling all broke and scattered; Yu Ye, Gu Fazhi, and Wu Gong were beheaded and their heads sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The armies at Xiling all broke and scattered. Yu Ye, Gu Fazhi, and Wu Gong were beheaded and their heads sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 東軍主卜道濟、督戰許天賜請降。

translations.literal: The eastern army commanders Bu Daoji and battle supervisor Xu Tianci asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army commanders Bu Daoji and battle supervisor Xu Tianci asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 庾業，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Ye was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ye was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 父彥達，以幹局為太祖所知，為益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yanda was known to Emperor Wen for his capacity and competence, and served as Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanda was known to Emperor Wen for his capacity and competence and served as Inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，官至豫章太守，太常卿。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xiaowu he reached the posts of Administrator of Yuzhang and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Xiaowu he rose to Administrator of Yuzhang and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 劉亮、全景文、孫超之進次永興同市，遇覬所遣陸孝伯、孔豫兩軍，與戰破之，斬孝伯、豫首。

translations.literal: Liu Liang, Quan Jingwen, and Sun Chaozhi advanced and halted at Tongshi in Yongxing; they met the two armies sent by Yi—those of Lu Xiaobo and Kong Yu—defeated them in battle, and beheaded Xiaobo and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang, Quan Jingwen, and Sun Chaozhi advanced and halted at Tongshi in Yongxing. They met the two armies Yi had sent—those of Lu Xiaobo and Kong Yu—defeated them in battle, and beheaded Xiaobo and Yu.

sentences.zh: 會稽聞西軍稍近，將士多奔亡，覬不能復制。

translations.literal: When Kuaiji learned that the western army was drawing near, officers and soldiers fled in large numbers; Yi could no longer restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaiji learned that the western army was drawing near, officers and soldiers fled in large numbers, and Yi could no longer restrain them.

sentences.zh: 二十日，上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，覬以東西交逼，憂遽不知所為。

translations.literal: On the twentieth, Wang Yan, magistrate of Shangyu, raised troops and attacked the commandery seat; Yi, pressed from east and west, was anxious and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth Wang Yan, magistrate of Shangyu, raised troops and attacked the commandery seat. Yi, pressed from east and west, was anxious and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 其夕，率千餘人聲云東討，實趣石瀃。

translations.literal: That evening he led more than a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern punitive campaign, but in truth he made for Shidu.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he led more than a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern punitive campaign, but in truth made for Shidu.

sentences.zh: 先已具船海浦，值潮涸不得去，眾叛都盡，門生載以小船，竄於脊山村。

translations.literal: He had already prepared boats on the sea shore, but the tide was out and he could not depart; his followers all deserted him; a student bore him off in a small boat and he hid on Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: He had already prepared boats on the seashore, but the tide was out and he could not depart. His followers all deserted him. A student bore him off in a small boat, and he hid on Jishan.

sentences.zh: 偽車騎從事中郎張綏先遣人於錢唐詣喜歸誠，及覬走，綏閉封倉庫，以待王師。

translations.literal: Zhang Sui, rebel Staff Officer of the Masters of Cavalry, had already sent a man to Qiantang to declare loyalty to Xi; when Yi fled, Sui sealed the storehouses and awaited the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sui, the rebel Staff Officer of the Masters of Cavalry, had already sent a man to Qiantang to declare loyalty to Xi. When Yi fled, Sui sealed the storehouses and awaited the royal army.

sentences.zh: 二十一日，晏至郡，入自北門，囚綏付作部，其夜殺之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first, Yan reached the commandery seat, entered by the north gate, imprisoned Sui and handed him to the construction office; that night he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first Yan reached the commandery seat, entered by the north gate, imprisoned Sui and handed him to the construction office. That night Sui was executed.

sentences.zh: 執尋陽王子房於別署，縱兵大掠，府庫空盡。

translations.literal: He seized Xunyang Prince Zifang in a separate building, let the troops plunder freely, and the treasury was emptied entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Xunyang Prince Zifang in a separate building, let the troops plunder freely, and the treasury was emptied entirely.

sentences.zh: 若邪村民錄送偽龍驤將軍、車騎中兵參軍軍主孔叡，將斬之。

translations.literal: Villagers of Ruoye captured and sent Kong Rui, rebel Dragon-cavalry General, Army Staff Officer of the Cavalry-and-Chariot Major, and army commander, intending to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers of Ruoye captured and sent in Kong Rui, the rebel Dragon-cavalry General, Army Staff Officer of the Cavalry-and-Chariot Major, and army commander, intending to execute him.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「吾年已過立，未沾官伍，蒙知己之顧，以身許之。

translations.literal: Rui said: "I am past the age of standing upright yet never entered official ranks; having received my patron's regard, I pledged my life to him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "I am past the age of standing upright yet never entered official ranks. Having received my patron's regard, I pledged my life to him.

sentences.zh: 今日就死，亦何所恨！」

translations.literal: To die today—what is there to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: To die today—what is there to regret!"

sentences.zh: 含笑就戮。

translations.literal: He went to execution smiling.
translations.idiomatic: He went to execution smiling.

sentences.zh: 孔璪叛投門生陸林夫，林夫斬首送之。

translations.literal: Kong Zan, betrayed, took refuge with his student Lu Linfu; Linfu beheaded him and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zan, abandoned, took refuge with his student Lu Linfu. Linfu beheaded him and sent the head.

sentences.zh: 二十二日，脊山民縛覬送詣晏，晏謂之曰：「此事孔璪所為，無豫卿事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second, the people of Jishan bound Yi and sent him to Yan; Yan said to him: "This was Kong Zan's doing; you had no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second the people of Jishan bound Yi and sent him to Yan. Yan said to him, "This was Kong Zan's doing. You had no part in it.

sentences.zh: 可作首辭，當相為申上。」

translations.literal: You may make the primary confession and I will report upward on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: You may make the primary confession and I will report upward on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 覬曰：「江東處分，莫不由身，委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Every disposition in Jiangdong was mine alone; to shift blame and beg for life—that is your sort's way of thinking!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Every disposition in Jiangdong was mine alone. To shift blame and beg for life—that is your sort's way of thinking!"

sentences.zh: 晏乃斬之東閣外。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon beheaded him outside the eastern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thereupon beheaded him outside the eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 臨死求酒，曰：「此是平生所好。」

translations.literal: Facing death he asked for wine and said: "This was what I loved all my life."
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he asked for wine and said, "This was what I loved all my life."

sentences.zh: 時年五十一。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等並詣喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。

translations.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and the others all came to Xi to submit and accept blame; Xi pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and the others all came to Xi to submit and accept blame. Xi pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 琛子寶素與父相失，自縊死。

translations.literal: Chen's son Baosu, separated from his father, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Baosu, separated from his father, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陳斬十七人，其餘皆原宥。

translations.literal: The eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded on the field, and the rest were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all. Seventeen were beheaded on the field, and the rest were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 初，遣庾業向會稽，追使奉朝請孫長度送仗與之，並令召募。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yu Ye was sent toward Kuaiji, a pursuing envoy, Palace Attendant Sun Changdu, was sent to deliver weapons to him and also ordered to raise recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yu Ye was sent toward Kuaiji, a pursuing envoy, Palace Attendant Sun Changdu, was dispatched to deliver weapons to him and also ordered to raise recruits.

sentences.zh: 行達晉陵，袁標就其求仗，長度不與，為標所殺。

translations.literal: When he reached Jinling, Yuan Biao asked him for weapons; Changdu refused and was killed by Biao.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jinling, Yuan Biao asked him for weapons. Changdu refused and was killed by Biao.

sentences.zh: 追贈給事中。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the post of Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the post of Attendant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄧琬遣臨川內史張淹自南路出東陽，淹遣龍驤將軍桂遑、征西行參軍劉越緒屯據定陽縣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Deng Wan had dispatched Interior Minister of Linchuan Zhang Yan southward through Dongyang; Yan sent Dragon-cavalry General Gui Huang and Western Campaign Staff Officer Liu Yuexu to occupy and hold Dingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Deng Wan had dispatched Interior Minister of Linchuan Zhang Yan southward through Dongyang. Yan sent Dragon-cavalry General Gui Huang and Western Campaign Staff Officer Liu Yuexu to occupy and hold Dingyang County.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若遣沈思仁討之，思仁遣軍主崔公烈攻其營，斬幢主朱伯符首，桂遑、劉越緒諸軍並奔逸。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuruo of Baling dispatched Shen Siren to punish them; Siren sent commander Cui Gonglie to attack their camp, beheaded the standard-bearer Zhu Bofu, and the armies of Gui Huang, Liu Yuexu, and the rest all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuruo of Baling dispatched Shen Siren to punish them. Siren sent commander Cui Gonglie to attack their camp, beheaded the standard-bearer Zhu Bofu, and the armies of Gui Huang, Liu Yuexu, and the rest all fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 晉安太守劉瞻據郡同逆，建安內史趙道生起義討之，聚徒未合。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, Administrator of Jin'an, held the commandery in rebellion; Zhao Daosheng, Interior Minister of Jian'an, rose in righteous campaign to punish him, but his gathered followers had not yet united.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, Administrator of Jin'an, held the commandery in rebellion. Zhao Daosheng, Interior Minister of Jian'an, rose in righteous campaign to punish him, but his gathered followers had not yet united.

sentences.zh: 七月，思仁遣軍主姚宏祖、鮑伯奮、應寄生等討破瞻，斬之於羅江縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Siren dispatched commanders Yao Hongzu, Bao Bofen, and Ying Jisheng to defeat Zhan and beheaded him in Luojiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Siren dispatched commanders Yao Hongzu, Bao Bofen, and Ying Jisheng to defeat Zhan and beheaded him in Luojiang County.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬先遣新安太守陽伯子及軍主任獻子襲黟縣，縣令吳茹公固守，力不敵，棄城走，伯子等屯據縣城。

translations.literal: Deng Wan had earlier dispatched Administrator of Xin'an Yang Bozi and army commander Ren Xianzi to raid Yi County; Magistrate Wu Rugu held firm, but his strength was insufficient and he abandoned the city and fled; Bozi and the others occupied and held the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan had earlier dispatched Administrator of Xin'an Yang Bozi and army commander Ren Xianzi to raid Yi County. Magistrate Wu Rugu held firm, but his strength was insufficient and he abandoned the city and fled. Bozi and the others occupied and held the county seat.

sentences.zh: 茹公與臺軍主丘敬文、李靈賜、蕭柏壽等攻圍彌時，八月乃克，斬伯子、獻子首。

translations.literal: Rugu, together with court commanders Qiu Jingwen, Li Lingci, and Xiao Baishou, besieged them for a long time; in the eighth month they took the city and beheaded Bozi and Xianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Rugu, together with court commanders Qiu Jingwen, Li Lingci, and Xiao Baishou, besieged them for a long time. In the eighth month they took the city and beheaded Bozi and Xianzi.

sentences.zh: 張淹屯軍上饒縣，聞劉胡敗，軍副鄱陽太守費曇欲圖之，詐云：「得鄧琬信，急宜諮論。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yan was encamped at Shangrao County; when he heard that Liu Hu had been defeated, Fei Tan, army adjutant and Administrator of Poyang, wished to plot against him and falsely said: "I have received a letter from Deng Wan and must consult urgently."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan was encamped at Shangrao County. When he heard that Liu Hu had been defeated, Fei Tan, army adjutant and Administrator of Poyang, wished to plot against him and falsely said, "I have received a letter from Deng Wan and must consult urgently."

sentences.zh: 欲因此斬淹。

translations.literal: He intended thereby to behead Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He intended thereby to behead Yan.

sentences.zh: 淹素事佛，方禮佛，不得時進。

translations.literal: Yan had long been devoted to Buddhism and was just then worshipping the Buddha, so he could not enter at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had long been devoted to Buddhism and was just then worshipping the Buddha, so he could not enter at once.

sentences.zh: 曇復誑云捕虎，借大鼓及仗士二百人，淹信而與之。

translations.literal: Tan deceived him again, saying they were hunting a tiger, and borrowed a great drum and two hundred armed men; Yan believed him and lent them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan deceived him again, saying they were hunting a tiger, and borrowed a great drum and two hundred armed men. Yan believed him and lent them.

sentences.zh: 曇因率眾入山，饗士約誓，揚言虎走城西，鳴鼓大呼，直來趣城；

translations.literal: Tan then led the troops into the hills, feasted the men and bound them by oath, proclaimed that the tiger had fled west of the city, beat the drum and shouted loudly, and came straight for the city;
translations.idiomatic: Tan then led the troops into the hills, feasted the men and bound them by oath, proclaimed that the tiger had fled west of the city, beat the drum and shouted loudly, and came straight for the city.

sentences.zh: 城門守衛，悉委仗觀之，曇率眾突入，淹正禮佛，聞難走出，因斬首。

translations.literal: the gate guards all cast aside their weapons to watch; Tan led his troops in a sudden rush; Yan was just worshipping the Buddha, heard the alarm and fled out, and was thereupon beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards all cast aside their weapons to watch. Tan led his troops in a sudden rush. Yan was just worshipping the Buddha, heard the alarm and fled out, and was thereupon beheaded.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自江左以來，舉干戈以圖宗國，十有一焉，其能克振者，四而已矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Since the establishment of the realm south of the Yangtze, men have raised arms against the imperial lineage eleven times; of these, only four succeeded in restoring order.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Since the realm south of the Yangtze was established, men have raised arms against the imperial lineage eleven times. Of these, only four succeeded in restoring order.

sentences.zh: 元皇外守虛器，政由王氏；

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan held an empty vessel without, while power lay with the Wang clan;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan held an empty vessel without, while power lay with the Wang clan;

sentences.zh: 蘇峻事雖暫申，旋受屠磔；

translations.literal: Su Jun's cause enjoyed only a brief triumph and he was soon torn apart on the rack;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's cause enjoyed only a brief triumph and he was soon torn apart on the rack;

sentences.zh: 桓玄宣武之子，運屬橫流；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was the son of Huan Wen, who bore the posthumous title Xuanwu; his fortune fell in an age of sweeping chaos;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was the son of Huan Wen, who bore the posthumous title Xuanwu; his fortune fell in an age of sweeping chaos;

sentences.zh: 世祖仗順入討，民無異望。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu marched in accord with righteousness to punish rebellion, and the people had no divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu marched in accord with righteousness to punish rebellion, and the people had no divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆漆顙夷宗，作戒於後，何哉？

translations.literal: All the rest were branded on the forehead and their clans exterminated, setting a warning for those after—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: All the rest were branded on the forehead and their clans exterminated, setting a warning for those after—why is this?

sentences.zh: 夫勝敗之數，實由眾心，社廟尊嚴，民情所係，安以義動，猶或稱難，況長戟指闕，志在陵暴者乎！

translations.literal: For the calculus of victory and defeat rests truly upon the people's hearts. The dignity of the altars of soil and grain is what the people's sentiment attaches to; even when roused by righteousness it may still be called arduous—how much more when spears are pointed at the palace gates and the aim is brutal domination!
translations.idiomatic: The calculus of victory and defeat rests truly upon the people's hearts. The dignity of the altars of soil and grain is what the people's sentiment attaches to. Even when roused by righteousness the task may still be called arduous—how much more when spears are pointed at the palace gates and the aim is brutal domination!

sentences.zh: 泰始交爭，逆順未辨，太宗身劋悖亂，事惟拯溺，國道屯詖，宜立長君，太祖之昭，義無不可。

translations.literal: In the Taishi struggle right and wrong were not yet clear; Emperor Ming himself cut down rebellion and disorder, his business was only to rescue the drowning. The state road was obstructed and bent—it was fitting to establish an elder sovereign; among Emperor Wen's sons born to the legitimate wife, by right there was none who could not be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi struggle right and wrong were not yet clear. Emperor Ming himself cut down rebellion and disorder; his business was only to rescue the drowning. The state road was obstructed and bent—it was fitting to establish an elder sovereign. Among Emperor Wen's sons born to the legitimate wife, by right there was none who could not be chosen.

sentences.zh: 子勛體自世祖，家運已絕，當璧之命，屬有所歸。

translations.literal: Zixun's body issued from Emperor Xiaowu, but the family fortune was already exhausted; the mandate to receive the jade tally was destined for another.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun's body issued from Emperor Xiaowu, but the family fortune was already exhausted. The mandate to receive the jade tally was destined for another.

sentences.zh: 曲直二途，未知攸適。

translations.literal: The paths of right and wrong—no one knew where they would lead.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of right and wrong—no one knew where they would lead.

sentences.zh: 徒以據有神甸，擅資天府，宗稷之重，威臨四方，以中制外，故能式清區宇。

translations.literal: Yet simply because one holds the sacred precinct, monopolizes the storehouse of heaven's bounty, and with the weight of the altars of state, one's majesty overawes the four quarters—governing the outer from the center—one can thus cleanse the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet simply because one holds the sacred precinct, monopolizes the storehouse of heaven's bounty, and with the weight of the altars of state overawes the four quarters—governing the outer from the center—one can thus cleanse the realm.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王所居，目以眾大之號，名曰京師，其義趣遠有以也。

translations.literal: The dwelling place of emperors and kings is called by the grandest title—the Capital—and the reason runs deeper than one might think.
translations.idiomatic: The dwelling place of emperors and kings is called by the grandest title—the Capital—and the reason runs deeper than one might think.
